teile.einleitung: Uri is a mountain canton in Central Switzerland and one of the three original cantons. The famous Gotthard lies here and, according to legend, the home of William Tell.
wichtigste: Together with Schwyz and Unterwalden, Uri is one of the original cantons of Switzerland.
The coat of arms of Uri shows a black bull's head.
The capital is Altdorf.
The Gotthard Pass lies in the canton of Uri.
The Gotthard Base Tunnel begins in the north at Erstfeld in the canton of Uri.
Andermatt is a well-known winter sports resort.
According to legend, William Tell comes from Bürglen.

abschnitte.text: The coat of arms of Uri shows a **black bull's head** on a yellow background. It is called the **Uristier** (Uri bull). It has a red nose ring and a red tongue. The coat of arms is very old and is among the best known in Switzerland. The canton's number plate code is **UR**.

Uri is a mountain canton through which the **Reuss** flows. The most important pass is the **Gotthard Pass**. It links northern Switzerland with Ticino. Already in the Middle Ages, merchants crossed the Gotthard. For this the famous **Devil's Bridge** was built in the wild **Schöllenen Gorge**. Today cars drive through the Gotthard Road Tunnel and trains through the railway tunnels.

At around 57 kilometres, the **Gotthard Base Tunnel** is the longest railway tunnel in the world. It begins in the north at **Erstfeld** in the canton of Uri and ends in Ticino. It opened in **2016**. Because it lies deep down in the mountain, the trains hardly have to climb and get through the Alps faster.

**Andermatt** lies high up in the Urseren Valley. It is a well-known **winter sports resort** with ski runs and plenty of snow. From here roads lead to several passes, for example the Gotthard, the Furka and the Oberalp. In summer many people come for walking.

Together with **Schwyz** and **Unterwalden**, Uri formed the **original cantons**. According to tradition, they concluded an alliance in 1291 from which Switzerland later arose. The Rütli meadow on Lake Uri lies on Uri soil. According to legend, the hero **William Tell** comes from **Bürglen**. In Altdorf stands a large Tell monument.

gewusst: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
The Rütli meadow, where according to legend the alliance was sworn, belongs to the canton of Uri.

teile.einleitung: Ticino is the southernmost canton in Switzerland and lies on the south side of the Alps. Italian is spoken here, the climate is mild, and there are palm trees, lakes and old stone villages.
wichtigste: The capital of the canton of Ticino is Bellinzona.
Ticino lies on the south side of the Alps and borders Italy in the west, south and east.
Ticino has been a canton of Switzerland in its own right since 1803.
The car number plate code TI stands for Ticino, the Italian name.
The flag of Ticino is red on the left and blue on the right.
The Monte Ceneri divides the canton into the Sopraceneri in the north and the Sottoceneri in the south.
Chiasso in the far south is the southernmost town in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: Ticino lies **south of the Alps**. That is why it is often warmer and sunnier there than in the north of Switzerland. In the west, south and east the canton borders **Italy**, and in the north the cantons of Valais, Uri and the Grisons. In the north there are high mountains and narrow valleys, and in the south lie large lakes such as **Lake Maggiore** and **Lake Lugano**. The Gotthard connects Ticino with the rest of Switzerland.

The **Monte Ceneri** pass divides the canton into two parts. “Sopra” means “above” in Italian, so the northern part is called the **Sopraceneri**. Bellinzona, Locarno and many mountain valleys lie there. The southern part is called the **Sottoceneri**, and “sotto” means “below”. Here lie Lugano, the largest city in the canton, and in the far south **Chiasso**, the southernmost town in Switzerland, with an important border crossing.

The capital **Bellinzona** is known for its three medieval castles. They are a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. For a long time the area of present-day Ticino was ruled by other members of the Confederation as a **subject territory**. Only in **1803** did Ticino become an independent canton with equal rights. Today it has its own government and its own parliament.

A typical Ticino dish is **polenta**, a porridge made of maize semolina. It is often eaten with meat, mushrooms or cheese. Chestnuts are also popular, and used to be an important food. A **grotto** is a simple inn, often in the woods or against a rock face. In the past grotti were cool cellars in which wine and cheese were stored. Today you sit there at stone tables in the shade.

In Ticino, **Italian** is the official language. Together with the Italian-speaking valleys in the Grisons it forms **Italian-speaking Switzerland**. Many place names, street signs and newspapers are therefore in Italian. The flag is **red and blue**, and the number plate code is **TI** for Ticino.

gewusst: Ticino is the only canton in which only Italian is an official language.
The three castles of Bellinzona are called Castelgrande, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro.

teile.einleitung: The Beznau nuclear power plant in the canton of Aargau is the oldest nuclear power plant in Switzerland. It has two units and has supplied electricity since the end of the 1960s.
wichtigste: The Beznau nuclear power plant stands on an artificial island in the Aare.
It lies in the municipality of Döttingen in the canton of Aargau.
Unit 1 has produced electricity since 1969.
The plant is cooled directly with river water.
Under a decision of 2024, Axpo plans to shut down the two units in 2032 and 2033.

abschnitte.text: The **Beznau nuclear power plant** stands on an **artificial island in the Aare**, in the municipality of Döttingen in the canton of **Aargau**. The island lies between the river and a canal that was built for a hydroelectric power station. The plant is run by the energy company **Axpo**. It has two units with **pressurised water reactors**. A reactor produces heat, which makes steam, and the steam drives turbines.

Beznau has no large cooling tower. It is cooled **directly with river water**. This is called **once-through cooling**: water from the Aare flows through the plant, absorbs heat and is returned to the river slightly warmer. When the Aare is very warm in summer, the plant therefore sometimes has to produce less electricity, to protect the river and its fish.

**Unit 1** has produced electricity since **1969**, and Unit 2 followed shortly after. This makes Beznau one of the oldest nuclear power plants in the world that are still in operation. In **2024** Axpo decided to shut down the two units for good in **2032 and 2033**. After that the plant will be dismantled over many years.

gewusst: Beznau supplies not only electricity but also heat for a district heating network in the region.
Beznau was the first commercial nuclear power plant in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Jura is the youngest canton in Switzerland. It lies in the north-west on the border with France, and mainly French is spoken there. The capital is Delémont (in German Delsberg).
wichtigste: The canton of Jura came into being on 1 January 1979.
Before that the area belonged to the canton of Bern.
Until the end of the 18th century it belonged to the Prince-Bishopric of Basel.
The flag shows a red bishop's crozier.
The cantonal parliament has 60 members and meets in Delémont.
The Franches-Montagnes are a high plateau with pastures and horses.
When the A16 was built, thousands of dinosaur footprints were found.

abschnitte.text: For centuries the **prince-bishops of Basel** ruled the area, last from **Porrentruy**. Their land is called the **Prince-Bishopric of Basel**. In 1792 and 1797 it was occupied by France. After 1815 a large part of it went to the canton of **Bern**. Many people in the Jura spoke French and were Catholic, while in the rest of the canton of Bern people mostly spoke German.

For a long time many people in the Jura wanted a **canton of their own**. After several votes, the **canton of Jura** came into being on **1 January 1979**. It is thus the youngest canton in Switzerland. Its parliament is simply called the “Parlement” and has **60 members**. It meets in the capital **Delémont**. Almost everywhere people speak **French**, with German only in the village of **Ederswiler**.

In the south lies the high plateau of the **Franches-Montagnes**, in German **Freiberge**. Many **horses** graze freely on the meadows there. In the north the **Ajoie** juts into France like a nose, with its main town **Porrentruy**. On the river **Doubs** lies the little town of **Saint-Ursanne** with an old stone bridge. It is very well preserved.

The canton's **flag** shows a red **bishop's crozier** and red and white stripes. The crozier recalls the bishops of Basel. When the **A16** motorway was built near Porrentruy, **thousands of dinosaur footprints** came to light. They date from the Jurassic. Today you can see finds in the **Jurassica** museum.

gewusst: In the Ajoie, thousands of dinosaur tracks were found during road building.
The Franches-Montagnes horses take their name from the high plateau of the Franches-Montagnes.

teile.einleitung: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is a long railway tunnel under the Bernese Alps. Since 2007 it has connected Frutigen in the canton of Bern with Raron in the Valais, and when it opened it was the longest land tunnel in the world.
wichtigste: The tunnel runs from Frutigen to Raron in the Rhône Valley.
It is about 35 kilometres long and was opened in 2007.
A large part of the tunnel is only single track.
Speeds of up to 250 km/h are permitted.
It cost about 5 billion francs.
It was built by BLS AlpTransit AG and is operated by BLS.
The Tropenhaus Frutigen uses warm mountain water from the tunnel.

abschnitte.text: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel passes under the **Bernese Alps** between the **Kander Valley** and the **Rhône Valley**. The north portal is at **Frutigen**, the south portal at **Raron** in the Valais. A “base tunnel” lies deep down, at the foot of the mountains. This way the trains hardly have to climb. The tunnel is part of **NEAT**, the New Rail Link through the Alps, which is meant to move more goods from the road onto the railway.

The tunnel has two tubes. To save money, however, not all parts were fully fitted out. Only about **40 per cent** of the route can be used as **double track**, and the rest is **single track**. In a section of the second tube about **14 kilometres** long, the **track and railway technology** are missing. That is why fewer trains can run than would actually be possible.

When it opened in **2007**, the Lötschberg Base Tunnel was the **longest land tunnel in the world**, that is, the longest tunnel lying entirely under land. Later the **Gotthard Base Tunnel** took over this record. Speeds of up to **250 km/h** are permitted in the tunnel. In the end the cost was about **5.3 billion francs**.

The tunnel was built by **BLS AlpTransit AG** on behalf of the Confederation. For the Gotthard and the Ceneri, another company was responsible, AlpTransit Gotthard AG. The tunnel is operated by **BLS**. Its name comes from the Bern-Lötschberg-Simplon Railway. After the SBB, it is the second largest standard gauge railway in Switzerland.

Deep inside the mountain the rock is warm. That is why **warm mountain water** flows out of the tunnel. In **Frutigen** it is used in the **Tropenhaus** (tropical house). There tropical fruits grow, and **sturgeons**, large fish, are farmed. In this way the tunnel's waste water becomes something useful.

gewusst: Thanks to the base tunnel, you get from Bern to Visp much faster than you used to over the old mountain line.
The old Lötschberg tunnel of 1913 lies much higher and is still used today, for example for the car shuttle train.

teile.einleitung: In February 1999 an extreme amount of snow fell in the Alps in a short time. Very many avalanches came down, and the winter of 1998/99 went down in history as an avalanche winter.
wichtigste: In the avalanche winter of 1998/99, 36 people died in avalanches in Switzerland.
17 of them died in buildings and on roads and railways.
The Valais village of Evolène had the most avalanche deaths in Switzerland.
Several north west stau situations brought the huge amounts of snow.
In Elm in the canton of Glarus, around 447 cm of new snow fell in one snowfall period.
Around 1,200 damaging avalanches were counted.
Property damage in Switzerland came to over 600 million francs.

abschnitte.text: In February 1999, **several north west stau situations** brought a great deal of snow to the Alps. In a **stau situation**, moist air is pushed against the mountains. It rises, cools down and drops its snow. There were three big snowfall periods shortly after one another. During the third, around **447 cm** of new snow was measured in **Elm** in the canton of Glarus. Many valleys were cut off from the outside world for days.

In the avalanche winter of 1998/99, **36 people** died in avalanches in Switzerland. **17** of them died in **buildings** and on **roads and railways**. The Valais village of **Evolène** suffered the most avalanche deaths in Switzerland. In total, around **1,200 damaging avalanches** were counted. The direct and indirect **property damage** came to **over 600 million francs**.

Large avalanches also came down in the neighbouring countries. The village of **Galtür** in Tyrol, Austria, was hit particularly hard. In February 1999, **31 people** died there in an avalanche. Many guests and locals then had to be brought out of the cut off valleys by helicopter.

The avalanche winter showed that the many **avalanche barriers** built since 1951 had prevented much worse. Even so, lessons were learned. The **SLF** in Davos developed the information system **IFKIS** for municipalities and avalanche services. This allows the experts on the spot to exchange measurement data and warnings more quickly. In addition, hazard maps were revised and new protective structures were built.

gewusst: The avalanche winter of 1999 claimed clearly fewer victims in Switzerland than the avalanche winter of 1951, also thanks to the many protective structures.
After 1999, Switzerland expanded its network of automatic measuring stations in the mountains further.

teile.einleitung: The Jura is a mountain range in the north-west of Switzerland. It stretches in a long arc from the area around Geneva to the area around Schaffhausen and is much lower than the Alps.
wichtigste: The Jura lies in the north-west of Switzerland on the border with France.
The mountains consist mainly of limestone.
The highest Jura peak in Switzerland is the Mont Tendre at 1,679 metres.
The Chasseral above Lake Biel has a tall transmitter tower.
The Creux du Van is a huge rock cirque in the canton of Neuchâtel.
Watches have been made in the Jura for centuries.
The Jurassic, an age of the dinosaurs, is named after the Jura.

abschnitte.text: The **Jura** is one of the three great landscapes of Switzerland, alongside the Central Plateau and the Alps. It stretches in an arc from the **Geneva** area to the area around **Schaffhausen**. A large part of the mountains lies in **France**. The Jura has long, parallel mountain chains with valleys between them. Do not confuse it with the **canton of Jura**, which covers only part of the mountains.

The Jura consists mainly of **limestone**. This rock was formed long ago on the bed of a sea. That is why **fossils** are often found in it, for example shells and ammonites. Water can slowly dissolve limestone, which is how **caves** and gorges are formed. The rocks gave their name to a whole geological age: the **Jurassic**, in which many dinosaurs lived.

The Jura mountains are much lower than the Alps. The highest peak on Swiss soil is the **Mont Tendre** in the canton of Vaud at 1,679 metres. It lies above the Vallée de Joux. Above Lake Biel stands the **Chasseral**, 1,606 metres high, with a **transmitter tower** 120 metres tall. In the canton of Neuchâtel lies the **Creux du Van**, a huge rock cirque with high, rounded rock walls.

The Jura is famous for the **watch industry**. From the 18th century, watchmaking developed in places such as **La Chaux-de-Fonds**, **Le Locle** and the **Vallée de Joux**. In the past, many farming families made watch parts at home during the long winter. Large firms later grew out of this. To this day, watchmaking is an important employer in the **Jura Arc**.

gewusst: A whole age of Earth's history, the Jurassic, is named after these mountains.
The limestone of the Jura was once sea floor, which is why fossilised sea creatures are found on the mountains.

teile.einleitung: A moraine is the debris that a glacier carries along and deposits. In Switzerland you find moraines everywhere, because during the Ice Age glaciers covered large parts of the country. Many hills and lakes were formed in this way.
wichtigste: Glacier debris is called moraine.
Moraines consist of a mixture of boulders, gravel, sand and clay.
The end moraine lies in front of the glacier tongue and shows the greatest advance.
Lateral moraines form ridges at the edge, and the ground moraine lies under the ice.
End moraines often dam lakes, for example Lake Zurich.
Drumlins and kettle holes are further traces of the Ice Age.

abschnitte.text: A **glacier** is a slowly flowing stream of ice. On its way it tears rock loose from the ground beneath, and stones fall onto the ice from the valley sides. It carries this debris along and at some point deposits it. The deposit is called **moraine**. It consists of a **mixture** of large boulders, gravel, sand and fine clay. Unlike with a river, the material is not sorted by size.

Depending on position, several types are distinguished. The **end moraine** lies as a ridge in front of the **glacier tongue**. It shows how far the glacier once reached. **Lateral moraines** form at the **edges** of the glacier as long ridges. The **ground moraine** lies **under** the ice. There the rock is ground up and deposited over a wide area, and it is often clayey and impermeable to water. When two glaciers flow together, their lateral moraines form a **medial moraine**.

When a glacier melts away, the end moraine is left as a **ridge across the valley**. It acts like a **dam**. Water collects behind it, and a **lake** forms. This is also the case with **Lake Zurich**: among other things, it is dammed by moraines of the Linth Glacier. The **Lindenhof** in the old town of Zurich is part of this end moraine.

**Drumlins** are elongated hills of moraine material that were shaped **under the ice**. Their long axis shows the direction in which the glacier flowed. There are many drumlins, for example, in the **Zurich Oberland**. A **kettle hole** forms when a block of ice left behind in the debris slowly melts. The ground sinks, and a hollow forms, often with a small lake or moor.

gewusst: Huge boulders that glaciers have deposited far from where they came from are called erratic boulders.
At today's glaciers you often see high lateral moraines, which show how thick the ice still was around 1850.

teile.einleitung: The Leibstadt nuclear power plant in the canton of Aargau is the most powerful nuclear power plant in Switzerland. It lies directly on the Rhine at the border with Germany.
wichtigste: Leibstadt is the most powerful nuclear power plant in Switzerland.
It lies on the Rhine in the canton of Aargau.
On the other side of the Rhine lies Germany.
A boiling water reactor operates in the plant.
Leibstadt is the youngest nuclear power plant in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The **Leibstadt nuclear power plant** stands in the municipality of Leibstadt in the canton of **Aargau**. It lies directly on the **Rhine**, which here forms the border with **Germany**. The plant went into operation in the 1980s and is thus the **youngest nuclear power plant** in Switzerland. It is also the **most powerful** in the country and supplies a large share of Swiss electricity.

A **boiling water reactor** operates in Leibstadt. Unlike in a pressurised water reactor, the water here boils directly in the reactor. The **steam** that is produced is sent straight to the **turbine** and drives a generator, which produces electricity. After that the steam is cooled back into water and flows back into the reactor.

For cooling, Leibstadt has a very tall **cooling tower**. The cloud above it is **water vapour**. With the cooling tower, the plant has to release only a little warm water into the Rhine. Besides Gösgen, Leibstadt is the second Swiss nuclear power plant with such a large cooling tower.

gewusst: The cooling tower of Leibstadt is among the tallest structures in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Glarus Thrust is a place where you can see especially clearly how the Alps were formed. There, old rocks lie on top of much younger ones, along a sharp line in the rock.
wichtigste: At the Glarus Thrust, older rocks lie on top of much younger ones.
On top lies reddish Verrucano from the Permian, below it Flysch from the early Tertiary.
The upper mass of rock was pushed about 40 kilometres northwards.
Since 2008 the area has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona.
Near Sool you can see the thrust surface up close at the Lochsite.
Twice a year the sun shines through the Martinsloch onto the church in Elm.

abschnitte.text: Normally younger layers of rock lie on top and older ones below. At the **Glarus Thrust** it is the other way round. On top lies the reddish **Verrucano**, a coarse rubble rock from the **Permian**, around 260 to 300 million years old. Below it lies **Flysch** from the **early Tertiary**, only about 35 to 50 million years old.

When the Alps were formed, the upper mass of rock was pushed about **40 kilometres** northwards over the younger layers. This is called a **thrust**. The boundary between the rocks is a sharp line that can be seen from far away in the mountain walls. At the **Lochsite** near **Sool** in the Sernf Valley you can even touch it.

The Zurich geologist **Albert Heim** first explained the layout with a **“double fold”**, that is, two folds lying against each other. The Frenchman **Marcel Bertrand** recognised a single great thrust as early as **1884**, without ever having been there. Heim only accepted this interpretation in **1902**. This gave rise to the **nappe theory**, which explains the structure of the Alps.

Since **2008** the area has belonged to the **UNESCO World Heritage** as the **Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona**. It lies in the cantons of Glarus, St Gallen and the Grisons. In the **Tschingelhörner** there is a natural hole in the rock, the **Martinsloch**. Twice a year the sun shines through it exactly onto the church of **Elm**.

gewusst: The thrust line is so clear that in good light you can see it from far away as a pale band in the rock walls.
The name Verrucano comes from a mountain in Tuscany in Italy, where a similar rock is found.

teile.einleitung: The Great St Bernard is an Alpine pass between the Valais and the Aosta Valley in Italy. The Romans already used it, and for almost a thousand years there has been a hospice at the top of the pass.
wichtigste: The pass links the Valais with the Aosta Valley in Italy.
The road leads from Martigny via Orsières through the Val d'Entremont.
The Romans called the pass Mons Iovis, “Mountain of Jupiter”.
Bernard of Aosta founded the hospice in the 11th century.
The hospice is run by Augustinian canons.
Napoleon crossed the pass with his army in 1800.
The road tunnel is 5.85 kilometres long and has been open since 1964.

abschnitte.text: The pass road begins in **Martigny** in the Rhône Valley. It climbs via **Orsières** through the **Val d'Entremont** up to the top of the pass at around 2,469 metres. On the other side it goes down into the **Aosta Valley** in Italy. Next to the hospice lies a small mountain lake, and the border runs very close by.

Over 2,000 years ago the pass was already an important route across the Alps. The **Romans** called it **Mons Iovis**, that is, “Mountain of Jupiter”. Jupiter was the most important god of the Romans. A **temple** to him stood at the top of the pass. Remains of it and old coins have been found there.

In the **11th century**, **Bernard of Aosta** founded a **hospice** for travellers on the pass. The pass is named after him. In **1923**, Pope **Pius XI** confirmed him as the patron saint of the Alps. The hospice is run by the canons of the **Congregation of the Great St Bernard**. They live by the rule of Saint Augustine and are therefore called **Augustinian canons**.

In May **1800**, **Napoleon Bonaparte** crossed the pass with his army to march into Italy. The painter **Jacques-Louis David** afterwards painted a famous picture in several versions. It shows Napoleon heroically on a rearing horse. In reality he crossed the pass on a sure-footed **mule**.

In winter the pass road is closed because of snow. Since **1964** there has been the **Great St Bernard Tunnel**. It is **5.85 kilometres** long and links the Valais with Italy. It can be used all year round. It was one of the first long road tunnels through the Alps.

gewusst: The famous St Bernard dogs are named after the hospice on the Great St Bernard.
The hospice is so high up that there is snow there on many days of the year.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland is a small country, but it sells a great many goods and services abroad. This export economy is especially important for jobs and prosperity in the country.
wichtigste: Switzerland mainly exports pharmaceutical products, chemicals, machinery, watches and precision instruments.
The European Union is overall Switzerland’s most important trading partner.
As a single country, the USA was the biggest buyer of Swiss exports in 2024.
Switzerland has been a founding member of EFTA since 1960.
Since 2014 a free trade agreement has applied between Switzerland and China.
A strong franc makes Swiss products more expensive abroad.

abschnitte.text: The largest part of the exports is made up of **pharmaceutical products** and chemicals, such as medicines from Basel. In addition come machinery, watches and fine measuring instruments. **Gold** also plays a big role: a lot of gold is processed and traded in Switzerland. Because gold is very valuable, the export figures therefore fluctuate strongly from year to year.

The **European Union** is overall the most important trading partner, because Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe. With the EU, **bilateral agreements** regulate trade. If you look at single countries, in 2024 the **USA** came first, ahead of Germany. Countries such as China, Italy and France are important too.

In 1960 Switzerland was a founding member of **EFTA**, the European Free Trade Association. Through EFTA and also on its own it has concluded many **free trade agreements**. Such agreements lower or abolish customs duties. Since 1 July 2014 an agreement with **China** has applied, which made Switzerland one of the first countries in Europe to have one.

On 6 December 1992 the people and the cantons narrowly rejected joining the **European Economic Area (EEA)**. After that Switzerland negotiated individual agreements with the EU, the so-called **bilateral path**. This path is still debated in politics today. It strongly shapes Switzerland’s foreign economic policy.

If the franc becomes stronger, customers abroad have to pay more for Swiss goods. This is called an **appreciation**. That is why in 2011 the **Swiss National Bank (SNB)** introduced a minimum rate of 1.20 francs per euro. In January 2015 it unexpectedly abolished it, and the franc suddenly became stronger. Many export firms had to save money or cut their prices.

gewusst: The organisation **Switzerland Global Enterprise** helps small and medium-sized firms take the step abroad, on behalf of the Confederation.
Because of the gold trade, Swiss export figures can be especially high in some years, although no gold is mined in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Grimsel Pass is an Alpine pass between the canton of Bern and the canton of Valais. It is known for its large reservoirs, which generate electricity, and for the source of the Aare.
wichtigste: The Grimsel Pass links the Bernese Oberland with Upper Valais.
The top of the pass is at around 2,164 metres above sea level.
On the Bernese side the road runs through the Haslital.
On the Valais side lies the small village of Gletsch.
Around the Grimsel there are several reservoirs that supply electricity.
The Aare rises at the Aare glaciers on the Grimsel.
The watershed between the Rhine and the Rhône runs over the top of the pass.

abschnitte.text: The Grimsel road begins at **Innertkirchen** in the Bernese Oberland. It climbs through the **Haslital**, where **Meiringen** also lies. The top of the pass is at around **2,164 metres**. On the Valais side it goes down to **Gletsch**. From there you can continue over the Furka Pass or into the Goms. In winter the pass road is closed because of snow.

On the Grimsel, several valleys were closed off with high **dams**. This created large artificial lakes. The largest is the **Lake Grimsel** near the top of the pass on the Bernese side. Right on the top of the pass, by contrast, lies a small natural lake, the **Totensee**. It lies right beside the road.

The water from the reservoirs flows through tunnels and pipes to **power stations**. There it drives **turbines** that generate electricity. The power stations on the Grimsel are among the important hydropower plants in Switzerland. A special attraction is the **Gelmerbahn**, a very steep funicular railway up to Lake Gelmer.

The **Aare** rises at the **Aare glaciers** near the Grimsel. It flows down through the Haslital into **Lake Brienz**. Later it flows through Bern and finally joins the Rhine. The Aare is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland.

A **watershed** runs over the top of the Grimsel Pass. This is a line where it is decided which way rainwater flows. To the north it flows via the Aare to the **Rhine** and into the **North Sea**. To the south it flows via the **Rhône** into the **Mediterranean**. So a raindrop on the top of the pass can end up in two quite different seas.

gewusst: The Rhône rises very close by, at the Rhône Glacier above Gletsch.
The Gelmerbahn is one of the steepest funicular railways in Europe.

teile.einleitung: Half-cantons are cantons that have only one seat in the Council of States and count only half a vote in the cantons' majority. There are six of them in Switzerland. Otherwise they are completely normal cantons with their own government.
wichtigste: There are six half-cantons in Switzerland.
They are Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
A half-canton has one seat in the Council of States, a full canton two.
In the cantons' majority, a half-canton counts as half a cantonal vote.
In total there are 23 cantonal votes.
The canton of Basel was divided in 1833.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland has **26 cantons**. Six of them are called **half-cantons**. In the Federal Constitution of 1999 they are officially called “cantons with half a cantonal vote”. Half-cantons have their own **government**, their own **parliament** and their own laws. They differ from the other cantons in only two things: in the Council of States and in the cantons' majority.

The **Council of States** is the chamber of parliament in which the cantons are represented. Each full canton sends **two** people there. A half-canton sends only **one** person. That is why the Council of States has 46 members: 20 cantons times 2 makes 40, plus 6 from the half-cantons.

To change the Federal Constitution, you need the **popular majority** and the **cantons' majority**. In the cantons' majority, each full canton counts with one vote. A half-canton counts only with **half a cantonal vote**. The 20 full cantons have 20 votes, and the six half-cantons together make 3. So in total there are **23 cantonal votes**.

**Obwalden** and **Nidwalden** used to form Unterwalden together, but had already been largely separate since the Middle Ages. **Appenzell** split in **1597** into the Catholic Innerrhoden and the Reformed Ausserrhoden. The canton of **Basel** was divided in **1833**. Before that there had been disputes and fighting between the city and the countryside.

Some half-cantons used to have the **Landsgemeinde**. In it, the voters gather in the open air and vote by show of hands. **Nidwalden** abolished it in 1996, **Ausserrhoden** in 1997 and **Obwalden** in 1998. **Appenzell Innerrhoden** still holds it every year today. Otherwise it only exists in the canton of Glarus.

gewusst: Appenzell Innerrhoden is the canton with the fewest inhabitants in Switzerland.
The two Appenzells are completely surrounded by the canton of St Gallen.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland consists of 26 cantons. Each canton is like a small state within the state, with its own constitution, its own parliament and its own government.
wichtigste: Switzerland has 26 cantons.
In politics the cantons are also called “Stände” (states).
The Council of States has 46 seats in total.
In most cantons the cantonal government is called the Executive Council.
Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden concluded the Federal Charter in 1291.
Each canton has an abbreviation of two letters, for example TG for Thurgau.
In 17 cantons, German is the only official language.

abschnitte.text: Each **canton** has its own **constitution**, its own **parliament** and its own **government**. In most German-speaking cantons the government is called the **Executive Council** (Regierungsrat) and usually has five or seven members. The cantons decide many things themselves, for example about schools, police and hospitals. This division of power between the federal government, the cantons and the municipalities is called **federalism**.

The history of the cantons begins with the **Federal Charter of 1291**. It was concluded by **Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden**. Only afterwards did further places join one by one, for example Lucerne, Zurich and Bern. Many cantons were only founded later, such as Aargau in 1803. The youngest canton is the **canton of Jura**, which has existed since 1979.

abschnitte.titel: The states in the Federal Palace
abschnitte.text: In politics the cantons are also called **Stände** (states). That is why the chamber in the Federal Palace in which they are represented is called the **Council of States** (Ständerat). Each canton has two seats there. Six cantons have only **half a cantonal vote** and therefore only one seat, for example Obwalden, Nidwalden and the two Basels. Together there are **46 seats**.

The cantons are very different. The Grisons is the largest by area, Basel-Stadt the smallest. The canton of **Bern** has the most municipalities, over 300 (as of 2025). In **17 cantons**, German is the only official language. Bern, Fribourg and Valais are bilingual, and the Grisons is trilingual. Each canton has an **abbreviation** that you can see on number plates, for example **TG** for Thurgau.

gewusst: In the canton of Glarus and in Appenzell Innerrhoden, people still vote in the open air at the Landsgemeinde today.
Each canton has its own coat of arms and its own anthem or a song that belongs to it.

teile.einleitung: Agriculture supplies Switzerland with food such as milk, grain, vegetables and fruit. Depending on the region it looks very different: fields on the Central Plateau, meadows and Alpine pastures in the mountains.
wichtigste: Agriculture belongs to the primary sector.
Most of the arable land lies on the Central Plateau.
For bread, mainly wheat is grown.
Sugar is obtained from sugar beet, and rapeseed oil from rape.
The Grosses Moos in the Seeland is regarded as the “vegetable garden of Switzerland”.
The Jura Water Correction made the marshy Seeland fertile.
The Confederation pays farms direct payments, for example for animal welfare and nature conservation.

abschnitte.text: The economy is divided into three sectors. **Agriculture** belongs to the **primary sector**, because it obtains raw materials directly from nature. Forestry and fishing also count here. Today only a few people in Switzerland work in agriculture. Even so, it is important for food and for looking after the landscape.

Most of the **arable land** lies on the **Central Plateau**, because it is flat and fertile there. For bread, mainly **wheat** is grown. **Sugar** is obtained from the **sugar beet**, and **rapeseed oil** from the yellow flowering fields of **rape**. Potatoes, maize and barley also grow. In the **mountains** there are mainly meadows and pastures for cows, which supply the milk for cheese.

The **Grosses Moos** in the Bernese and Fribourg **Seeland** is called the **“vegetable garden of Switzerland”**. Lettuce, carrots, onions and many other vegetables grow here. In the past the area was a **marsh** that was often flooded. That only changed with the **Jura Water Correction** in the 19th and 20th centuries. Rivers were diverted, the lakes were lowered and the land was drained.

The Confederation supports farms with **direct payments**. These are contributions for services that benefit everyone. Payment is made, for example, for **animal welfare**, for **nature conservation** and for looking after the landscape in the mountains. Anyone who receives money must follow certain rules, for example on protecting soil and water.

gewusst: Because the peat soil in the Grosses Moos has been shrinking since it was drained, the land now lies lower in some places than it used to.
Sugar beet from Switzerland is processed into sugar in Aarberg and Frauenfeld.

teile.einleitung: The **Emmental** is a hilly landscape in the canton of Bern. It is known for large farmhouses, covered wooden bridges, cheese and Swiss wrestling. The name comes from the river Emme, which flows through the valley.
wichtigste: The Emmental is a landscape with many green hills in the canton of Bern.
Typical are scattered single farms with large, deep roofs.
Next to the farmhouse there is often a Stöckli for the older generation.
Covered wooden bridges lead over the Emme.
On its edge lies the Napf, in whose streams you can find tiny grains of gold.
Gotthelf’s story “The Black Spider” is set in the Emmental.

abschnitte.text: The Emmental is a landscape with **many green hills**, meadows and woods. The farms often lie singly on the slopes and on the hill ridges, which are called **Eggen**. These **scattered single farms** are typical, and there are fewer large closed villages. On the edge of the Emmental lies the **Napf**, a viewpoint mountain about 1,400 metres high on the border of the cantons of Bern and Lucerne.

The old **Emmental farmhouses** have huge roofs that reach almost to the ground. Under the roof there is room for the living quarters, the stable and the hay. Next to the big house there is often a smaller house, the **Stöckli**. When the young people take over the farm, the parents move into the Stöckli. In this way the generations stay close together.

In the Emmental a lot of milk is made into **cheese**. The cheesemakers warm the milk in large **copper vats** until it thickens. From it they shape large wheels of cheese. The best-known cheese is **Emmental** with its large holes. It carries the name of the valley out into the whole world.

Several old **covered wooden bridges** with a roof lead over the Emme. Very popular in the Emmental is Swiss wrestling, called **Schwingen**. In it two men or women wrestle in **linen shorts** on sawdust. In the streams on the Napf lie tiny **flakes of gold**. With luck and patience you can wash them out with a pan.

The pastor and writer **Jeremias Gotthelf** lived in **Lützelflüh** in the Emmental. Many of his stories tell of life on the farms. His eerie story **“Die schwarze Spinne”** (“The Black Spider”) appeared in 1842. It is set in the area of **Sumiswald** in the Emmental and is still read in schools today.

gewusst: With luck you can find real gold in the streams on the Napf, but only tiny grains.
The roofs of Emmental farmhouses sometimes reach almost to the ground.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background. It is one of the best-known symbols of Switzerland and has a special, square shape.
wichtigste: The Swiss flag is red and white.
It shows a white cross in the middle.
The flag is square, as otherwise only the flag of Vatican City is.
The sign of the Red Cross looks like the Swiss flag with the colours swapped.
On 1 August lanterns and bonfires light up everywhere.
Many Swiss products carry the Swiss cross.

abschnitte.text: The flag of Switzerland has a **red** background and a **white cross** in the middle. The four arms of the cross are equally long. The cross does not touch the edge. A similar sign was carried earlier by the canton of Schwyz, after which Switzerland is named.

Most flags in the world are rectangular. The Swiss flag, by contrast, is **square**. Only one other state also has a square flag: **Vatican City** in Rome. On ships, however, Switzerland uses a rectangular flag.

The **Red Cross** was founded in **Geneva** in 1863, among others by **Henry Dunant**. It helps injured and needy people. As its sign people chose the Swiss flag with **swapped colours**: a red cross on a white background. In this way they honoured Switzerland as the country of its founding.

On **1 August**, the national holiday, flags hang everywhere. In the evening **lanterns** and **bonfires** glow. Many Swiss products, such as pocket knives, watches or chocolate, show the **Swiss cross**. In this way you can tell that they come from Switzerland. There are clear rules for this indication of origin.

gewusst: Every municipality and every canton of Switzerland also has a coat of arms of its own.
Since 1889 the law has laid down what the Swiss coat of arms looks like.

teile.einleitung: The Little Ice Age was a long, rather cool period from about the 14th to the 19th century. In the Alps, the glaciers grew strongly during this time.
wichtigste: During the Little Ice Age, the Alpine glaciers advanced in three major phases.
The Gorner Glacier had already reached roughly its later greatest extent around 1385.
The Maunder Minimum, a phase of low solar activity, fell within the Little Ice Age.
The glacier level of around 1850 is regarded as the last high point before the warming.
The glaciers overran farms and pastures in mountain villages.
The tongue of the Great Aletsch Glacier has retreated by more than 3 km since 1870.

abschnitte.titel: What was the Little Ice Age?
abschnitte.text: The **Little Ice Age** lasted from roughly the 14th century to the middle of the 19th century. On average it was only a little cooler than before, but that was enough for the **glaciers** to grow. The Alpine glaciers advanced in **three major phases**: in the 14th century, in the 17th century and around 1850. The **Gorner Glacier** in the Valais had already reached roughly its later greatest extent around 1385.

There are several reasons for the cooling. The **Maunder Minimum** fell in this period, a phase in which the sun was less active and showed hardly any sunspots. In addition, large **volcanic eruptions** threw dust and gases high into the air, which weakened the sunlight. The particularly harsh winter of 1783/84 was preceded by the eruption of **Laki** in Iceland.

For people in the mountains, the Little Ice Age was hard. The growing glaciers **overran farms and pastures**. Cool, wet summers led to poor harvests. Many communities held **processions** and prayed for the ice to stop. At the high point around 1855, the **Lower Grindelwald Glacier** was the only Alpine glacier whose tongue reached below 1,000 metres.

The glacier levels of around 1850 can often still be recognised today by **moraine ridges**. These are ridges of debris that the ice pushed ahead of itself. Because they are still young, they are **hardly overgrown** and easy to see. The level of around 1850 is often used as a **reference point**, because it is the last high point before the warming. Since 1870 the tongue of the **Great Aletsch Glacier** has retreated by more than 3 km.

From about **1860**, many Alpine glaciers began to retreat, even though it was hardly any warmer yet. One **hypothesis** explains this with **soot from industry**. The dark soot settled on snow and ice. Dark surfaces absorb more heat from the sun, so the ice melted faster. Researchers are still investigating this explanation today.

gewusst: After a volcanic eruption in Indonesia, 1816 went down in history as the “year without a summer”, and there was hunger in Switzerland too.
On old paintings and engravings you can see how far the glaciers reached into the valley around 1850.

teile.einleitung: An erratic boulder is a large block of stone that does not match the rock of its surroundings. In the ice age glaciers often carried it many kilometres and left it lying.
wichtigste: Erratic boulders consist of rock that does not otherwise occur in the area.
Ice-age glaciers brought them from the Alps to the Central Plateau and as far as the Jura.
They are also called “erratic blocks”, from the Latin errare, to wander.
From about one cubic metre upwards we speak of an erratic boulder rather than of glacial debris.
The Pierres du Niton in Geneva are the starting point of Swiss height measurement.
Louis Agassiz made it known that erratic boulders come from glaciers.

abschnitte.titel: A stone in the wrong place
abschnitte.text: If a large **granite block** lies on the **Central Plateau**, that is strange, because there is no granite in the ground there. Such blocks are called **erratic boulders** or **erratic blocks**. This comes from the Latin word **errare**, to wander, because they seem to have travelled. From a volume of about one **cubic metre** upwards we speak of an erratic boulder.

In the ice ages huge glaciers reached from the Alps far into the lowlands. They carried stones along on and in the ice. When the ice melted, the blocks stayed lying. Granite blocks from the Valais on the slope of the **Jura** show that the **Rhône Glacier** once reached as far as the Jura. If you compare the rock with rocks in the Alps, you can work out where it came from.

In the past nobody could explain how the blocks came to their places. The naturalist **Louis Agassiz**, a professor in Neuchâtel, put forward the idea of a great **ice age** from 1837. Erratic boulders and glacial polish were important proof for him. Today this explanation is generally accepted.

In the harbour of **Geneva** two erratic boulders stick out of the lake, the **Pierres du Niton**. On the larger one lies a survey mark, the **Repère Pierre du Niton**. From it the heights of the whole of Switzerland were determined. According to the national survey it lies at **373.6 metres above sea level**.

In the past many erratic boulders were broken up and used as **building stone** for walls, steps and fountains. Later people began to protect them. The **Pierre des Marmettes** near Monthey in the Valais is a huge granite block from the Mont Blanc area. The Swiss Society for Natural Sciences bought it in 1906 in order to save it.

gewusst: On the Pierre des Marmettes there even stood a little house.
Some erratic boulders on the Central Plateau come from areas more than 100 kilometres away.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Statistical Office divides Switzerland into seven major regions. Each major region is made up of whole cantons. This makes it easy to compare areas of Switzerland with one another and with regions in Europe.
wichtigste: The FSO distinguishes seven major regions.
The major regions always consist of whole cantons.
They correspond to the European statistical level NUTS 2.
Zurich and Ticino each consist of only one canton.
Eastern Switzerland is the largest major region by area.
The Espace Mittelland has the most inhabitants (as of 2024).

abschnitte.text: Switzerland has 26 cantons. For some comparisons that is a lot of small pieces. So the **Federal Statistical Office (FSO)** groups the cantons into **seven major regions**. They are a **statistical level** above the cantons. The major regions have no government or parliament of their own.

The **Lake Geneva region** includes Vaud, Valais and Geneva. The **Espace Mittelland** includes Bern, Fribourg, Solothurn, Neuchâtel and Jura. **Northwestern Switzerland** consists of Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft and Aargau. Then there are the major regions of **Zurich** and **Ticino**. **Eastern Switzerland** includes Glarus, Schaffhausen, both Appenzells, St Gallen, the Grisons and Thurgau. **Central Switzerland** includes Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden, Nidwalden and Zug.

Two major regions consist of only one canton: **Zurich** and **Ticino**. All the others combine several cantons. **Eastern Switzerland** is the largest by area, mainly because of the large canton of the Grisons. The most people live in the **Espace Mittelland**, almost two million in 2024.

In Europe there is a common system for statistical regions. It is called **NUTS**. The Swiss major regions correspond to level **NUTS 2**. The cantons lie one level lower, at **NUTS 3**. This makes it possible, for example, to compare income or unemployment in Eastern Switzerland with a region in Germany or Italy.

The boundaries of the major regions always follow **cantonal borders**. A canton is never split. That is why the major regions do not exactly match natural landscapes such as the Central Plateau or the Alps. The canton of Bern, for example, shares in the Jura, the Central Plateau and the Alps, but belongs entirely to the Espace Mittelland.

gewusst: The major region of Eastern Switzerland includes seven cantons, more than any other.
The name “Espace Mittelland” is a mixture of French and German, because both languages are spoken there.

teile.einleitung: GLAMOS stands for “Glacier Monitoring Switzerland”, the Swiss glacier measurement network. Every year it measures how Switzerland's glaciers are changing.
wichtigste: GLAMOS is run jointly by ETH Zurich, the University of Fribourg and the University of Zurich.
The Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) is one of the funders.
Changes in the length of glaciers have been observed in Switzerland since 1880.
In 2024, the mass balance was measured directly in the field on around 20 glaciers.
One of the longest measurement series in the world has been running on the Clariden Firn since 1914/15.
A negative mass balance means that a glacier is shrinking.

abschnitte.text: **GLAMOS** is a joint programme of **ETH Zurich**, the **University of Fribourg** and the **University of Zurich**. It is supported, among others, by the **Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)**, MeteoSwiss and swisstopo. Switzerland has been observing its glaciers for a very long time: measurements of glacier lengths began in **1880**.

On almost **100 glaciers**, a measurement is taken every year of how far the **glacier snout** has moved. In 2023, 95 glaciers were surveyed, and almost all of them had retreated. This shows over many decades how the glaciers are changing.

The **mass balance** compares how much snow a glacier gains in winter with how much ice it loses in summer. If it is **negative**, the glacier loses more than it gains and shrinks. The calculation covers the **hydrological year** from 1 October to 30 September. In 2024 the mass balance was determined directly in the field on around **20 glaciers**.

Researchers drill **stakes** into the ice. When the ice melts, the stake sticks out further, and you can see how much has been lost. In snow pits they measure the amount of snow. With the **geodetic method**, they compare **elevation models** made from aerial photos or laser scans taken at two points in time. This shows how thickness and volume change.

On the **Clariden Firn** in the canton of Glarus, snow and ice have been measured at fixed points since **1914/15**. Together with the Silvretta Glacier, this series is one of the longest in the world. Such long series are valuable because they make it easy to see changes in the climate.

gewusst: Reports on the glaciers have appeared regularly in Switzerland since 1881.
The measurements in the field are extrapolated with models to all the glaciers in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Lavaux is a winegrowing area in the canton of Vaud with steep terraces above Lake Geneva. The landscape is so special that it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: Vines grow on the terraces of the Lavaux.
The Lavaux lies on Lake Geneva in the canton of Vaud.
It stretches roughly between Lausanne and Vevey.
Since 2007 the Lavaux has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The walls of the terraces are built of stone.
The most common grape variety is Chasselas.
The terraces were laid out many hundreds of years ago by monks.

abschnitte.text: The **Lavaux** lies in the canton of **Vaud** on the north shore of **Lake Geneva**. It stretches roughly between **Lausanne** and **Vevey**. On the steep slopes **vines** grow, row after row on narrow **terraces**. In between lie small winegrowing villages such as Cully, Epesses or Saint-Saphorin. Walking paths lead right through the vines.

So that vines can be planted on the steep slope, **walls of stone** were built. They hold the earth in place and form flat steps. The terraces were laid out **many hundreds of years ago** by **monks**, who owned monasteries in the area in the Middle Ages. Since then the winegrowers have repaired the walls again and again. Since **2007** the Lavaux has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

In the Lavaux people tell of **three suns** that ripen the grapes. The first is the sun in the **sky**. The second is the **lake**, which reflects the sunlight back onto the vines. The third are the **walls**, which store heat during the day and give it off again at night. This makes the Lavaux especially warm.

The most common grape variety in the Lavaux is **Chasselas**, from which a white wine is made. In autumn comes the **grape harvest**, in French **“vendange”**. Because the slopes are so steep, the grapes usually have to be picked **by hand**. Machines can hardly drive on the narrow terraces.

gewusst: Together, the terrace walls in the Lavaux are many hundreds of kilometres long.
Chasselas is the most important white grape of western Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The geography of Switzerland is very varied: in a small area there are high Alpine peaks, hills in the Central Plateau and the chains of the Jura. Each canton has its own highest point.
wichtigste: Switzerland consists of the Alps, the Central Plateau and the Jura.
The highest point of the canton of Uri is the Dammastock at 3,630 m.
At 3,614 m, the Tödi is the highest mountain in the canton of Glarus.
The Napf, at 1,408 m, is the highest point of the Central Plateau.
The Rheinwaldhorn is the highest mountain in Ticino.
Many of the cantons' highest points lie on cantonal borders.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland consists of three **major landscapes**: the **Alps** in the south, the **Central Plateau** in the middle and the **Jura** in the north-west. The Alps take up the largest part of the area. Most of the towns and cities are on the Central Plateau. The highest mountain in Switzerland is the **Dufourspitze** at 4,634 m in the Valais.

The highest point of the canton of **Uri** is the **Dammastock** at 3,630 m, on the border with the Valais. In **Glarus**, the **Tödi** rises to 3,614 m, the highest peak of the Glarus Alps. In the canton of **Schwyz** it is the **Bös Fulen** at around 2,802 m. In the canton of **Lucerne** it is the **Brienzer Rothorn** at 2,350 m, where Lucerne, Bern and Obwalden meet.

The **Napf**, between the Emmental and the Entlebuch, is the highest point of the **Central Plateau** at **1,408 m**. In the canton of **Fribourg**, the **Vanil Noir** at 2,389 m in the Gruyère region is the highest. In **Vaud**, the **Les Diablerets** massif at around 3,210 m forms the highest point, on the border with the Valais.

In the canton of **St Gallen**, the **Ringelspitz** at around 3,247 m is the highest peak, on the border with the Grisons. In **Ticino** it is the **Rheinwaldhorn**, also called the Adula, at 3,402 m on the border with the Grisons. It is striking that many highest points lie exactly on a **cantonal border**, because borders often run over peaks and ridges.

gewusst: The Napf is regarded as one of the finest viewpoints in the Central Plateau: in clear weather you can see the whole chain of the Alps.
In the mountains, cantonal borders often follow the watersheds, that is, the ridges between two valleys.

teile.einleitung: Gravel and sand are important raw materials for building. In Switzerland they are extracted in many gravel pits, above all on the Central Plateau.
wichtigste: The large gravel deposits on the Central Plateau come largely from deposits left by the Ice Ages.
Gravel is needed mainly for making concrete.
Because transport is expensive, gravel is extracted as close as possible to the building site.
In the canton of Zurich, an extraction area must be entered in the cantonal structure plan.
After extraction, a pit is usually filled in and restored.
Gravel pits are a habitat for the sand martin and the natterjack toad.
Gravel layers are often important groundwater aquifers.

abschnitte.titel: A legacy of the Ice Ages
abschnitte.text: During the **Ice Ages**, large glaciers covered wide parts of Switzerland. They pushed stones ahead of them and ground them down. Meltwater carried **gravel** and **sand** into the valleys and laid them down in thick layers. That is why there are large gravel deposits on the **Central Plateau** today. Gravel consists of rounded little stones that water has smoothed.

Most of the gravel is needed to make **concrete**. Concrete consists of gravel, sand, cement and water. Gravel is heavy but cheap. Something like this is called a **bulk material**. Because transport is expensive in proportion to the price, gravel is extracted as **close to the building site** as possible. The canton of Zurich requires large building sites to transport excavated material and gravel by **rail** wherever possible. That way fewer lorries are on the roads.

You cannot extract gravel just anywhere. In the canton of Zurich, an extraction area must first be entered in the **cantonal structure plan**. This plan sets out how land in the canton is to be used. To save gravel, a lot is **reused**: in the canton of Zurich in 2025, over 80 per cent of mineral building waste such as concrete and asphalt is reused. Old concrete is turned into **recycled concrete**.

**Gravel layers** are often important **groundwater aquifers**. The water flows through the gaps between the stones and is filtered as it does so. A large part of our drinking water comes from this groundwater. That is why gravel extraction is delicate where there is groundwater: it must not be polluted. After extraction, a pit is usually filled with **clean excavated soil** and **restored**, that is, turned back into meadow, field or forest.

Gravel pits are valuable habitats. The **sand martin** digs nesting burrows into the steep sandy walls and raises its young there. The **natterjack toad** is a **pioneer species**: it likes new, warm pools where hardly any plants are growing yet. In the past it found such places on wild rivers, today often in gravel pits. That is why in many pits areas are deliberately left free for nature.

gewusst: Sand martins used to nest on the steep banks of free flowing rivers, today almost only in gravel pits.
Gravel pits replace the gravel banks that disappeared when rivers were straightened, for many animals.

teile.einleitung: The Jungfraujoch is a mountain saddle between the Mönch and the Jungfrau in the Bernese Oberland. Up there lies the highest railway station in Europe, which you reach on the Jungfrau Railway.
wichtigste: A “Joch” is a crossing between two peaks.
The Jungfraujoch lies between the Mönch and the Jungfrau.
The Jungfraujoch station is at around 3,454 metres and is the highest railway station in Europe.
The Jungfrau Railway begins at the Kleine Scheidegg.
The railway was finished in 1912 after around 16 years of building.
The Sphinx is a research station with a viewing terrace.
There is an ice palace in the glacier ice.

abschnitte.text: A **Joch** is a lower point between two mountains, that is, a crossing. The **Jungfraujoch** lies between the **Mönch** and the **Jungfrau**. On one side you look into the Bernese Oberland, on the other onto the huge **Aletsch Glacier**. The area belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch. In advertising, the Jungfraujoch is called the “Top of Europe”.

The **Jungfrau Railway** starts at the **Kleine Scheidegg**. From there it first runs briefly in the open air and then in a long **tunnel** through the Eiger and the Mönch. On the way there are stops where you can look out through windows in the rock onto the ice. The building work was very difficult and took around **16 years**. In **1912** the railway finally reached the Jungfraujoch.

On a rock near the Jungfraujoch stands the **Sphinx**. The building has a dome and a **viewing terrace** from which you can see very far in clear weather. Inside the Sphinx there is a **research station**. Scientists measure the air and the weather there, for example. Because the station is so high up, the air there is especially clean.

In the glacier ice near the Jungfraujoch, passages and rooms have been carved out. This is called the **ice palace**. There are also **figures made of ice**, for example animals. Because it is always cold in the glacier, they do not melt. If you visit the Jungfraujoch, you should take warm clothes, because even in summer it is cold at the top and the air is thinner.

gewusst: The Jungfraujoch station lies in the rock and is the highest railway station in Europe.
The Jungfrau Railway runs most of the route through a tunnel in the mountain.

teile.einleitung: Montreux is a town in the canton of Vaud at the eastern end of Lake Geneva. It is known for its mild climate, with palms on the shore, and for the Montreux Jazz Festival, to which musicians from all over the world come every summer.
wichtigste: Montreux lies on Lake Geneva on the Vaud Riviera.
The Montreux Jazz Festival has existed since 1967 and takes place in July.
On the lakeshore stands a statue of Freddie Mercury.
Because of the mild climate, palms grow on the shore.
A rack railway runs up to the Rochers de Naye.
The GoldenPass connects Montreux with the Bernese Oberland.
In Advent there is the Christmas market “Montreux Noël”.

abschnitte.text: Montreux lies at the eastern end of **Lake Geneva**. The area around **Vevey** and Montreux is called the **Vaud Riviera**. The mountains protect the town from the cold north wind, so the climate is **mild**. On the lakeshore even **palms** grow. A long promenade with flowers invites you to take a stroll. Very close by, on a small rocky island, stands the well-known **Chillon Castle**.

The **Montreux Jazz Festival** was founded in **1967** by **Claude Nobs**. It takes place every year in **July**. At the beginning mainly jazz musicians played, and today stars from rock, pop and many other kinds of music also appear. It is one of the best-known music festivals in the world. Many concerts were recorded and are now a valuable archive.

**Freddie Mercury**, the singer of the band **Queen**, often worked in Montreux. The band had a recording studio here. Since **1996** a **statue** of him has stood on the lakeshore. Many fans visit it. The well-known song “Smoke on the Water” by the band **Deep Purple** also tells of Montreux: it is about a fire at the casino in 1971.

From Montreux a **rack railway** runs almost to the summit of the **Rochers de Naye**. At the top there is a park with **marmots**, and you can see far over Lake Geneva. The **GoldenPass** panoramic train runs from Montreux via **Zweisimmen** towards **Interlaken** in the Bernese Oberland. On the lake, old **paddle steamers** of the **CGN** shipping company with large paddle wheels operate.

In winter the lakeshore turns into a large **Christmas market**. It is called **“Montreux Noël”**, begins at the end of November and lasts into **December**. There are many little wooden huts with gifts and food. On the Rochers de Naye you can then even visit Santa Claus's house.

gewusst: Montreux is one of the best-known music towns in Switzerland, even though it is not very large.
Chillon Castle near Montreux is among the most visited historic buildings in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Maggia Valley is a long valley in the canton of Ticino that begins at Locarno and leads far into the mountains. It is known for its stone houses, the clear water of the Maggia and the smoothly polished rocks in the riverbed.
wichtigste: The Maggia flows through the Maggia Valley.
The valley begins north of Locarno.
The old stone houses are called rustici.
In the side valley of Bavona Valley, a high waterfall plunges down at Foroglio.
In Mogno stands a round stone church by Mario Botta.
Cevio is a larger village with a valley museum.

abschnitte.text: The **Maggia Valley**, in Italian Valle Maggia, branches off north of **Locarno**. The river **Maggia** flows through the whole valley and flows into **Lake Maggiore** between Locarno and Ascona. Further up, the valley divides into several **side valleys**, for example the **Bavona Valley** and the Val Lavizzara. The mountains are high and steep, and the villages often lie close to the river.

Over a very long time the Maggia has **polished smooth** the rocks in its bed. In many places large, round boulders lie in the water. In summer many people bathe among the rocks. The water is very clear, but also cold. After heavy rain the Maggia can swell quickly, so you have to be careful when bathing.

The old houses in the Maggia Valley are built almost entirely of **stone**. They are called **rustici**, and a single house is a **rustico**. Even the roofs are often covered with heavy **stone slabs**. In the past, farming families who kept goats and cows lived in them. Today many rustici are used as **holiday homes**.

In the **Bavona Valley** lies the village of **Foroglio**. There a high **waterfall** plunges over a rock face. In **Mogno** an old church was destroyed by an **avalanche**. In its place the Ticino architect **Mario Botta** built a modern church of light and dark **stone**. It is round and is regarded as a special building. In **Cevio** a **valley museum** shows how people used to live in the valley.

gewusst: For Mario Botta's church in Mogno, stones from the area were used, including light marble from the valley.
At Ponte Brolla, at the entrance to the valley, the Maggia has carved a deep gorge into the rock.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland has four national languages. Most cantons have only one official language, but four cantons are multilingual: Bern, Fribourg and Valais are bilingual, and the Grisons is even trilingual.
wichtigste: Four cantons have more than one official language.
Bern, Fribourg and Valais are bilingual: German and French.
The Grisons is trilingual: German, Romansh and Italian.
In the canton of Bern and in the Grisons, the majority speak German.
In Fribourg and in the Valais, the majority speak French.
Upper Valais is German speaking, Lower Valais French speaking.

abschnitte.text: An **official language** is a language in which authorities, courts and schools work. In a multilingual canton, **several official languages** apply at the same time. Laws are published in all the languages. Most of the time, however, the language groups live in different parts of the canton. The border between German and French is often jokingly called the **Röstigraben** (rösti ditch).

In the **Valais**, **German and French** are official languages. **Upper Valais** in the east, roughly from the Pfynwald to the Goms, is German speaking. **Central Valais** and **Lower Valais** in the west are French speaking. The majority speak French. The capital, called **Sitten** in German, is called **Sion** in French.

In the canton of **Fribourg**, about two thirds of the people speak **French** and about a quarter German. The city of Fribourg is also bilingual, and in German it is called Freiburg. In the canton of **Bern**, by contrast, the great majority speak **German**. French is spoken mainly in the **Bernese Jura**. The city of **Biel**, in French Bienne, is the largest bilingual city in Switzerland.

The **Grisons** is the only **trilingual** canton. The official languages are **German**, **Romansh** and **Italian**. About three quarters of the people speak mainly German. **Italian speaking Grisons** includes the **Val Poschiavo**, the **Bregaglia**, the **Misox** and the **Calanca Valley**. In the village of **Bivio** on the Julier Pass you can even hear all three languages side by side.

gewusst: Romansh is an official language of a canton only in the canton of the Grisons.
In Biel many street signs are bilingual, for example Bahnhofstrasse and Rue de la Gare.

teile.einleitung: The **Emme** is a river in the canton of Bern. It rises in the Bernese Pre-Alps, flows north through the Emmental and joins the Aare near Solothurn. It is known for its dangerous floods.
wichtigste: The Emme rises on the Bolberg between the Hohgant and the Augstmatthorn.
It flows north through the Emmental.
The Emme is about 82 kilometres long.
Near Solothurn it flows into the Aare.
The town of Burgdorf with its castle lies on the Emme.
Emmental cheese is named after the valley of the Emme.

abschnitte.text: The Emme rises in the **canton of Bern** on the **Bolberg**, between the **Hohgant** and the **Augstmatthorn**. These mountains lie in the Bernese Pre-Alps north of **Lake Brienz**. From there the Emme first runs down the valley as a wild mountain stream. Then it reaches the hilly **Emmental**, which is named after it.

The Emme flows **north** through the Emmental. At the entrance to the Emmental lies the town of **Burgdorf**. Above its old town stands **Burgdorf Castle**. After about **82 kilometres** the Emme flows into the **Aare** near **Solothurn**, between Zuchwil and Luterbach. That makes it much shorter than the Aare.

In the past the Emme was especially feared for its dangerous **floods**. In a heavy thunderstorm the river can swell very quickly. Then it sweeps away stones, wood and sometimes bridges as well. The writer **Jeremias Gotthelf** described the great flood of **1837** in his story “Die Wassernot im Emmental” (“The Flood Disaster in the Emmental”). Today dams and river defences protect the villages better.

The famous **Emmental cheese** is named after the valley of the Emme, a cheese with large holes. Beware of confusion: in the **canton of Lucerne** there is a river of its own called the **Kleine Emme**, which means “Little Emme”. It has nothing to do with the Emme in the canton of Bern. The Kleine Emme flows into the Reuss at **Emmenbrücke**.

gewusst: Jeremias Gotthelf wrote a whole story about the flood of 1837, “Die Wassernot im Emmental”.
There are two Emmes: the Emme in the canton of Bern and the Kleine Emme in the canton of Lucerne.

teile.einleitung: Interlaken is a well-known holiday resort in the Bernese Oberland. The town lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz. From here you can reach mountains such as the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau, which attract people from all over the world.
wichtigste: Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.
From the area you can see the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau.
The Höhematte is a large meadow in the middle of the town.
The Jungfraujoch at 3,454 metres is called the “Top of Europe”.
On the Schynige Platte there is an alpine garden.
At the Unspunnen Festival a stone weighing around 83 kilograms is thrown.

abschnitte.text: The name **Interlaken** comes from Latin and means “between the lakes”. The town lies on a plain between **Lake Thun** and **Lake Brienz**. The **Aare** links the two lakes. In the middle of the town lies the **Höhematte**, a large open meadow. It may not be built on and offers a clear view of the **Jungfrau**. **Paragliders** often land there.

From the area around Interlaken you can see the famous mountains **Eiger**, **Mönch** and **Jungfrau**. They form the best-known mountain chain of the **Bernese Oberland**. Since **1912**, the **Jungfrau Railway** has run through a tunnel in the Eiger and Mönch up to the **Jungfraujoch**. The station there is at **3,454 metres** and is the highest railway station in Europe. That is why it is called the “Top of Europe”.

A **funicular railway** goes straight from Interlaken up the **Harder Kulm** in a few minutes. From there you can see both lakes and the mountains. From **Wilderswil**, an old **rack railway** climbs the **Schynige Platte**. There is an **alpine garden** there with hundreds of plant species from the Alps.

In the nearby **Lauterbrunnen Valley**, the **Trümmelbach Falls** plunge down inside a mountain. They carry away the meltwater of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. You can visit them by lifts and paths. Very close by begins the **UNESCO World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch**. It includes the **Great Aletsch Glacier**, the largest glacier in the Alps.

Near Interlaken the **Unspunnen Festival** takes place, a large festival with Swiss wrestling, yodelling and traditional costumes. It only takes place every few years. Famous is the **stone throwing**. In it, the **Unspunnen Stone**, which weighs around **83 kilograms**, is thrown as far as possible. The first Unspunnen Festival took place in 1805.

gewusst: The Unspunnen Stone has already been stolen twice and later turned up again.
In Interlaken you hear very many different languages on the streets, because guests come from all over the world.

teile.einleitung: A glacial lake outburst flood is the sudden bursting of a glacial lake, with a flood wave. In Switzerland, such events have repeatedly threatened valleys.
wichtigste: A glacial lake outburst flood is the sudden bursting of a lake dammed by ice or moraine.
In 1818 a lake outburst at the Giétro Glacier devastated the Val de Bagnes.
An ice dam can float once the lake is deep enough.
Moraine dams are dangerous because the loose debris erodes quickly.
An ice or rock fall into the lake can also trigger a flood wave.
Protective structures have been built at the Glacier de la Plaine Morte and in Grindelwald.

abschnitte.titel: What is a glacial lake outburst flood?
abschnitte.text: Sometimes glacier ice or a **moraine**, a wall of debris, dams a lake. If this dam suddenly breaks, a **flood wave** pours into the valley. This is called a **glacial lake outburst flood**. In Icelandic it is called a jökulhlaup, and in English people speak of a GLOF.

**Ice** is lighter than water. If a lake dammed by ice becomes deep enough, the water pressure lifts the ice dam: it begins to **float**, and the water drains away beneath the glacier. **Moraine dams** consist of loose debris and can **erode** quickly. If ice or rock falls into the lake, a surge wave is created that can flow over the dam.

Ice collapses from the **Giétro Glacier** dammed the Dranse in the Valais **Val de Bagnes** into a lake. The engineer **Ignaz Venetz** had a **tunnel** dug through the ice dam to lower the lake. This reduced the amount of water. In June 1818 the dam broke anyway, and the flood devastated the valley as far as Martigny.

At the **Glacier de la Plaine Morte**, the **Lac des Faverges** empties almost every year and threatens the **Simmental** near Lenk. In 2019 a **channel** about 800 m long was cut into the ice so that the water drains away continuously. At the **Lower Grindelwald Glacier**, a **relief tunnel** was built in 2009 so that the glacial lake could be emptied in a controlled way.

In June 2024, the glacial lake **Calderas** in the Grisons suddenly drained. The water triggered debris flows and hit the **Alp Flix** in the municipality of Surses. Because glaciers are melting, new lakes are forming in the Alps. Experts therefore watch them closely.

gewusst: Ignaz Venetz later also became known as one of the pioneers of the ice age theory.
When the Lac des Faverges bursts each year, the water flows via the Trüebbach into the Simme.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Schwyz lies in Central Switzerland on Lake Lucerne. It is one of the three founding members of the Confederation and gave the whole country its name. The capital is also called Schwyz.
wichtigste: Switzerland takes its name from the canton of Schwyz.
The coat of arms is red with a small white cross in the corner.
The two Mythen rise above the town of Schwyz.
The Federal Charter lies in the Federal Charter Museum in Schwyz.
Einsiedeln Abbey is a large Benedictine monastery.
The Hölloch in the Muotatal is one of the longest caves in the world.
The town of Brunnen lies on Lake Lucerne.

abschnitte.text: Together with **Uri** and **Unterwalden**, Schwyz is one of the three members that concluded the **Federal Charter** in 1291. Already in the Middle Ages all the Confederates were called “**Schwyzer**”. Later the name **Schweiz** (Switzerland) grew out of this. The **Schwyz coat of arms** is red and has a small white cross in the top corner. It recalls the Swiss flag.

In the **Federal Charter Museum** in Schwyz lies the **Federal Charter**. It is an important **document** from the early history of the Confederation and is written in Latin. In it, the three members promised to help one another. In the museum you can also see old **flags** and further charters. Many school classes visit the museum.

Above the town of Schwyz rise the **Grosser** and **Kleiner Mythen** (Great and Little Mythen). The two pointed mountains are a landmark of the canton. In the **Muotatal** lies the **Hölloch**, one of the longest caves in the world. Researchers keep discovering new passages there. The town of **Brunnen** lies on **Lake Lucerne**, and boats sail from there across the lake.

In **Einsiedeln** stands a large **Benedictine monastery**. The abbey church is richly decorated inside. In it stands the **Black Madonna**, a dark figure of Mary. For many centuries people have made pilgrimages to Einsiedeln. The town also lies on the Way of St James, on which pilgrims walk through Switzerland.

gewusst: The whole country, Switzerland, is named after the canton of Schwyz.
The passages in the Hölloch are together over 200 kilometres long.

teile.einleitung: The Linth Correction was one of the first great building works in Switzerland. From 1807 the wild Linth was diverted into Lake Walen, to protect the Linth plain from floods and marshes.
wichtigste: The Linth Correction began in 1807.
It was led by Hans Conrad Escher.
The Linth was diverted into Lake Walen.
Before that the Linth plain was often flooded and marshy, and malaria was widespread.
The level of Lake Walen fell by about 5.5 metres.
The client was the Diet of the Old Confederation.
From 2008 to 2013 the Linth works were renewed.

abschnitte.text: In the 18th century the mountain slopes in the **Glarus region** were heavily logged. Without forest, a lot of debris slid into the **Linth**. The river deposited the rubble in the flat **Linth plain**, especially near **Ziegelbrücke**. As a result the **Maag**, the outflow of Lake Walen, became blocked.
