The Dukes of Milan had the castles greatly extended.
Since the year 2000 the castles have belonged to the UNESCO World Heritage.

abschnitte.titel: Three castles one above the other
abschnitte.text: The three castles lie as if on a staircase. Below in the city stands **Castelgrande**, which means “big castle”. Higher up the slope lies **Montebello**, the middle castle. Right at the top **Sasso Corbaro** stands enthroned. From there you can see far out into the valley.

Bellinzona lies at a narrow spot in the Ticino valley. Here routes meet that lead to important **Alpine passes** such as the Gotthard, Lukmanier and San Bernardino. With castles and walls this route could be blocked. From Castelgrande a long wall, the **Murata**, runs right across the valley to the river **Ticino**. Anyone who wanted to go through the valley had to get past this barrier.

In the Middle Ages Bellinzona long belonged to the Duchy of **Milan**. The **Dukes of Milan** greatly extended the castles to protect themselves against the Confederates in the north. Around 1500 Bellinzona nevertheless came under the rule of the Confederates from Uri, Schwyz and Nidwalden. After that the castles were no longer needed for wars.

abschnitte.titel: World Heritage and destination for outings
abschnitte.text: Since the year **2000** the three castles and the city walls have belonged to the **UNESCO World Heritage**. They are regarded as an especially well-preserved example of a medieval fortification. Today you can visit the castles. An easy way is a **lift** that runs up inside the rock of Castelgrande from the old town.

gewusst: The name Castelgrande simply means “big castle” in Italian.
The lift to Castelgrande runs up right through the rock.

teile.einleitung: The **Entlebuch** is a rural mountain region in the canton of Lucerne. It lies between the city of Lucerne and the Emmental. The region is known for its bogs and landscapes, which are protected as the **Entlebuch Biosphere**.
wichtigste: The Entlebuch lies in the canton of Lucerne and covers about 400 km².
The Glaubenberg Pass links the Entlebuch with Sarnen.
Sörenberg lies at the foot of the Brienzer Rothorn.
The Biosphere Centre is in Schüpfheim.
About a third of the workforce works in agriculture and forestry.
The Entlebucher Mountain Dog is the smallest Swiss mountain dog breed.

abschnitte.text: The Entlebuch lies in the **canton of Lucerne**, between the city of Lucerne and the **Emmental**. The region covers an area of **397 km²**. That is clearly more than the whole canton of Zug. Part of the border with the Bernese Emmental is formed by the river **Ilfis**. This border was already fixed in the 15th century.

The **Glaubenberg Pass** at 1,543 m above sea level links the Entlebuch with **Sarnen** in the canton of Obwalden. In the upper Entlebuch lies the holiday resort of **Sörenberg**. It belongs to the municipality of **Flühli** and lies at the foot of the **Brienzer Rothorn**. A cable car runs up to the summit. In winter Sörenberg is a popular ski area.

The Entlebuch is a **UNESCO biosphere reserve**. In a biosphere reserve nature is to be protected, and at the same time the people there are to be able to live and work well. Especially valuable are the many **bogs** of the region. The **Biosphere Centre** is in **Schüpfheim**. From there the biosphere reserve is looked after.

In the Entlebuch many people work in **agriculture and forestry**, about a third of the workforce. In the Swiss average it is only a few per cent. The **Entlebucher Mountain Dog** also comes from the region. It is the smallest of the four Swiss mountain dog breeds. In the past it helped the farmers to drive their cattle.

gewusst: An “Entlebucher” can also be a dog: the Entlebucher Mountain Dog.
The Entlebuch is larger than the whole canton of Zug.

teile.einleitung: Campione d'Italia is a small place on Lake Lugano that belongs to Italy but is entirely surrounded by Switzerland. Such an area is called an **exclave**. For a long time life there was almost like in Switzerland, today it is more closely tied to Italy.
wichtigste: Campione d'Italia lies on the eastern shore of Lake Lugano.
On land the place is completely enclosed by the canton of Ticino.
The municipality belongs to the Italian province of Como in Lombardy.
Since 1 January 2020 Campione has belonged to the customs territory of the EU.
Until the end of 2019 the cars had Ticino number plates.
The official currency is the euro, whereas in the past people mostly paid in francs.
The casino is well known, and its new building was designed by Mario Botta.

abschnitte.text: Campione d'Italia lies on the **eastern shore of Lake Lugano**. On one side is the lake, and on the land side the place borders only municipalities of the **canton of Ticino**. Anyone who wants to travel from Campione to Italy has to use Swiss roads. Politically, Campione is a municipality of the **province of Como** in the region of **Lombardy**.

In the Middle Ages a man called **Toto of Campione** left the place in the year 777 to the **monastery of Sant'Ambrogio** in Milan. The monastery owned Campione until 1797. That is why the place did not come to the Confederation like the rest of Ticino. In **1933** the Fascist dictator **Benito Mussolini** had the addition “d'Italia” attached to the name. In this way he wanted to stress that the place belongs to Italy.

For a long time everyday life in Campione was closely tied to Switzerland. Until the end of 2019 the place in fact belonged to the **Swiss customs territory**. The cars ran with **Ticino number plates** (TI), and in everyday life people mostly paid in **Swiss francs**. Most landline connections still have the Swiss dialling code **+41** today. People who ring from Italy therefore dial 0041.

abschnitte.titel: In the EU customs territory since 2020
abschnitte.text: Since **1 January 2020** Campione has belonged to the **customs territory of the European Union**. Since then cars have had to be registered in Italy. Officially the **euro** applies, because Campione is a part of Italy. The place is known for its **casino**. The large new building was designed by the Ticino architect **Mario Botta**, and it opened in 2007.

gewusst: Anyone who telephones Campione d'Italia from Italy mostly rings with the Swiss dialling code 0041.
When it opened in 2007 the casino of Campione was one of the largest casinos in Europe.

teile.einleitung: The **Valais** is the region of Switzerland with the greatest earthquake risk. In the past there were several strong quakes here. That is why special rules for earthquake-proof building apply in the Valais.
wichtigste: The Visp earthquake of 25 July 1855 was one of the strongest quakes in Switzerland.
On 25 January 1946 the ground shook in the area of the Wildhorn and the Rawil.
An aftershock on 30 May 1946 set off a rockfall on the Rawilhorn.
The Valais Rhône Valley lies in the highest earthquake zone, Z3b.
Soft loose sediments in the valley strengthen the earthquake waves.
Since 2018 all building projects in the Valais have had to be planned to withstand earthquakes.

abschnitte.text: The strength of an earthquake is described in two ways. The **magnitude** is a single value for the whole quake and measures the energy released. The **intensity**, by contrast, describes the **effect at a particular place**. It is graded according to observed damage and how strongly people feel the quake. Intensity decreases with distance from the focus of the quake.

On **25 July 1855** the **Visp earthquake** took place. It had an estimated magnitude of around 6.4 and is regarded as one of the strongest quakes in Switzerland in recent centuries. Numerous buildings and churches were damaged, and rockfalls broke loose in the Mattertal. On **25 January 1946** the epicentre lay in the area of the **Wildhorn and the Rawil** north of Sion. A strong aftershock on 30 May 1946 set off a **rockfall** on the Rawilhorn.

abschnitte.titel: Why the Rhône Valley is especially at risk
abschnitte.text: According to the standard **SIA 261**, the Valais Rhône Valley is assigned to earthquake zone **Z3b**. That is the highest earthquake zone in Switzerland, with possible shaking of intensity VIII to IX. The ground beneath adds to this: the valley is filled with thick, soft **loose sediments**. These deposits amplify the ground movement, a little like jelly wobbling. The damage there can be greater than on solid rock.

For places such as **Sion** or **Brig-Visp**, so-called **spectral microzonation maps** were drawn up. They show how strongly the **local ground** changes the earthquake waves at a place. In this way it is known where the ground shakes especially strongly. Buildings can then be planned and calculated accordingly.

Since **1 January 2018** the Valais building law has required all building projects to comply with the earthquake standards **SIA 260 ff.** The canton checks this in the **building permit procedure**. Because of the dense development in the Rhône Valley, the canton expects damage of **4.5 to 10 billion francs** in a quake of magnitude 6 near Sion. That is why precaution is regarded as especially important.

gewusst: An earthquake can set off further natural hazards: in 1946 an aftershock brought a mass of rock crashing down on the Rawilhorn.
Soft ground can strengthen earthquake waves, which is why it often shakes more in the valley than on rock.

teile.einleitung: A **catchment area** is the whole area from which water flows into a particular river. Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe, and its water flows into different seas. Here you can find out where the rain goes in the different parts of the country.
wichtigste: A catchment area includes all the land that drains into a river.
The boundary between two catchment areas is called a watershed.
About two thirds of Switzerland drains via the Rhine into the North Sea.
Geneva belongs to the catchment area of the Rhône.
From the Val Poschiavo the water flows to the Po, from the Val Müstair to the Adige.
In the “Water Castle” near Brugg, water from about 40 per cent of Switzerland collects.

abschnitte.text: Every raindrop flows downhill into a stream and finally into a river. All the areas whose water reaches the same river form its **catchment area**. The boundary between two catchment areas is called a **watershed**. It mostly runs along **mountain ridges** and **passes**. On one side the water flows into one river, on the other side into another.

abschnitte.titel: The Rhine and the North Sea
abschnitte.text: About **two thirds** of the area of Switzerland drains via the **Rhine**. For the **Aare**, **Reuss** and **Limmat** also belong to its area. Even **Lake Neuchâtel** in the west belongs to it: it drains via the Zihl into Lake Biel and from there with the Aare to the Rhine. In this way this water finally reaches the **North Sea**.

Near **Brugg** in the canton of Aargau the **Aare**, **Reuss** and **Limmat** flow together close to one another. Here the water from about **40 per cent** of the Swiss land area collects. That is why this place is called the **Water Castle of Switzerland**. Shortly afterwards the Aare flows into the Rhine.

The water from the Valais and from **Geneva** belongs to the area of the **Rhône**, which flows into the Mediterranean. The **Arve** from France also belongs there. From Ticino and the **Val Poschiavo** the water flows to the **Po**. The Poschiavino flows into the Adda and this into the Po, which enters the Adriatic. From the **Val Müstair** the **Rom** flows to South Tyrol into the **Adige**. The **Inn** from the Engadine flows via the Danube into the Black Sea.

gewusst: Although Lake Neuchâtel lies in the far west of Switzerland, its water ends up in the North Sea.
Water from Switzerland reaches four seas: the North Sea, the Mediterranean, the Adriatic and the Black Sea.

teile.einleitung: The Maloja Pass connects the Upper Engadine with the Bregaglia in the canton of the Grisons. It is an unusual pass: on one side it is almost flat, on the other it drops away steeply.
wichtigste: The Maloja Pass lies at about 1,800 metres above sea level.
The Engadine side is almost flat.
On the west side the road drops steeply into the Bregaglia with 13 hairpin bends.
The Bregaglia is Italian speaking and belongs to the Grisons.
The road was built by the Grisons engineer Richard La Nicca.
The painter Giovanni Segantini lived in Maloja from 1894.

abschnitte.titel: A pass with only one steep side
abschnitte.text: The top of the pass lies at **1,812 m above sea level**, and the highest point of the road is in the village of **Maloja** at 1,815 m. From there to the east lies the **Upper Engadine** with Lake Sils, and the valley drops away only very **gently**. To the west, however, the land plunges steeply into the **Bregaglia**. There the road winds down with **13 hairpin bends**. If you drive from the Engadine, you hardly notice that you are on a pass.

From **1827 to 1839** a road fit for vehicles was built over the Maloja Pass. The Grisons engineer **Richard La Nicca** was responsible. He was known for roads and river corrections. The road runs from the Engadine through the Bregaglia as far as **Chiavenna** in Italy. It is an important link between the Grisons and the south.

The **Bregaglia** is a valley west of the pass. It belongs to the canton of the **Grisons**, but people there speak **Italian**. The valley has a milder climate than the Engadine. Steep granite mountains frame it, and there are old villages with stone houses. In the Bregaglia you also find **chestnut woods**.

The painter **Giovanni Segantini** moved to Maloja in **1894**. He painted many pictures of the Engadine **mountain landscape** with bright light and wide meadows. In 1899 he died on the **Schafberg** in the Upper Engadine, where he was working on a large picture. A museum in St Moritz now shows many of his works.

gewusst: Near the Maloja Pass the Inn rises, whose water flows all the way to the Black Sea.
In the Engadine the Maloja wind often blows, coming from the Bregaglia over the pass into the valley.

teile.einleitung: The Matterhorn is the best-known mountain in Switzerland. With its pyramid shaped peak it stands above Zermatt in the Valais, exactly on the border with Italy.
wichtigste: The Matterhorn is 4,478 metres high.
The border between Switzerland and Italy runs over its summit.
In Italian it is called Monte Cervino, in Valais German Horu.
In 1865 it was climbed for the first time, and four men died on the descent.
In 1871 Lucy Walker stood on the summit as the first woman.
The normal route leads from the Hörnli Hut over the Hörnli Ridge.

abschnitte.text: The **Matterhorn** stands in the canton of the **Valais** above the village of **Zermatt**. It is **4,478 metres** high. Its shape came about because glaciers wore the mountain away from several sides. What was left is a steep peak with four ridges. The **border with Italy** runs over the summit. On the Italian side lies the village of **Breuil-Cervinia** in the Aosta Valley.

In Italian the mountain is called **Monte Cervino** or simply Cervino. In French people say Mont Cervin. The locals in Zermatt call it **Horu** in **Valais German**, which means “the horn”. The Matterhorn can be seen on many pictures, postcards and packages and is regarded as a symbol of Switzerland.

For a long time the Matterhorn was regarded as unconquerable. On **14 July 1865**, a roped party led by the Englishman **Edward Whymper** reached the summit for the first time. They climbed up the **Hörnli Ridge**. On the descent one climber slipped and pulled three others with him. The rope to the rest broke, and **four men** lost their lives. Only three survived. In **1871** the Englishwoman **Lucy Walker** stood on the summit as the first woman.

The **normal route** from Zermatt leads over the **Hörnli Ridge**, the north east ridge. Many climbers spend the night beforehand in the **Hörnli Hut**, which stands on this ridge. Early in the morning they set off for the summit with a **mountain guide**. The climb is difficult and suitable only for experienced mountaineers.

In the area around Zermatt lives the **Valais Blackneck goat**. It is black at the front and white at the back. In summer you often see its herds beneath the Matterhorn. Zermatt itself is car free. With the **Gornergrat Railway** you travel up to a viewpoint with a view of the Matterhorn and many glaciers.

gewusst: The Matterhorn was shaped by glaciers, and such a mountain is called a horn peak.
The Matterhorn is one of the most photographed mountains in the world.

teile.einleitung: The **Doubs** is a river that rises in France, forms part of the border with Switzerland for a stretch and makes a great loop through the canton of Jura. It is known for deep, wooded valleys and the waterfall **Saut du Doubs**.
wichtigste: The Doubs rises near Mouthe in the French Jura.
From Les Brenets it forms the border between Switzerland and France.
The Saut du Doubs is a waterfall about 27 metres high.
The loop called Clos du Doubs lies entirely on Swiss soil in the canton of Jura.
The Doubs flows into the Saône, and its water reaches the Mediterranean.
Source and mouth are only about 90 kilometres apart.

abschnitte.text: The Doubs rises near **Mouthe** in the **French Jura** from a **karst spring**. Karst is limestone rock in which the water flows underground and comes out again at springs. The river is around **450 kilometres** long but makes huge detours. As the crow flies, source and mouth are only about **90 kilometres** apart.

At the Neuchâtel village of **Les Brenets** the Doubs begins to form the **border** between Switzerland and France. There lies the **Lac des Brenets**. At the end of the lake the river plunges about **27 metres** down at the **Saut du Doubs**. You can reach the waterfall on foot or by **boat** across the lake.

abschnitte.titel: The loop in the canton of Jura
abschnitte.text: Further downstream the Doubs flows right into Switzerland. The great river loop is called the **Clos du Doubs**. It is about 29 kilometres long and lies entirely on Swiss soil in the **canton of Jura**. On it lies the pretty little town of **Saint-Ursanne**. After that the river turns back towards France.

abschnitte.titel: All the way to the Mediterranean
abschnitte.text: At **Verdun-sur-le-Doubs** in France the Doubs flows into the **Saône**. The Saône flows into the **Rhône** and this into the **Mediterranean**. In this way part of the Jura belongs to the catchment area of the Rhône. Most other rivers of northern Switzerland, by contrast, flow via the Rhine into the North Sea.

gewusst: The Doubs is around 450 kilometres long, although source and mouth are only about 90 kilometres apart.
You can travel to the Saut du Doubs by boat across the Lac des Brenets.

teile.einleitung: Zug is one of the smallest cantons in Switzerland and lies in Central Switzerland. It has two lakes, a pretty old town and a famous cake.
wichtigste: The canton of Zug is one of the smallest cantons in Switzerland.
The coat of arms is white with a blue horizontal bar.
The canton contains Lake Zug and Lake Ägeri.
In 2023 the canton of Zug had 11 municipalities.
After the city of Zug, Baar is the largest municipality.
The Zuger Kirschtorte is a well-known speciality.
On Lake Ägeri lies Morgarten, where a famous battle took place in 1315.

abschnitte.text: Zug is one of the **smallest cantons** in Switzerland. Even so, there are two lakes: **Lake Zug** and **Lake Ägeri**. The coat of arms is **white and blue**: white with a blue horizontal bar in the middle. In 2023 the canton had **11 municipalities**. After the city of Zug, **Baar** has the most inhabitants. Many international firms have their seat in the canton of Zug.

The old town of **Zug** lies right on Lake Zug. Its landmark is the **Zytturm**, a tower with a large clock and a colourful tiled roof. “Zyt” means “time” in Swiss German. Above the town lies the **Zugerberg**. You reach it by **funicular railway** and have a fine view at the top.

The **Zuger Kirschtorte** is a sweet speciality. It consists of layers of nut meringue, sponge and buttercream. The sponge is soaked in **kirsch**, a spirit made from cherries. In the Zug region there used to be very many cherry trees, and they are still typical of the area today.

Near **Baar** you can visit the **Höllgrotten**. These are stalactite caves. Over a very long time, water rich in lime formed stalactites and shimmering shapes there. Paths lead through the caves, and you can marvel at them on a guided tour or by yourself.

On the shore of Lake Ägeri lies **Morgarten**. Here in **1315** the **Battle of Morgarten** took place. The men of Schwyz defeated an army of the Habsburgs. The battle is regarded as an important event in the early history of the Confederation. Zug itself joined the alliance of the Confederates in 1352.

gewusst: The Höllgrotten near Baar were discovered in the 19th century while tuff stone was being quarried.
The Zytturm was built in the Middle Ages as part of the town's fortifications.

teile.einleitung: The Franches-Montagnes, in German called the Freiberge, are a high plateau in the Jura. With their wide pastures, single fir trees and horses they are among the special landscapes of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Franches-Montagnes lie mostly in the canton of Jura.
In German they are called the Freiberge.
The main town is Saignelégier.
The high plateau lies at about 1,000 m above sea level.
Typical are wooded pastures, pastures with single fir trees.
In the north and north-west the Doubs forms the boundary of the Franches-Montagnes.

abschnitte.titel: A high plateau in the Jura
abschnitte.text: The **Franches-Montagnes** lie in the south-west of the **canton of Jura**, and a small part belongs to the canton of Bern. In German they are called the **Freiberge**, which means “free mountains”. In the Middle Ages settlers who cleared the land received special **freedoms**. The main town is **Saignelégier**.

Typical of the Franches-Montagnes are the **wooded pastures**, called **Wytweiden** in German. These are pastures with trees on which cows and horses graze between single **fir trees**. Forest and pasture merge into one another. This landscape came about through the work of the farmers over centuries. Wooded pastures cover about a third of the Franches-Montagnes.

The high plateau lies at about **1,000 m above sea level**. The winters are long and cold. The ground consists of **limestone**, which has turned to karst. That means rainwater seeps into cracks and drains away underground. That is why there are hardly any streams on the plateau. In the north the **Doubs** has dug a deep valley.

The Franches-Montagnes are the home of the **Franches-Montagnes horse**, called the **Freiberger** in German, the only native breed of horse in Switzerland. In Saignelégier a large **horse market** takes place every year in August, the Marché-Concours. A well-known nature area is the **Étang de la Gruère**. This bog lake was dammed in the 17th century for a mill and is protected today.

gewusst: The Franches-Montagnes horse is a calm, strong horse that used to be used mainly in farming and in the army.
In winter the Franches-Montagnes are a popular area for cross-country skiing.

teile.einleitung: Solothurn lies on the Central Plateau at the foot of the Jura. The city of Solothurn is known for its Baroque old town and has a special favourite number: 11. The canton is named after the capital.
wichtigste: Solothurn joined the Confederation in 1481 together with Fribourg as its eleventh member.
The number 11 is regarded as the city's lucky number.
The St Ursus Cathedral is the landmark of Solothurn.
To the north, above the city, lies the Weissenstein.
The coat of arms is red at the top and white at the bottom.
Solothurn is also called the “ambassadors' town”.
Most people in the canton speak German.

abschnitte.text: In Solothurn the number **11** is especially popular. In the city there are many things **eleven times over**, for example churches, chapels, fountains and towers. This has to do with history: Solothurn joined the Confederation in **1481** together with Fribourg and was thus the **eleventh member**. That is why 11 is regarded as the city's **lucky number**.

The landmark of Solothurn is the **St Ursus Cathedral**. A broad **flight of steps** leads to its entrance. The church is named after Saint **Ursus**, the patron saint of Solothurn. It was built in the 18th century. The whole old town has many fine buildings from the **Baroque period**, which is why people speak of the most beautiful Baroque town in Switzerland.

In the past, the **ambassadors of the King of France** lived in Solothurn for a long time. In French an ambassador is called an **ambassadeur**. That is why Solothurn is also called the “**ambassadors' town**”. The ambassadors brought money and French style to the city. Splendid houses and gardens still recall this today.

To the north, above the city, lies the **Weissenstein**, a mountain in the **Jura**. You can go up by **gondola lift** and look far across the Central Plateau as far as the Alps. The **Aare** flows through the city of Solothurn. The canton's **coat of arms** is very simple: **red** at the top and **white** at the bottom. Most people speak **Swiss German** in everyday life.

gewusst: The number 11 also plays a part at the St Ursus Cathedral, for example in the altars and bells.
Solothurn was the eleventh member to be admitted to the Confederation.

teile.einleitung: The Misox is a valley in the south of the canton of the Grisons. It lies south of the Alps, Italian is spoken there, and it leads from the San Bernardino down to near Bellinzona.
wichtigste: The Misox belongs to the canton of the Grisons.
In the Misox people speak Italian.
In Italian the valley is called Mesolcina.
The Moesa flows through the valley.
The road over the San Bernardino leads through the Misox.
Roveredo is the largest place in the valley.
At Mesocco stands one of the largest castle ruins in Switzerland.

abschnitte.titel: A Grisons valley in the south
abschnitte.text: The **Misox**, in Italian **Mesolcina**, lies on the **south side of the Alps**. Although it belongs to the canton of the **Grisons**, people there speak **Italian**. The valley thus belongs to **Italian speaking Grisons**, like the Val Poschiavo and the Bregaglia. The **Moesa** flows through the whole valley. It flows into the Ticino at Arbedo, near **Bellinzona**.

At the upper end of the Misox lies the **San Bernardino**. A road leads over this pass from the Rheinwald into the Misox. Since 1967 there has also been the **San Bernardino Road Tunnel**. The **A13** motorway runs through it from Chur to Bellinzona. For many travellers the Misox is therefore an important link to the south.

Near the village of **Mesocco**, the ruin of **Mesocco Castle** stands on a rock. It is one of the **largest castle ruins** in Switzerland. In the past the lords of the castle controlled the route over the pass. Today you can visit the old walls and have a fine view into the valley.

The largest place in the valley is **Roveredo** in the lower Misox, not far from the border with Ticino. The small **Calanca Valley** branches off from the Misox. The Misox and the Calanca Valley together form the **Moesa region**. The climate in the lower valley is mild, and chestnut trees and vines grow there.

gewusst: Although the Misox belongs to the Grisons, it lies closer to Bellinzona than to Chur.
The Moesa region is named after the river that flows through the Misox.

teile.einleitung: The Gösgen nuclear power plant stands in the canton of Solothurn on the Aare. Its large cooling tower can be seen from far away.
wichtigste: The Gösgen nuclear power plant stands in the municipality of Däniken in the canton of Solothurn.
It lies on the Aare between Olten and Aarau.
A pressurised water reactor operates in the plant.
Commercial operation began in 1979.
A natural draught cooling tower releases water vapour into the air.

abschnitte.text: The **Gösgen nuclear power plant** stands in the municipality of **Däniken** in the canton of **Solothurn**. It lies on the **Aare** between Olten and Aarau. It is named after the nearby village of Gösgen. In **1979** the plant began **commercial operation**. Since then it has supplied an important share of Swiss electricity.

A **pressurised water reactor** operates in Gösgen. In the reactor, uranium atoms are split. This produces a lot of heat. The water in the inner circuit is under high **pressure**, so that it does not boil despite the great heat. It passes its heat on to a second circuit. There steam is produced, which drives a **turbine** and a generator.

Gösgen has a large **cooling tower**. The white cloud that comes out of the top is not smoke but **water vapour**. The cooling tower cools the steam down again after the turbine. This means the plant has to release much less warm water into the Aare than a plant cooled with river water.

gewusst: In suitable weather, the steam cloud above the Gösgen cooling tower can be seen from many kilometres away.

teile.einleitung: A hazard map shows where natural hazards such as floods, avalanches, landslides or rockfall can threaten people and buildings. In Switzerland it helps to build safely.
wichtigste: Hazard maps show dangers with the colours red, blue, yellow and yellow and white.
Red means considerable, blue moderate and yellow low danger.
The level results from intensity and probability of occurrence.
Events that occur about every 30, 100 and 300 years are studied.
The cantons draw up the hazard maps, based on the Forest Act and the Hydraulic Engineering Act of 1991.
They become binding through the land-use planning of the municipalities.

abschnitte.titel: What is a hazard map for?
abschnitte.text: In Switzerland there are many **natural hazards**: floods, avalanches, landslides and rockfall. A **hazard map** shows which areas are threatened and how strongly. In this way it can be decided where building is allowed and where protection is needed. The **cantons** are responsible for the maps, and the Confederation supports them with expertise and money.

**Red** means considerable danger, and there you may not build anything new as a rule. **Blue** is the regulation area with moderate danger: building is allowed with conditions, for example with reinforced walls. **Yellow** is the information area with low danger. **Yellow and white hatching** shows a residual danger from very rare events. That is important for hospitals, for example.

For the classification two quantities are combined: the **intensity**, that is, how strong an event is, and the **probability of occurrence**, that is, how often it happens. Events that occur about every **30, 100 and 300 years** are studied. Frequent strong events give red, rare weak ones yellow. For avalanches an area counts as a red zone from a pressure of **30 kN/m²**.

The **Forest Act** and the **Hydraulic Engineering Act** of **1991** oblige the cantons to record endangered areas. The Forest Act concerns avalanches, landslides and falling processes, the Hydraulic Engineering Act floods. The maps only become binding for landowners when the municipalities take them over into **land-use planning**, that is, into the zoning plan and building regulations.

gewusst: An avalanche pressure of 30 kN/m² corresponds to about 3 tonnes per square metre and can destroy normal buildings.
Hazard maps are revised when new protective structures are built or new events occur.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. Many people speak more than one language, and some towns are even bilingual.
wichtigste: The four national languages are set out in Article 4 of the Federal Constitution.
The Confederation publishes its laws in full in German, French and Italian.
In 2023 around 60 per cent named German as their main language.
In 2023 around 8 per cent named Italian as their main language.
In 2023 around 17 per cent had two or more main languages.
In German speaking Switzerland, people mostly speak Swiss German in everyday life.
Biel/Bienne is the largest bilingual city in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: **Article 4** of the **Federal Constitution** says: the national languages are **German**, **French**, **Italian** and **Romansh**. The Confederation publishes its laws in full in **German, French and Italian**. Romansh is an official language in dealings with Romansh speaking people. In Romansh, Switzerland is called **“Svizra”**.

Most people live in German speaking Switzerland. In 2023, **around 60 per cent** of the population named **German** as their main language. French comes second. **Italian** was named by around **8 per cent**, and Romansh by only a small part. Around **17 per cent** have **two or more main languages**. Many people also speak languages from other countries, for example English or Portuguese.

In German speaking Switzerland, people mostly speak **Swiss German** in everyday life. This is not one single language, but there are many **dialects**: Bernese sounds different from Basel or Valais German. What is written is mostly **Standard German**. In school, children therefore learn both.

Italian speaking Switzerland consists of **Ticino** and parts of the Grisons, the **southern Grisons valleys**. In Italian it is called **“Svizzera italiana”**. Anyone greeting someone there in the morning says **“Buongiorno”**, which means “Good day”. The Grisons is the only canton with three official languages: German, Romansh and Italian.

On the **language border** between German and French there are bilingual places. The largest bilingual city is **Biel/Bienne** in the canton of Bern. There the street signs are written in both languages, and many people switch language in the middle of a conversation. The cantons of **Bern**, **Fribourg** and **Valais** are also bilingual.

gewusst: The border between German and French is jokingly called the “Röstigraben” (rösti ditch).
Romansh has several written forms, and in addition there is the shared written language Rumantsch Grischun.

teile.einleitung: Zurich Airport in Kloten is the largest airport in Switzerland. From here millions of people fly all over the world every year.
wichtigste: Zurich Airport has the code ZRH.
It has three runways, the longest being runway 16/34 at about 3,700 m.
In 2025 about 33 million passengers used the airport.
The airline Swiss has its most important base in Zurich.
Flights are normally allowed from 6 am to 11 pm.
Since 1980 the airport has had a railway station of its own.

abschnitte.text: Every airport has a code of three letters, the **IATA code**. Zurich has **ZRH**, Geneva has GVA. In 2025 Zurich Airport counted about **33 million passengers**, more than ever before. The airline **Swiss** has its **hub** here: many travellers only change planes in Zurich.

The airport has **three runways**. The longest is **runway 16/34** at about 3,700 m, then come 14/32 at about 3,300 m and 10/28 at about 2,500 m. The numbers stand for the compass direction of the runway. Because some runways cross, running the airport is complicated.

Since **1980** there has been a **railway station** under the terminal. Long-distance trains and suburban trains run directly to the airport. To **Dock E** runs the **Skymetro**, a small train that glides on a cushion of air. Right next to the airport stands **The Circle**, a large building complex with hotels, offices and shops, opened in 2020.

Aircraft make noise. That is why take-offs and landings are normally allowed only from **6 am to 11 pm**. To make up for delays, flying is still allowed until 11.30 pm. The airport lies close to the border. **Germany** forbids approaches over southern Germany at certain times, in the evening, at night and in the early morning.

gewusst: The Skymetro floats on a cushion of air instead of rolling on wheels.
From Zurich Airport you are in the main station in about ten minutes by train.

teile.einleitung: The Glacier Express is a famous panoramic train through the Swiss Alps. It links Zermatt with St Moritz and takes its time so that passengers can enjoy the views.
wichtigste: The Glacier Express runs between Zermatt and St Moritz.
It is known as the “slowest express train in the world”.
The whole journey takes about 8 hours.
The highest point is the Oberalp Pass.
The train has existed since 1930.
It is run by the Rhaetian Railway and the Matterhorn Gotthard Railway.

abschnitte.text: The **Glacier Express** runs between **Zermatt** and **St Moritz**. The journey takes about **8 hours**. That is why people call it, with a wink, the **“slowest express train in the world”**. The train has existed since **1930**. It is run by the **Rhaetian Railway** and the **Matterhorn Gotthard Railway**.

The carriages have large **panoramic windows** that reach up into the roof. This means you can also see the high peaks above the train. On the way, the train crosses around **291 bridges** and goes through many tunnels. A well-known structure is the Landwasser Viaduct near Filisur in the Grisons.

The highest point of the line is the **Oberalp Pass** at around 2,033 m above sea level. In the past the train also went over the Furka. Since **1982** it has passed through the **Furka Base Tunnel** beneath the pass. This means the train can run all year round.

The line has **metre gauge**: the rails are one metre apart. That is narrower than on most railways on flat ground. Narrow-gauge railways can take tighter bends, which is handy in the mountains. On steep sections a **rack rail** between the rails helps.

gewusst: Part of the line belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage Site “Rhaetian Railway in the Albula/Bernina Landscapes”.
On the Glacier Express, food is served directly at your seat.

teile.einleitung: In a temperature inversion it is warmer above than below. In winter there is then often fog over the Central Plateau, while the sun shines on the mountains. The air in the valley can become poor.
wichtigste: In an inversion the temperature rises with height.
Normally it gets colder with increasing height.
The warm layer of air above acts like a lid.
That is why exhaust fumes and fine particles collect in the cold air near the ground.
Cold air in a hollow is called a cold-air pool.
In December, inversions often last longer than in March.

abschnitte.text: Normally it gets colder the higher you climb. In a **temperature inversion** it is the other way round: above a cold layer of air at the ground lies **warmer air**. “Inversion” means reversal. The boundary between the two layers is called the **inversion layer**. In winter, **high fog** often forms beneath it on the **Central Plateau**. On the mountains the sun then shines above a **sea of fog**.

A **ground inversion** forms on clear, windless nights. The ground radiates a lot of heat and cools the air directly above it. A **subsidence inversion** forms in a **high-pressure area**. There, air sinks over a wide area, is compressed and warms up. This creates a warm layer above colder air at the ground.

Cold air is **heavier** than warm air. It therefore flows down into low-lying places. In hollows and basins it stays put and forms a **cold-air pool**. A well-known example is the valley of **La Brévine** in the Neuchâtel Jura. Because of its cold winter nights it is called the “Siberia of Switzerland”.

The warm air above acts like a **lid**. Exhaust fumes from traffic and heating cannot rise and collect below. Smoke from a chimney spreads sideways beneath the inversion layer. **Fine particles** in particular then often reach raised levels. In winter they come mainly from wood fires and traffic. Ozone, by contrast, is a typical summer problem.

abschnitte.titel: Why it lasts longer in December
abschnitte.text: Around the **winter solstice** the days are short and the sun is low. Its strength often does not suffice to warm the cold air at the ground. That is why inversions in December often last for days. In March the sun is stronger and clears the fog more easily. A worked example: if you measure minus 3 °C at 400 metres and plus 5 °C at 1,000 metres, the temperature rises by 8 °C over 600 metres, that is, by around 1.3 °C per 100 metres.

gewusst: In an inversion it can be warmer on the Rigi or the Säntis than in Zurich.
If you stand above the sea of fog, the hills and mountains look like islands rising from a white ocean.

teile.einleitung: Nidwalden is a small canton in Central Switzerland on Lake Lucerne. Together with Obwalden it forms the old Unterwalden, one of the three founding members of the Confederation. The capital is Stans.
wichtigste: The coat of arms is red with a white double key.
Nidwalden has eleven municipalities (as of 2025), the largest being Stans.
In the north the canton borders Lake Lucerne.
The cable car “CabriO” with an open upper deck goes up the Stanserhorn.
The Bürgenstock is a well-known excursion destination above the lake.
The Winkelried Monument stands on the village square of Stans.

abschnitte.text: Nidwalden and **Obwalden** together form the old **Unterwalden**. In 1291, Unterwalden concluded the **Federal Charter** with Uri and Schwyz. Today they are two cantons in their own right, each with one seat in the Council of States. The Nidwalden **coat of arms** is red with a white **double key**. The key is the symbol of the **Apostle Peter**.

In the north, **Lake Lucerne** forms the border of Nidwalden. Places such as **Buochs** and **Beckenried** lie on the shore. From the Engelberg valley, the **Engelberger Aa** flows through the canton and joins the lake at Buochs. Nidwalden has **eleven municipalities** (as of 2025). The largest is the capital **Stans**.

The **“CabriO”** cable car goes up the **Stanserhorn** near Stans. It has an **open upper deck** where you stand in the open air during the ride. High above the lake lies the **Bürgenstock** with large hotels. From the top you can see far across Lake Lucerne. Both mountains are popular excursion destinations.

On the village square of **Stans** stands the **Winkelried Monument**. It commemorates **Arnold Winkelried**, a hero from a legend. According to this legend he came from Nidwalden and helped the Swiss Confederates at the **Battle of Sempach** in 1386. Whether Winkelried really existed is not certain among historians. The story is nevertheless very well known in Switzerland.

gewusst: When it opened, the cable car up the Stanserhorn was the first aerial cable car in the world with an open upper deck.
Nidwalden and Obwalden both have a key on their coat of arms.

teile.einleitung: Vaud is a large canton in western Switzerland between Lake Geneva, the Jura and the Alps. French is spoken here, and winegrowing has a long tradition.
wichtigste: The capital of Vaud is Lausanne.
The flag is white and green and bears the words “Liberté et Patrie”.
Vaud has a share of Lake Geneva and Lake Neuchâtel.
Until 1798 Vaud was a subject territory of Bern.
Vaud has been a canton of Switzerland since 1803.
The famous Chillon Castle stands right on Lake Geneva.
The Fête des Vignerons takes place in Vevey.

abschnitte.text: The flag of Vaud is **white and green**. In the white part are the words **“Liberté et Patrie”**, which mean “Liberty and Fatherland”. The capital is **Lausanne**, a city on Lake Geneva with many hills. The number plate code of Vaud is **VD**, from “Vaud”, the French name of the canton.

The canton has a share of two large lakes: **Lake Geneva** in the south and **Lake Neuchâtel** in the north. At the southern end of Lake Neuchâtel lies the town of **Yverdon-les-Bains**. It is known for its warm thermal water. Parts of the **Jura** and the **Alps** also belong to the canton.

From the 16th century, Vaud was a **subject territory** of **Bern**. The Bernese installed bailiffs who administered the land. In **1798** Vaud became independent of Bern. Since **1803** it has been a canton of Switzerland with equal rights. The words on the flag recall this.

**Chillon Castle** stands on a rock right on **Lake Geneva**, near Montreux. It is one of the best-known castles in Switzerland and very old. In the past, its owners controlled the road along the lake from here. Today very many people visit the castle every year.

On the slopes above Lake Geneva grow many **vines**, for example in the **Lavaux**. In **Vevey** the **Fête des Vignerons** takes place, a huge festival of winegrowers. It is celebrated only about every 20 to 25 years. A typical dish is the **papet vaudois**: leeks and potatoes are cooked together and served with a sausage.

gewusst: The Fête des Vignerons in Vevey is part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage.
By area, Vaud is one of the largest cantons in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The climate of Switzerland is very varied, even though the country is small. The Alps divide Switzerland into a north and a south with different weather.
wichtigste: The west wind usually brings rain from the Atlantic to the north side of the Alps.
Ticino has the mildest climate in Switzerland.
The foehn is a warm, dry downslope wind.
The central Valais is one of the driest regions in Switzerland.
The Swiss heat record is 41.5 degrees, measured in 2003 in Grono.
The lowest temperature was measured in 1987 in La Brévine.
The air gets colder with increasing height.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe. Mostly the **west wind** blows from the **Atlantic**. It brings moist air, which rises over the mountains and falls as rain. That is why quite a lot of rain falls on the **north side of the Alps**, and snow in winter. On the Central Plateau there is often **fog** in autumn and winter, while it is sunny in the mountains above.

South of the Alps it is clearly milder. **Ticino** has the mildest climate in Switzerland, and in many gardens even **palm trees** grow. **Locarno** is among the sunniest places in the country. When it rains in the south, it is often heavy. The Swiss **heat record** of **41.5 degrees** was measured in **2003** in **Grono** in the Misox, a valley in the Grisons on the south side of the Alps.

The **foehn** is a warm, dry **downslope wind**. With the **south foehn**, air flows from the south against the Alps. It rises, cools down and often lets heavy rain fall on the **south side of the Alps**. On the north side the dry air then sinks down into the valley and warms up strongly as it does so. Foehn is often stormy and brings clear views.

The **central Valais** is one of the **driest** regions in Switzerland. It is surrounded on all sides by high mountains that keep the rain out. The clouds drop their rain on the mountain slopes beforehand. That is why the people of the Valais used to water their meadows with long water channels, the Suonen.

On the mountains it is mostly **colder** than in the valley. The **air cools with increasing height**, on average by about 0.6 degrees per 100 metres. But it can also get especially cold in hollows, where cold air collects. That is how the **lowest temperature** in Switzerland was measured in **1987** in **La Brévine** in the Neuchâtel Jura. For this reason the place is also called the “Siberia of Switzerland”.

gewusst: In La Brévine, minus 41.8 degrees was measured in January 1987.
The foehn can make the temperature on the north side of the Alps rise by many degrees within hours.

teile.einleitung: The city of St Gallen wanted to draw heat from deep inside the Earth to warm its homes. The geothermal project was planned on a large scale, but had to be abandoned.
wichtigste: In 2010, around 83 per cent of the voters in the city of St Gallen approved the project.
The framework credit was 159 million francs.
The drilling site was in the Sittertobel.
The heat was mainly meant to flow into the city's district heating network.
In July 2013 the drilling triggered an earthquake of magnitude around 3.5.
Because too little hot water flowed, the power plant was not built.

abschnitte.text: On 28 November 2010, the voters of the **city of St Gallen** approved a **framework credit** of **159 million francs** with around **83 per cent**. This was to pay for drilling, a power plant and the expansion of the **district heating network**. The city wanted to replace heating oil and natural gas with local, renewable heat.

The project was **hydrothermal**: the aim was to bring up hot water from a water-bearing rock layer, an **aquifer**, at a depth of around 4,000 metres. The cooled water was to flow back down through a second borehole. Drilling took place from the **Sittertobel**, in the west of the city. At depth they measured around **140 to 145 °C**, as expected.

In July 2013, **natural gas** unexpectedly flowed into the borehole at a depth of around 4,450 metres. To stabilise it, heavy drilling fluid was pumped in. On 20 July 2013 the ground shook with a **magnitude of around 3.5**. The quake was clearly felt in the region, but caused only slight damage.

In tests, only about 6 litres of hot water flowed per second instead of the roughly 50 litres needed. Running the plant economically was therefore not possible. The city gave up the power plant. Earlier, in **Basel**, the **Deep Heat Mining** project had been stopped after noticeable earthquakes in 2006. St Gallen had therefore deliberately chosen a different method.

gewusst: The temperature at depth was exactly right; the only problem was that the amount of water was too small.
Other geothermal projects in Switzerland now learn from the experience of Basel and St Gallen.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland is about 41,300 square kilometres in size. That is small compared with many countries in Europe, yet on this area there are mountains, lakes, forests, fields and cities.
wichtigste: Switzerland is about 41,300 km² in size.
From west to east it measures about 350 km, from north to south about 220 km.
The Alps take up about 60 per cent of the area.
About a quarter of the area is unproductive, such as rock, glaciers and waters.
A good third is used for farming, alpine pastures included.
Settlements make up about 8 per cent of the area.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland measures about **41,300 km²**. From **Chancy** in the west to the **Val Müstair** in the east it is about **350 km** as the crow flies. From **Bargen** in the north to **Chiasso** in the south it is about **220 km**. By train you can cross the country in a day.

Germany is about **357,000 km²** in size. If you divide this number by the area of Switzerland, you get about 8.6. So Switzerland fits about **9 times** into Germany. Even so, Switzerland is bigger than Belgium, for example.

Switzerland consists of three **major landscapes**. The **Alps** cover about 60 per cent of the area, the **Central Plateau** about 30 per cent and the **Jura** about 10 per cent. Most people, however, live on the Central Plateau, because the land is flatter there.

The **Federal Statistical Office** measures with the **land use statistics** how the ground is used. According to the survey of 2018, about **a quarter** is unproductive: rock, scree, glaciers and waters. About **36 per cent** is **agricultural land**, alpine pastures included. Just under a third is **forest**. The **settlement area** with houses, roads and railway lines makes up just under **8 per cent** and grows mainly on the Central Plateau.

gewusst: If you pressed the mountains of Switzerland flat, their area would be much bigger than 41,300 km².
Forest covers almost as much of the area of Switzerland as agriculture does.

teile.einleitung: On 28 May 2025, the Birch Glacier broke off above the village of Blatten in the Lötschental. Ice and rock buried almost the whole village, which had been evacuated in time.
wichtigste: On 28 May 2025 the Birch Glacier broke off above Blatten.
Beforehand, rock from the Kleines Nesthorn had been falling onto the glacier for days.
Millions of tonnes of rock debris overloaded the glacier until it collapsed.
On 19 May 2025 the authorities ordered the evacuation.
Around 90 per cent of the village was buried.
The Lonza was dammed into a lake.

abschnitte.text: From mid-May 2025 the rock face of the **Kleines Nesthorn** became unstable. In several rockfalls, rock fell onto the **Birch Glacier** below. By the end of May, about 9 million tonnes of rock lay on the ice. Even in the years before, the glacier's snout had unusually **advanced**, because more and more debris weighed on it.

The Birch Glacier had been observed since an **ice collapse in December 1993**. That is why experts recognised the danger early. On **19 May 2025** the authorities ordered the **evacuation** of Blatten. Around 300 people had to leave their homes within a short time. The early evacuation prevented a large number of casualties.

On **28 May 2025** the overloaded glacier collapsed almost completely. Ice, rock and debris plunged into the valley. The **Swiss Seismological Service** recorded a signal of **magnitude 3.1**. Around **90 per cent** of the village of Blatten was buried, including about 130 houses and the church.

abschnitte.titel: A new lake and the consequences
abschnitte.text: The masses of debris blocked the river **Lonza** and dammed it into a **lake**. This flooded parts of the village that had not been buried. The **Swiss Insurance Association** estimated the insured damage at around **320 million francs**. Forest, farmland and a nature reserve were also lost.

gewusst: The debris cone above Blatten is in places up to 100 metres thick.
Before the collapse, the ice was moving at about 10 metres a day.

teile.einleitung: Aargau lies in the north of Switzerland between Basel and Zurich. It is known for its many castles, its rivers and its nickname “Rüebliland” (carrot country). The capital is Aarau.
wichtigste: The canton of Aargau was founded in 1803.
It is also called the “canton of castles”.
The Habsburg family comes from the Habsburg near Brugg.
Near Windisch lay the large Roman camp of Vindonissa.
In the north the Rhine forms the border with Germany.
The Beznau and Leibstadt nuclear power stations are in Aargau.
By population, Aargau ranks fourth among the cantons.

abschnitte.text: Aargau lies on the **Central Plateau**. In the east it borders the canton of **Zurich**, in the west **Solothurn** and **Basel-Landschaft**. In the north flows the **Rhine**, and on the other side lies Germany. The Aare, Reuss and Limmat also flow through the canton and meet near Brugg. In the south lies **Lake Hallwil**, a small part of which belongs to the canton of Lucerne.

In Aargau there are very many **castles and manor houses**, for example **Lenzburg**, **Hallwyl** and **Wildegg**. That is why it is also called the “canton of castles”. Especially famous is the **Habsburg** near Brugg. The **Habsburg** family comes from there. They later became very powerful and for a long time were emperors in Austria.

Around 2,000 years ago a large camp of Roman soldiers lay near **Windisch**. It was called **Vindonissa**. Even today you can see remains of the camp and an amphitheatre there. Much later, the lands of Aargau belonged to various lords. Only in **1803** did Aargau become a canton in its own right, with **Aarau** as its capital.

In the past, particularly many **carrots** were grown in Aargau. In Switzerland carrots are also called **Rüebli**, which is why Aargau is called “Rüebliland”. The Aargau carrot cake is also well known. Today Aargau is an important place for **energy**: the **Beznau** and **Leibstadt** nuclear power stations and many hydroelectric power stations on the rivers are here. With many inhabitants, Aargau ranks **fourth** among the cantons.

gewusst: One of the most powerful ruling families in Europe, the Habsburgs, takes its name from a castle in Aargau.
Near Brugg the Aare, Reuss and Limmat flow together. This spot is called the Wasserschloss (“water castle”).

teile.einleitung: The Gotthard Road Tunnel carries cars and lorries under the Gotthard Pass. It links German-speaking Switzerland with Ticino and is one of the most important roads across the Alps.
wichtigste: The tunnel runs between Göschenen in Uri and Airolo in Ticino.
The A2 motorway runs through it.
At around 17 km it is the longest road tunnel in the Alps.
On 24 October 2001 a serious fire broke out after a lorry accident.
In 2016 the people voted in favour of building a second tube.
The second tube is due to open around 2030.

abschnitte.text: The **Gotthard Road Tunnel** runs between **Göschenen** in the canton of Uri and **Airolo** in Ticino. It is around **17 km** long and opened in **1980**. The **A2** motorway runs through it. It is the **longest road tunnel in the Alps**.

Today there is only **one tube**. In it, cars drive in **two-way traffic**, that is, in both directions side by side. This is demanding and requires great care. Lorries may only drive with a gap between them. In the holidays, long **traffic jams** often form in front of the tunnel.

On **24 October 2001**, two lorries collided in the tunnel. A **serious fire** broke out, in which eleven people lost their lives. Safety was improved afterwards. Since then, for example, stricter rules apply to lorries, and there are more refuges.

The tunnel is old and has to be **renovated**. So that it is not closed for long while this happens, a **second tube** is being built. The people voted for this in **2016**. The new tube is due to open around **2030**. After that the old tube will be renewed. Later, only one lane per direction is to be used in each tube.

gewusst: A safety tunnel runs parallel to the road tunnel, and people can escape through it in an emergency.
Above the tunnel, the pass road over the Gotthard is still open in summer.

teile.einleitung: The **Energy Strategy 2050** is the Confederation’s plan for Switzerland’s energy supply. It relies on using less energy, more renewable energy and a step-by-step exit from nuclear energy. The voters accepted important parts of it at the ballot box.
wichtigste: The strategy is based on efficiency, renewable energy and a step-by-step exit from nuclear energy.
The trigger was the reactor disaster at Fukushima in March 2011.
On 21 May 2017 the people accepted the new Energy Act with 58.2 per cent.
Since then no general licences may be granted for new nuclear power plants.
On 9 June 2024 the Electricity Act was accepted with 68.7 per cent.
The Mühleberg nuclear power plant was switched off in December 2019.

abschnitte.text: The Energy Strategy 2050 has three pillars. First, less energy is to be used, which is called **efficiency**. Second, **renewable energy** is to be expanded, for example water, sun and wind. Third, Switzerland is leaving **nuclear energy** step by step. Existing nuclear power plants may keep running as long as they are safe.

In **March 2011** a serious reactor disaster occurred at the Japanese nuclear power plant **Fukushima Daiichi**. After that the **Federal Council** and **Parliament** decided on a step-by-step exit from nuclear energy. On **20 December 2019** the energy company BKW took the **Mühleberg** nuclear power plant off the grid for economic reasons. It was the first Swiss commercial nuclear power plant to be shut down for good, and it has been dismantled ever since.

A **referendum** was called against the new **Energy Act**. On **21 May 2017**, **58.2 per cent** voted in favour. So the first package of measures came into force in **2018**. Since then no **general licences** may be granted for new nuclear power plants any more. The **grid surcharge** on every kilowatt hour used rose from 1.5 to at most **2.3 centimes**. It finances support payments for renewable energy and the restoration of waters.

On **9 June 2024** the voters accepted the **Electricity Act**, also called the **“Mantelerlass”**, with **68.7 per cent**. It makes it easier to build large hydro, wind and solar plants. By **2035** at least **35 terawatt hours** of electricity a year are to be produced from renewable energy without hydropower, for example from sun, wind and biomass. That is many times today’s production from these sources.

By 2050 Switzerland is pursuing the goal of **net zero**. This means that no more greenhouse gases are emitted than natural and technical stores can absorb. For this, fossil energy must be largely replaced by electricity from renewable sources. Part of the **CO2 levy** on heating oil and natural gas flows into the **Buildings Programme** of the Confederation and the cantons. It supports heat insulation and renewable heating systems.

gewusst: On the Energy Act and the Electricity Act the people had the last word at the ballot box.
In 2019 Mühleberg in the canton of Bern was the first Swiss nuclear power plant to be switched off for ever.

teile.einleitung: Lucerne is the largest canton in Central Switzerland. It lies on Lake Lucerne and is known for the city of Lucerne, its carnival and many lakes. The capital is also called Lucerne.
wichtigste: Over 400,000 people live in the canton of Lucerne, more than in any other canton of Central Switzerland.
In 1332 Lucerne joined the Confederation as its first city.
The coat of arms is divided vertically into blue and white.
Willisau is known for Willisauer Ringli.
The Swiss Ornithological Institute has its seat in Sempach.
Lucerne was the capital of the Helvetic Republic in 1798 to 1799.
The Lucerne Carnival begins with the Urknall.

abschnitte.text: The canton of Lucerne lies in **Central Switzerland**. Over **400,000 people** live in the canton, more than in all the other cantons of Central Switzerland. The city of Lucerne lies on **Lake Lucerne**. Other lakes are, for example, **Lake Sempach** and Lake Baldegg. In **Sempach** the **Swiss Ornithological Institute** has its seat, which studies and protects birds.

In **1332**, Lucerne concluded an alliance with **Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden**. It was the first **urban member** of the Confederation. The **Lucerne coat of arms** is divided vertically into a **blue** and a **white** half. From 1798 to 1799, Lucerne was for a short time the capital of the **Helvetic Republic**, after Aarau and before Bern.

In the city of Lucerne, the wooden **Chapel Bridge** crosses the Reuss. Next to it stands the octagonal **Water Tower**. The bridge is among the best-known landmarks of Switzerland. Above the city rises **Pilatus**. Many tourists from all over the world visit Lucerne every year.

The **Lucerne Carnival** begins on **Fat Thursday** (Schmutziger Donnerstag) at five o'clock in the morning. At the reveille, **Bruder Fritschi** arrives in the city on a ship. A loud bang, the **Urknall** (“big bang”), is the starting signal for the **Guggenmusigen**, the carnival brass bands. A sweet speciality from **Willisau** are the hard **Willisauer Ringli**, which have been made since the 19th century.

gewusst: The Chapel Bridge in Lucerne is regarded as one of the oldest covered wooden bridges in Europe.
Lucerne was for a short time the capital of the whole of Switzerland, at the time of the Helvetic Republic.

teile.einleitung: The Zurich Metropolitan Area is the region around Zurich that is closely tied to the city economically. It extends over several cantons, because many people commute to Zurich every day for work or school.
wichtigste: The Zurich Metropolitan Area association was founded in 2009.
At the time of its founding, around two million people lived in the area.
Whether a municipality belongs is decided mainly by commuter flows.
The Metropolitan Conference has a chamber of the cantons and one of the municipalities.
The Swiss Spatial Concept knows three metropolitan areas: Zurich, Basel and the Lake Geneva region.
The metropolitan area includes several agglomerations.
Zurich Airport in Kloten is the largest airport in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: An **agglomeration** is a continuous urban area around a core city. A **metropolitan area** is larger: it includes **several agglomerations**, for example Zurich, **Winterthur** or **Zug**. What matters most is the **commuter interdependence**, that is, how many people travel back and forth between a municipality and Zurich every day. That is why municipalities from neighbouring cantons also belong.

In **July 2009** the **Zurich Metropolitan Area association** was founded. At that time about **1.9 million** people lived in the area, in 238 municipalities, and there were about 900,000 jobs. The association is meant to strengthen cooperation between cantons, cities and municipalities. Questions about transport, housing or the economy do not stop at the cantonal border.

The most important body is the **Metropolitan Conference**. It has two **equal chambers**: one for the **cantons** and one for the **cities and municipalities**. This way both levels of government have a say. As in the federal parliament, both sides must agree for something to be decided jointly.

The **Swiss Spatial Concept** is a joint plan of the Confederation, cantons and municipalities for the development of the country. It names three **metropolitan areas**: **Zurich**, **Basel** and the **Lake Geneva region**. In addition there is the **Capital Region of Switzerland** around Bern, which is listed separately. These areas are the economic centres of Switzerland.

Many people mean a lot of traffic. Since **2022** the **Limmattal light railway** has run continuously from **Zurich-Altstetten** to **Killwangen-Spreitenbach**. It serves the fast growing **Limmat Valley** and is meant to help build the settlements along the line more densely. Another important location factor is **Zurich Airport**, which lies mostly on the territory of **Kloten**.

gewusst: The Zurich Metropolitan Area reaches beyond the borders of the canton of Zurich into several neighbouring cantons.
The Zurich S-Bahn connects many places in the metropolitan area and gets very many commuters to their destination every day.

teile.einleitung: Obwalden is a canton in Central Switzerland. Together with Nidwalden it used to form Unterwalden. It is known for Lake Sarnen, the Titlis and Brother Klaus, the patron saint of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The capital of Obwalden is Sarnen on Lake Sarnen.
Engelberg has belonged to Obwalden since 1815, but lies separately from the rest of the canton.
At around 3,238 metres, the Titlis is the highest mountain in the canton.
Brother Klaus lived as a hermit in the Ranft near Flüeli.
Over the Brünig Pass you reach the Bernese Oberland.
The coat of arms is red at the top and white at the bottom, with a key.

abschnitte.text: The capital of Obwalden is **Sarnen**, on **Lake Sarnen**. The mountain village of **Engelberg** also belongs to the canton, and has done since **1815**. But Engelberg lies completely apart from the rest of the canton, because **Nidwalden** lies in between. Obwalden and Nidwalden together form the old **Unterwalden**; today they are two cantons in their own right.

The highest mountain in Obwalden is the **Titlis**. It is around **3,238 metres** high and has a glacier. From Engelberg you go up by **cable cars**, one of which rotates during the ride. In the south the **Brünig Pass** leads from Obwalden to **Meiringen** in the Bernese Oberland. A railway also runs over the Brünig.

**Brother Klaus** was really called **Niklaus von Flüe**. He lived in the 15th century and later withdrew as a **hermit** to the **Ranft** near Flüeli. Many people came to him to ask for advice. He is said to have helped the Confederates reach agreement in the **Covenant of Stans** in 1481. Today he is regarded as the **patron saint of Switzerland**, and many people make a pilgrimage to the Ranft.

The **coat of arms** of Obwalden is **red** at the top and **white** at the bottom. On it is a **key** in the reversed colours. In the State Archive in Sarnen lies the **White Book of Sarnen**, an old chronicle from the 15th century. It contains one of the oldest written versions of the story of **William Tell**.

gewusst: On the Titlis there is a cable car whose cabin turns completely round once during the ride.
Brother Klaus was canonised by the Catholic Church in 1947.

teile.einleitung: The Great Aletsch Glacier in the Valais is the largest glacier in the Alps. It is around 20 kilometres long and belongs to the Jungfrau-Aletsch UNESCO World Heritage Site. Because of climate change it is melting fast.
wichtigste: The Great Aletsch Glacier is the largest glacier in the Alps.
At the Konkordiaplatz the ice is over 900 metres thick.
The area has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001.
In 2017 it covered around 78 square kilometres, compared with around 105 in 1850.
The river Massa is formed from its meltwater.
Dark stripes on the ice are called medial moraines.

abschnitte.text: A **glacier** is a huge mass of ice that moves slowly down a valley. The Great Aletsch Glacier is formed from several firn streams. The longest tributary is the **Great Aletsch Firn** at around 9 kilometres. Then there are the **Jungfraufirn** and the **Grüneggfirn**. They flow together at the **Konkordiaplatz**. There the ice is more than **900 metres** thick.

Glacier ice moves slowly. Near the Konkordiaplatz the Aletsch Glacier flows at up to about **180 metres a year**. When two arms of a glacier flow together, their edges of rubble join to form a **medial moraine**. On the Aletsch Glacier these can be seen as long, dark stripes. The meltwater flows south as the **Massa** and joins the Rhône above Naters.

Above the glacier's snout lies the **Aletsch Forest**. It grows on an old lateral moraine near the **Riederfurka**. There stand many old **Swiss stone pines** and larches. The forest is protected. From the **Eggishorn** above Fiesch there is a famous view of the glacier, and also from the Riederalp and the Bettmeralp.

In December **2001** the Jungfrau-Aletsch area was added to the **UNESCO World Heritage** list. It was the first natural heritage site in the Alps. Later the area was enlarged. Today it is called **Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch**. World Heritage means that a place is especially valuable to the whole of humanity.

Since about 1850 the Aletsch Glacier has shrunk greatly. At that time it covered around **105 square kilometres**, and in **2017** only around **78**. The main cause is the **warming of the climate**. In the past the glacier dammed the **Märjelensee**. When this lake burst out suddenly, there were serious floods on the Massa in the 19th century.

gewusst: At the Konkordiaplatz you could stack several tall towers one on top of another under the thick ice.
The glacier's snout has retreated by several kilometres since 1850.

teile.einleitung: The **Eiger** is one of the best-known mountains in Switzerland. It stands in the Bernese Oberland above Grindelwald. Its steep **north face** is world-famous and was long regarded as one of the most dangerous walls in the Alps.
wichtigste: The Eiger is about 3,967 metres high and stands in the canton of Bern.
Below the Eiger lies the village of Grindelwald.
The Eiger north face is about 1,650 metres high.
In 1858 Charles Barrington of Ireland was the first to stand on the summit.
In 1938 Heckmair, Vörg, Harrer and Kasparek climbed the north face.
The Jungfrau Railway runs through the Eiger in a tunnel.

abschnitte.titel: A mountain in the Bernese Oberland
abschnitte.text: The **Eiger** is about **3,967 metres** high. It stands in the **canton of Bern**, in the Bernese Oberland. Together with the **Mönch** and the **Jungfrau** it forms a famous trio. Directly below its north face lies the village of **Grindelwald**. From there you can see the dark wall rising steeply.

In **1858** a person reached the summit for the first time. It was the Irishman **Charles Barrington**. On 11 August 1858 he climbed up with the Grindelwald mountain guides **Christian Almer** and **Peter Bohren**. They did not choose the north face but an easier route.

The **Eiger north face** is about **1,650 metres** high. It is among the best-known and most difficult rock walls in the Alps. Falling stones and sudden changes in the weather made it feared. From **21 to 24 July 1938** the first climb was achieved. Anderl **Heckmair**, Ludwig **Vörg**, Heinrich **Harrer** and Fritz **Kasparek** managed it together.

The **Jungfrau Railway** runs in a long tunnel through the Eiger and the Mönch up to the **Jungfraujoch**. In the middle of the mountain it stops at the **Eismeer station**. There travellers look through large windows at glaciers. The earlier Eigerwand station has no longer been served since 2016. Since **December 2020** the **Eiger Express** cable car has brought visitors quickly from Grindelwald to the **Eigergletscher** station.

gewusst: The Jungfrau Railway stops in the middle of the Eiger so that you can look at the ice through windows.
The first climb of the north face in 1938 took four days.

teile.einleitung: An avalanche is a large mass of snow that slides down a mountainside. Avalanches can be very dangerous, which is why Switzerland has warnings, protective structures and rules for snow sports fans.
wichtigste: The avalanche bulletin for Switzerland is published by the SLF in Davos.
Slab avalanches cause the most deaths among snow sports fans.
Snow slabs can break away from a slope angle of about 30 degrees.
Ski tourers carry an avalanche transceiver.
After about 15 minutes the chance of survival for buried people drops sharply.
Avalanche barriers protect many mountain villages.
The winter of 1951 went down in Swiss history as the “avalanche winter”.

abschnitte.text: An **avalanche** forms when snow comes loose on a steep slope and slides down into the valley. There are different kinds. In a **loose snow avalanche**, everything starts at one point and the avalanche gets wider as it goes down. In a **slab avalanche**, a whole layer of snow breaks away at once. A **powder avalanche** whirls up a lot of snow and can be very fast.

Among snow sports fans, **slab avalanches** cause the most deaths. Often the person triggers the slab themselves when they cross a weak layer of snow. Snow slabs can **break away from a slope angle of about 30 degrees**. That is why ski tourers pay close attention to how steep the slopes are and to the warnings.

The **WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF** in **Davos** publishes the **avalanche bulletin** in winter. It shows the **avalanche danger** for each region on a scale from 1 (low) to 5 (very high). Anyone going off the pistes should read the bulletin beforehand. When the danger is high, municipalities also close roads and pistes.

Ski tourers carry an **avalanche transceiver**. It sends a signal that other devices can pick up. They also carry a shovel and a probe. Quick rescue is very important, because the **chance of survival drops sharply after about 15 minutes**. That is why companions must start searching immediately and not wait for help. **Avalanche dogs** also help with the search.

Above many mountain villages, **avalanche barriers** of steel grids or wooden walls stand on steep slopes. They hold the snow in place so that it does not slide in the first place. **Protective forest** also holds back avalanches. Many of these structures were built after the **avalanche winter of 1951**. At that time almost 100 people died in avalanches in Switzerland.

gewusst: A powder avalanche can reach speeds of over 200 kilometres per hour.
The five level avalanche danger scale applies across the whole of Europe.

teile.einleitung: Molasse is the name given to the rocks that form the ground of the Swiss Central Plateau. They consist of debris that rivers carried from the growing Alps into the foreland millions of years ago.
wichtigste: Molasse is the erosion debris of the rising Alps.
It was deposited roughly 34 to 5 million years ago.
The basin came about because the weight of the Alps pressed the Earth's crust downwards.
Four groups are distinguished, in which sea and fresh water alternated twice.
Bernese sandstone comes from the Upper Marine Molasse.
At the edge of the Alps lies the folded Subalpine Molasse.
Fossil sharks' teeth show that there was once a sea here.

abschnitte.text: As the **Alps** were forming, they were at the same time being worn away. Rivers carried **rubble, sand and clay** from the mountains into the foreland. Over time these deposits became rock: rubble became **conglomerate**, in Switzerland often called **Nagelfluh**, sand became **sandstone** and clay became **marl**. Together, these rocks are called **molasse**. They were deposited roughly **34 to 5 million years ago**, in the Oligocene and Miocene.

The heavy mountain range pressed the **European Earth's crust** in front of it downwards. In this way a long trough formed north of the Alps, the **Molasse Basin** or **foreland basin**. It gradually filled with debris. Near the edge of the Alps the molasse is in places **over 4,000 metres** thick, and towards the Jura it becomes thinner.

In the Molasse Basin, **sea** and **land** alternated twice. That is why four groups are distinguished, from old to young: **Lower Marine Molasse**, **Lower Freshwater Molasse**, **Upper Marine Molasse** and **Upper Freshwater Molasse**. In the marine molasse you often find fossil **sharks' teeth**. They show that the basin was connected with the sea. **Bernese sandstone**, from which many houses of the Bernese old town are built, comes from the Upper Marine Molasse.

When the rivers came out of the mountains into the flat land, they became slower and lost strength. That is why they dropped the **coarse rubble first**, close to the edge of the Alps, in large **debris fans**. Finer sand and clay were carried further into the basin. That is why you find Nagelfluh mainly at the edge of the Alps, for example at the Rigi, and finer rocks further out.

At the **edge of the Alps** the molasse was **pushed together** during the late mountain building. Its layers were folded, stacked in slices and **set steeply**. This strip is called the **Subalpine Molasse**. Further north, by contrast, the layers lie almost flat. This **Central Plateau Molasse** forms the ground under most of the Central Plateau.

gewusst: The summit of the Rigi consists of Nagelfluh, that is, petrified river rubble from the molasse period.
Bernese sandstone was quarried mainly in Ostermundigen near Bern.

teile.einleitung: The Hölloch in the Muotatal is one of the longest cave systems in the world. To date, researchers have surveyed over 210 kilometres of passages. The cave lies deep in the limestone of the canton of Schwyz.
wichtigste: The Hölloch lies near Stalden in the Muotatal in the canton of Schwyz.
By November 2022, over 210 kilometres of passages had been surveyed.
The mountain farmer Alois Ulrich began exploring it in 1875.
The passages were formed because water dissolved the limestone.
The difference in height inside the cave is around 1,000 metres.
After heavy rain, flooding can block the passages.

abschnitte.text: The entrance to the **Hölloch** lies near **Stalden** in the **Muotatal** in the canton of Schwyz. From there the cave system stretches far beneath the karst area of the **Silberen**. By **November 2022**, around **210 kilometres** of passages had been surveyed. Research continues all the time. This makes the Hölloch one of the longest caves in the world.

In **1875**, the mountain farmer **Alois Ulrich** from Stalden was the first to venture far into the Hölloch. Systematic exploration began in **1889**. Later, cavers drew plans of the passages on many expeditions. Some research trips last several days. The researchers spend the nights in the cave.
