The Hölloch lies in **limestone**. Rainwater takes up **carbonic acid** from the air and the soil. This water can chemically **dissolve** limestone. Over a very long time, passages and halls were formed in this way. This process is called **karstification**. The difference in height between the lowest and the highest point is **1,033 metres**.

The cave system has roughly **three levels**. The lowest usually lies below the **karst water table** and is filled with water. That is why most of it cannot be entered. After heavy rainfall the water rises quickly and can block passages. Researchers have been trapped in the cave for several days until the water fell again.

In the cave it is always dark and cool. Even so, small animals live there. In **2010** a new **pseudoscorpion** was described: **Pseudoblothrus infernus**. Pseudoscorpions are tiny arachnids without a poisonous sting. This species is adapted to life in complete **darkness**. Visitors can see the front part of the cave on guided tours.

gewusst: The Latin name “infernus” of the pseudoscorpion means roughly “from the underworld” and fits the name Hölloch, which means “hell hole”.
In the cave it is similarly cool all year round, whether it is summer or winter outside.

teile.einleitung: The Mönch is one of the best-known mountains in Switzerland. Together with the Eiger and the Jungfrau it forms a famous group of three in the Bernese Oberland, which you can see from far away.
wichtigste: The Mönch stands in the Bernese Oberland between the Eiger and the Jungfrau.
It is about 4,100 metres high, and a measurement in 1999 gave 4,110 metres.
This makes the Mönch one of the four thousanders of the Alps.
Many climbers start at the Jungfraujoch, which can be reached by train.
The Mönchsjoch Hut lies high up near the Mönch.
In 1857 the Mönch was climbed for the first time.

abschnitte.text: From Interlaken or Grindelwald you see three mighty peaks side by side: the **Eiger**, the **Mönch** and the **Jungfrau**. The Mönch stands exactly in the middle. The Eiger is the lowest of the three, the Jungfrau the highest. The peaks lie on the border between the cantons of Bern and Valais. Behind them begins the great glacier world around the Aletsch Glacier.

The Mönch is about **4,100 metres** high. A measurement in 1999 gave 4,110 metres above sea level. Because it is higher than 4,000 metres, it counts as one of the **four thousanders**. Its summit is covered with ice and snow. Even in summer it can be very cold and windy up there.

The Jungfrau Railway runs through a tunnel in the Eiger and the Mönch as far as the **Jungfraujoch**. From there it is not far to the Mönch. That is why the Mönch is popular with climbers. Even so, you need experience, good equipment and often a mountain guide. The **Mönchsjoch Hut** lies high up at the Mönchsjoch and can be reached on foot from the Jungfraujoch.

In **1857** Sigismund Porges, together with mountain guides, was the first to reach the summit. This was in the time when many Alpine peaks were being climbed for the first time. This period is called the **golden age of mountaineering**. Today many people climb the Mönch every year.

A **Mönch** (monk) is a man who lives in a monastery and prays. The name of the mountain, however, probably has a different origin. On the Alpine pastures at the foot of the mountain, **geldings**, that is, male horses, used to be kept in summer, and they were called “Münche”. The mountain above them was therefore first called Münchenberg.

gewusst: The tunnel of the Jungfrau Railway runs through the Mönch, and the highest railway station in Europe lies on the Jungfraujoch.
The summits of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau belong to the UNESCO World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch.

teile.einleitung: The **Engadine** is a long high valley in the canton of Graubünden. Through the valley flows the Inn, called “En” in Romansh, from which the Engadine takes its name. It is known for lakes, mountains, old customs and St Moritz.
wichtigste: The Engadine lies in the canton of Graubünden in the east of Switzerland.
The Inn is called “En” in Romansh and gives the valley its name.
Many people there speak Romansh.
St Moritz hosted the Winter Olympics in 1928 and 1948.
On 1 March the children celebrate Chalandamarz.
The water of the Inn flows via the Danube into the Black Sea.

abschnitte.text: The Engadine is a long **high valley** in the canton of **Graubünden**. It begins at the Maloja Pass and stretches north-east as far as the border with Austria. People distinguish the **Upper Engadine** with its lakes and the **Lower Engadine**. Through the valley flows the **Inn**. In Romansh it is called **“En”**, and that is where the name Engadine comes from.

In the Engadine many people speak **Romansh** as well as German, one of the four national languages of Switzerland. An old custom is **Chalandamarz** on 1 March. Then the children go through the village with **bells** and drive away the winter. The children’s book **“Schellen-Ursli”** (“Ursli and the Cowbell”) tells of it too. At the festival Ursli wants to carry the biggest bell, and the story is set in **Guarda**.

abschnitte.titel: St Moritz and the ski marathon
abschnitte.text: The well-known holiday resort of **St Moritz** lies in the Upper Engadine. The Winter Olympics took place there in **1928** and **1948**. Every year the **Engadin Ski Marathon** takes place. Thousands of people run on cross-country skis from **Maloja** to **S-chanf**. At **Pontresina** the car-free **Val Roseg** branches off. Many guests go there by horse-drawn carriage to the Roseg Glacier.

A well-known speciality is the **Engadine nut tart**. It is filled with **walnuts** and **caramel**. The Inn flows from the Engadine to **Austria** and enters the **Danube** at **Passau**. The Danube flows all the way to the **Black Sea**. In this way water from the Engadine travels very far to the east.

gewusst: The Engadine is named after its river: the Inn is called “En” in Romansh.
Water from the Engadine flows via the Inn and the Danube as far as the Black Sea.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland consists of 26 cantons. Each canton has its own laws, its own government and its own coat of arms, and together they form the federal state.
wichtigste: Switzerland has 26 cantons.
The Grisons is the largest canton by area.
The most people live in the canton of Zurich.
The canton of Schwyz gave the whole of Switzerland its name.
Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are regarded as the founders of Switzerland.
On Swiss number plates, the abbreviation of the canton comes before the number.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland is divided into **26 cantons**. You can imagine them like the pieces of a puzzle that together make up the country. Each canton has its own **constitution**, its own **government** and its own **parliament**. The cantons decide, for example, on schools, police and hospitals. This sharing of power is called **federalism**.

The largest canton by area is the **Grisons**, with many mountains and valleys. The smallest is **Basel-Stadt**. The most people live in the canton of **Zurich**, the fewest in **Appenzell Innerrhoden**. However different the cantons are, in the **Council of States** every canton has the same number of votes.

The three **original cantons** of **Uri**, **Schwyz** and **Unterwalden** are regarded as the founders of Switzerland. According to tradition, they made an alliance in **1291**. Later more places joined. The canton of **Schwyz** gave the whole country its name, and the Swiss cross also goes back to the flag of Schwyz. The youngest canton is the **Jura**, which has existed since 1979.

Every canton has an **abbreviation** of two letters, for example BE for Bern or GE for Geneva. It appears on **number plates** before the number, and next to it is the canton's coat of arms. So you can tell on the road which canton a car comes from. Every canton also has a **capital**, where the government and parliament work.

gewusst: Six cantons have only one seat in the Council of States instead of two, for example Obwalden and Nidwalden.
In Appenzell Innerrhoden and Glarus, people vote in the open air at the Landsgemeinde.

teile.einleitung: The glaciers in Switzerland are getting smaller because it keeps getting warmer. This decline is called glacier retreat. It is greatly changing the landscape of the Alps.
wichtigste: There are around 1,400 glaciers in Switzerland.
The main cause of glacier retreat is global warming.
The Alpine glaciers last reached a great peak around 1850.
In 2022 the Swiss glaciers lost about 6 per cent of their ice.
In 2019 the Pizol Glacier was bid farewell with a funeral ceremony.
Where a glacier melts, stones and often a new lake are left behind.

abschnitte.text: A glacier is a large mass of ice that forms from snow. If more ice melts in summer than snow is added in winter, it shrinks. The main cause is **global warming**: temperatures are rising. There are around **1,400 glaciers** in Switzerland, and almost all of them are getting smaller.

Around **1850** the Alpine glaciers reached their last great **peak**. Since then they have been retreating, and in recent decades ever faster. In **2022** the Swiss glaciers lost about **6 per cent** of their ice, more than ever measured. At the **Morteratsch Glacier**, **signs with dates** along the path show where the ice used to be.

The **Pizol Glacier** in the St Gallen Alps has shrunk so much that it is hardly considered a glacier any more. In **2019**, people bid it farewell with a **funeral ceremony**. They wanted to show how serious glacier retreat is. At the **Rhône Glacier**, part of the ice is covered with **white sheets** in summer so that it melts more slowly.

abschnitte.titel: What remains and what is missing
abschnitte.text: Where a glacier disappears, **stones**, debris and sometimes a **new lake** are often left behind. In summer the **meltwater** is important for the **rivers**, for hydropower plants and for farming. If the glaciers get smaller, this water will one day be missing in hot summers.

gewusst: The white sheets on the Rhône Glacier reflect sunlight back and so slow down the melting.
Some glaciers in Switzerland could disappear completely by the end of this century.

teile.einleitung: The **Ceneri Base Tunnel** is a railway tunnel in the canton of Ticino. It runs under the Monte Ceneri and is the last big building block of the new flat railway through the Alps. Since it opened, Lugano and Locarno have moved much closer together.
wichtigste: The Ceneri Base Tunnel passes under the Monte Ceneri between Bellinzona and Lugano.
It is part of the NEAT, together with the Gotthard Base Tunnel.
The tunnel consists of two single-track tubes with cross passages.
The rock was mostly blasted, not bored.
The main breakthrough took place in January 2016.
The journey time from Locarno to Lugano was halved to around 30 minutes.

abschnitte.text: The **Monte Ceneri Pass** lies at about 554 metres above sea level. It separates the area around Bellinzona from the area around Lugano. The pass is not high, but for heavy **freight trains** the gradient was nevertheless an obstacle. The **north portal** of the tunnel lies at Vigana in the municipality of Camorino, the **south portal** at **Vezia** near Lugano. The tunnel is around 15 kilometres long.

abschnitte.titel: The flat railway through the Alps
abschnitte.text: The Ceneri Base Tunnel belongs to the **NEAT**, the New Rail Link through the Alps. Together with the Gotthard Base Tunnel it forms a **flat railway**. That means trains can travel through the Alps almost without any gradient. Without the Ceneri, heavy freight trains would have had to climb a gradient once more before Lugano. Only with it is the route flat all the way.

At the Gotthard, huge **tunnel boring machines** did most of the work. At the Ceneri, by contrast, the rock was mostly excavated by **drill and blast**. In this method holes are drilled into the rock, filled with explosive, and then the rock is cleared away. In **January 2016** the **main breakthrough** took place. After that tracks, railway technology and safety systems were installed.

As at the Gotthard, the trains run in **two separate single-track tubes**. In each tube the trains go in only one direction. **Cross passages** join the two tubes. In an emergency, passengers can in this way escape into the other, safe tube.

Since it opened in 2020, especially people in Ticino have benefited. The journey time between **Locarno** and **Lugano** has been halved to around **30 minutes**. Bellinzona and Lugano are also linked faster. In this way Ticino has grown together into one connected **suburban railway area**.

gewusst: Thanks to the tunnel, the journey from Locarno to Lugano takes only about half as long as before.
Only with the Ceneri Base Tunnel is the Gotthard axis flat all the way to Lugano.

teile.einleitung: The canton of St Gallen lies in Eastern Switzerland between Lake Constance, the Rhine Valley and Lake Walen. It completely surrounds the two Appenzells. The capital, St Gallen, is known for the Abbey District with its famous library.
wichtigste: The canton of St Gallen was founded in 1803 by the Act of Mediation.
The parliament is called the Cantonal Council and meets in the Abbey District.
The coat of arms shows a bundle of rods with an axe.
In the Rhine Valley the canton borders Austria and Liechtenstein.
Rorschach is a port town on Lake Constance.
Wil is called the “abbots' town”.
Bad Ragaz uses warm spring water from the Tamina Gorge.

abschnitte.text: The canton of St Gallen came into being in **1803** through Napoleon's **Act of Mediation**. It was formed from areas of the former **Prince-Abbot** of St Gallen and from several subject territories. The **coat of arms** shows a bundle of rods with an **axe**. It is a symbol of **unity**, because many rods together are strong. The parliament is called the **Cantonal Council** and meets in the government building in the **Abbey District**.

In the city of St Gallen stood a famous **monastery** that goes back to the monk Gallus. The **Abbey District** with its cathedral and **Abbey Library** is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the library lie very old, valuable manuscripts. The town of **Wil** was for a long time the residence of the **Prince-Abbots** of St Gallen. That is why it is called the **abbots' town**.

abschnitte.titel: Lake Constance and the Rhine Valley
abschnitte.text: In the north lies **Lake Constance**. There lies the port town of **Rorschach**, from which passenger boats depart. In the east the **Rhine** flows through the St Gallen **Rhine Valley**. It forms the border with **Austria** and with **Liechtenstein**. The canton of St Gallen completely surrounds the two Appenzells, which lie like an island in its middle.

In **Bad Ragaz** there is warm **thermal water**. It comes from the **Tamina Gorge** near Pfäfers and is piped to Bad Ragaz. High above **Lake Walen** lies the **Flumserberg** skiing and walking area. From there you can see the lake and the jagged **Churfirsten**. St Gallen is also known for its **bratwurst** and for fine **embroidery**.

gewusst: The Abbey Library of St Gallen is one of the oldest libraries in the world.
The two Appenzells lie completely within the canton of St Gallen, like an island.

teile.einleitung: During the ice ages a large part of Switzerland was covered by thick glaciers. The ice planed out valleys, created lakes and left marks in the rock. The landscape of Switzerland is still strongly shaped by these times today.
wichtigste: The last great cold period in the Alps is traditionally called the Würm glaciation.
About 24,000 years ago the glaciers were at their greatest extent.
At that time the Rhône Glacier reached from the Valais as far as the area of Solothurn.
About 11,700 years ago the last ice age came to an end.
Many lakes on the Central Plateau lie in basins that glaciers scooped out.
The Little Ice Age lasted from about 1300 to 1850.

abschnitte.text: The last great cold period in the Alps is traditionally called the **Würm glaciation**. In Switzerland people also speak of the **Birrfeld glaciation**. About **24,000 years ago** the glaciers were at their greatest extent. At that time ice covered large parts of the **Central Plateau**. About **11,700 years ago** the ice age came to an end. Since then we have been living in a warm period, the **Holocene**.

The glaciers flowed out of the Alps far into the lowlands. The ice-age **Rhône Glacier** flowed from the Valais across the area of Lake Geneva into the Central Plateau. It reached as far as the area of **Solothurn** and **Wangen an der Aare**. Other glaciers too, for example from the Reuss Valley or the Linth area, pushed far to the north.

Many large lakes on the Central Plateau owe their origin to the glaciers, for example **Lake Zurich**. The ice deepened valleys and **scooped out basins**. When the glaciers melted, these basins filled with water. Often the lake was also dammed by **moraines**. Moraines are ridges of stones and debris that a glacier leaves behind.

Glaciers leave typical marks. Stones on the underside of the ice grind the rock smooth and scratch grooves into it. In this way a **glacial polish** arises. The scratches show in which direction the ice flowed. Under the glacier **meltwater** also swirled in circles carrying stones. These stones ground round, deep holes into the rock, the **potholes**, called **Gletschertöpfe** in German.

Even after the last ice age the climate fluctuated. Roughly between **1300 and 1850** there was a cooler period that is called the **Little Ice Age**. The summers were cooler, and the Alpine glaciers advanced several times. Some villages in the Alps were threatened at that time by growing glaciers. Since the end of that period the glaciers have been melting back again.

gewusst: Lake Zurich lies in a basin that an ice-age glacier scooped out.
At the Glacier Garden in Lucerne you can see potholes from the Ice Age.

teile.einleitung: Cross-border commuters live abroad and work in Switzerland. Every day or every week they cross the border. There are especially many in Geneva, Basel and Ticino.
wichtigste: In the second quarter of 2026, according to the FSO, around 414,000 foreign cross-border commuters worked in Switzerland.
More than half live in France, followed by Italy and Germany.
Geneva has the most cross-border commuters, while in Ticino they make up the largest share of all employees.
Cross-border commuters from abroad receive the G permit.
Cross-border commuters from the EU and EFTA must return to their place of residence at least once a week.
In Ticino they are called “frontalieri” in Italian.

abschnitte.text: A **cross-border commuter** lives in a neighbouring country and works in Switzerland. Many cross the border every day by car, train or bus. According to the **Federal Statistical Office (FSO)**, there were around **414,000** people in the second quarter of 2026. Their number has more than doubled since the mid-1990s.

More than half of the cross-border commuters live in **France**, above all around Geneva and Basel. **Italy** and **Germany** follow. The canton of **Geneva** is almost entirely surrounded by France and has the most cross-border commuters. In **Ticino** their share of all employees is the highest. Many of them commute from the provinces of Como, Varese and Verbano-Cusio-Ossola.

abschnitte.titel: The G permit and the rules
abschnitte.text: Anyone who works in Switzerland as a cross-border commuter gets the **G permit**, the cross-border commuter permit. Other permits are B for residence, C for settlement and L for short stays. For people from the **EU** and **EFTA**, it is enough to return to their place of residence abroad at least **once a week**. In the past, a daily return was required.

Where cross-border commuters pay tax is governed by **agreements** between the countries. With **Italy**, a new cross-border commuter agreement has applied since **July 2023**. Since then, new cross-border commuters have also been taxed more heavily in Italy. This changes how attractive a job in Ticino is for them.

Many cross-border commuters work in hospitals, in industry, in retail or on building sites. Since **December 2019**, the **Léman Express** suburban railway has linked Geneva with the surrounding French countryside. It is meant to move commuters from the car onto the railway. Cross-border commuters are also debated politically: some stress that the economy needs them, while others worry about traffic and wages.

gewusst: The word “frontalieri” comes from “frontiera”, the Italian word for border.
Three countries meet in the Basel region, so cross-border commuters from Germany and France come there.

teile.einleitung: Appenzell Ausserrhoden lies in Eastern Switzerland around Appenzell Innerrhoden. The canton is known for its hilly landscapes, old customs such as the Silvesterchlausen and Appenzeller cheese.
wichtigste: The government and the cantonal council have their seat in Herisau.
In 1597 the land of Appenzell was divided because of religion.
The Protestants formed Ausserrhoden.
In 1997 Ausserrhoden abolished the Landsgemeinde.
In Urnäsch, the Silvesterchläuse go from house to house on New Year's Eve.
In Trogen stands the Pestalozzi Children's Village.
The Säntis lies on the border of the two Appenzells and St Gallen.

abschnitte.text: In the past there was only one **land of Appenzell**. After the Reformation, the **Protestants** and the **Catholics** could not agree. So in **1597** the land was divided. The Protestants formed **Ausserrhoden**, the Catholics **Innerrhoden**. Both Appenzells are completely surrounded by the canton of St Gallen, and Ausserrhoden lies almost all the way round Innerrhoden.

**Herisau** is the largest place in Appenzell Ausserrhoden. The **government** and the **cantonal council** meet there. The court has its seat in Trogen. Until **1997**, the voters met every year for the **Landsgemeinde** in the open air. Then it was abolished, and since then voting has been done at the **ballot box**.

In **Urnäsch** there is a particularly old custom: the **Silvesterchlausen**. The Silvesterchläuse wear splendid costumes and large **bells** and go from house to house. There they sing a **Zäuerli**, a song without words. They come on 31 December and on **13 January**, the old New Year's Eve according to the earlier calendar.

On the border of the two Appenzells and St Gallen lies the **Säntis**. It is 2,502 metres high and the highest mountain in the **Alpstein**. From the Appenzell region comes the savoury **Appenzeller cheese**, which is rubbed with a herbal brine whose recipe is secret. In **Trogen** stands the **Pestalozzi Children's Village**. It was founded in 1946 for children who had lost their homes in the war.

gewusst: Both Appenzell coats of arms show a black bear standing upright; the Ausserrhoden coat of arms also has the letters V and R.
The recipe for the herbal brine for Appenzeller cheese is a closely guarded secret.

teile.einleitung: Wood is an important raw material in Switzerland, because around a third of the country is covered by forest. Wood is used for building and heating. In the mountains, the forest also protects against natural hazards.
wichtigste: Around 5 million cubic metres of wood are harvested from Swiss forests every year.
More wood grows back than is harvested.
After hydropower, wood is the second most important renewable energy.
Since 1876 a law has protected the forest area of Switzerland.
In 1999 Storm Lothar blew down huge amounts of wood.
Around half of the forest is protection forest.

abschnitte.text: Forest owners in Switzerland harvest around **5 million cubic metres** of wood every year. That is less than grows back. As a result, the **stock of wood** is high in many forests. Many forests belong to municipalities, cantons or corporations, and others to private owners. The most common tree in the Swiss forest is the **spruce**.

Wood is a popular **building material** for houses, bridges, furniture and roof frames. Wood is also used as **energy**, mainly for heat. There are heating systems that burn wood chips, pellets and logs. According to the **Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)**, after **hydropower** wood is the second most important renewable energy source in Switzerland.

In **cascading use**, wood is first used as a **material**, for example as timber for building. After that it can still serve for boards or other products. Only at the end is it **burned**. In this way the **carbon** stored in the wood stays locked in for as long as possible. That is good for the climate.

In the 19th century many forests were overused. This was followed by serious floods. So in **1876**, the federal government introduced a **ban on clearing** with the **Forest Police Act**, at first for the mountains. In **1902** it was extended to the whole of Switzerland. Since then the rule has been that the **forest area** must in principle not get smaller. If clearing is allowed as an exception, equivalent replacement has to be created.

Around half of the Swiss forest is **protection forest**. It protects people, villages and roads from **avalanches**, **rockfall** and **landslides**. Storms such as Storm **Lothar** on 26 December 1999 are dangerous for the forest. In one day it blew down around three times a normal year's harvest. The bark beetle known as the **European spruce bark beetle** multiplies in huge numbers after storms and in hot summers and damages weakened spruces.

gewusst: The ban on clearing of 1876 is one of the oldest environmental protection laws in the world.
One cubic metre of wood stores roughly one tonne of carbon dioxide.

teile.einleitung: The national maps show Switzerland in great detail, with mountains, paths, rivers and houses. They are popular with walkers and help with calculating using the scale.
wichtigste: The national maps are published by the Federal Office of Topography swisstopo.
For walks you usually need the scale 1:25,000.
At 1:25,000, 4 cm on the map correspond to 1 km in reality.
Contour lines connect points of the same height.
After the Dufour map, the Siegfried map appeared at scales of 1:25,000 and 1:50,000.
Eduard Imhof became world famous for his artistic relief drawings.

abschnitte.text: The national maps of Switzerland are published by the **Federal Office of Topography swisstopo**. It surveys the country and keeps the maps up to date. The maps exist on paper and digitally, for example in an app. There are different **scales**: for **walks** the most common is **1:25,000**, for larger areas 1:50,000 or 1:100,000.

The **scale** says how much smaller the map is than reality. At **1:25,000**, 1 cm on the map is 25,000 cm in reality, that is 250 m. **4 cm** on the map are therefore **1 km**. At **1:50,000**, 1 cm equals 500 m, so **3 cm** are **1.5 km** in reality. At **1:100,000**, 1 cm corresponds to exactly 1 km. Two places that are **12 km** apart are therefore **12 cm** apart on this map.

A map is flat, but the landscape is not. That is why **contour lines** are drawn in. These are **lines that connect points of the same height**. When the lines are close together, the terrain is **steep**. When they are far apart, it is **flat**. In addition there is shading, which makes the mountains look three dimensional, as if the sun were shining from the top left.

The first accurate map of the whole of Switzerland was the **Dufour map** at a scale of 1:100,000. It was made under General **Guillaume-Henri Dufour** in the 19th century. After that came the **Siegfried map** at scales of **1:25,000** and **1:50,000**. It is named after Hermann Siegfried. Later the present day national maps followed.

The Swiss cartographer **Eduard Imhof** became world famous for his **artistic relief drawing**. He used colours and shadows to show what mountains and valleys look like. His ideas strongly shaped Swiss maps. Swiss national maps are still regarded around the world as especially beautiful and accurate.

gewusst: The Dufourspitze, the highest mountain in Switzerland, is named after General Dufour.
Swisstopo has its headquarters in Wabern near Bern.

teile.einleitung: The Alps did not simply grow upwards. During the formation of the mountains, huge slabs of rock were pushed over one another across long distances. Geologists call such slabs **nappes**.
wichtigste: A nappe is a large package of rock that has been pushed over other rocks.
The Alps arose when Europe and the Adriatic Plate collided.
From bottom to top in Switzerland come the Helvetic, the Penninic and the Austroalpine.
A klippe is an isolated remnant of a nappe, a window is a gap in a nappe.
In 1902 Maurice Lugeon summed up the nappe theory.
The summit of the Matterhorn belongs to the Austroalpine Dent Blanche Nappe.

abschnitte.text: A **nappe** is a slab of rock pushed far over other rocks. During the formation of the mountains large packages of rock broke away from their place of origin. They were pushed over many kilometres onto **foreign rocks**, like tablecloths pulled across a table. That is why in the Alps older rocks often lie above younger ones.

The Alps arose when the **Adriatic Plate**, also called the Apulian Plate, collided with the **European continental margin**. The Adriatic Plate is a spur of Africa. Between the two there used to be an ocean, which disappeared in the process. In front of the growing Alps, **flysch** was deposited in the sea, an alternating sequence of sandstone, marl and clay. Later it was itself overridden by nappes.

In the Swiss Alps three large nappe systems lie on top of one another. At the bottom lies the **Helvetic** with rocks from the European shelf, the shallow sea at the edge of Europe. Above it follows the **Penninic** from the former ocean area. At the top lies the **Austroalpine**, which comes from the Adriatic margin. South of the **Insubric Line** lie the **Southern Alps**, which were hardly pushed northwards at all.

Erosion has eaten into many nappes again. If only a separated remnant is left, lying on younger ground, it is called a **klippe**. If, conversely, a nappe has been worn away in one place so that you can see deeper units, this is called a **tectonic window**. A famous example is the **Tauern Window** in Austria.

The Lausanne geologist **Maurice Lugeon** put forward a comprehensive theory of the nappe structure of the Alps in **1902**. The Zurich geologist **Albert Heim** accepted it in the same year. A fine example is the **Matterhorn**. Its summit pyramid consists of gneisses of the **Dent Blanche Nappe**, which comes from the Adriatic continental margin.

gewusst: Because the summit rocks come from the Adriatic margin, people jokingly speak of the “African” summit of the Matterhorn.
Because of the nappes, older rocks in the Alps often lie above younger ones, that is, the opposite of what you would expect.

teile.einleitung: The **Dufourspitze** is the highest mountain in Switzerland. It lies in the canton of Valais and is the highest summit of the Monte Rosa massif. It bears its name in honour of General Guillaume-Henri Dufour.
wichtigste: At 4,634 metres the Dufourspitze is the highest mountain in Switzerland.
It lies in the canton of Valais, not far from Zermatt.
It is the highest summit in the Monte Rosa massif on the border with Italy.
The summit itself lies entirely in Switzerland.
In the past the summit was simply called the “Highest Peak”.
In 1863 the Federal Council gave it the name Dufourspitze.

abschnitte.text: The **Dufourspitze** is **4,634 metres** high. No summit in Switzerland is higher. It lies in the **canton of Valais**, not far from the holiday resort of **Zermatt**. It is the highest summit in the great mountain massif of **Monte Rosa**. A massif is a group of connected mountains.

The **Monte Rosa massif** lies on the border between Switzerland and **Italy**. Many summits of the massif lie exactly on the border. The summit of the Dufourspitze, however, lies entirely in **Switzerland**, just beside the border. Around the mountain lie large glaciers, for example the Gorner Glacier.

In the past the summit was simply called the **“Highest Peak”**. In **1863** the **Federal Council** decided to name it after **General Guillaume-Henri Dufour** of Geneva. Dufour was an important officer and engineer. He led the work on the first accurate national map of Switzerland, the **Dufour Map**. With the name the Federal Council honoured the general and map-maker.

The Dufourspitze is a goal for experienced **mountaineers**. The route leads over glaciers and rocky ridges. For it you need good equipment, experience and usually a **mountain guide**. Most people spend the night beforehand in the **Monte Rosa Hut**. From the summit you can see far over the Valais and the Italian Alps.

gewusst: The highest mountain in Switzerland is named after a map-maker: General Dufour led the first accurate national map.
Before it received its name in 1863, the summit was quite simply called the “Highest Peak”.

teile.einleitung: Zurich is the canton with the most inhabitants in Switzerland. It lies in the north of the country and has towns and cities, villages, lakes and hills, but no high mountains.
wichtigste: The abbreviation for the canton of Zurich is ZH.
In 2023 around 1.6 million people lived in the canton of Zurich.
In 2023 the canton had around 160 municipalities.
The highest mountain in the canton is the Schnebelhorn.
The largest airport in Switzerland lies in Kloten.
Lake Greifensee lies entirely within the canton of Zurich.
In the north the canton borders Germany.

abschnitte.text: More people live in the canton of Zurich than in any other canton. In 2023 there were around **1.6 million**. The capital is the **city of Zurich**, the largest city in Switzerland. Other large towns are Winterthur and Uster. In 2023 there were around **160 municipalities**. The number plate code and abbreviation are **ZH**.

The largest lake is **Lake Zurich**. But it does not belong only to Zurich, also to the cantons of Schwyz and St Gallen. **Lake Greifensee**, by contrast, lies **entirely within the canton of Zurich**, as does Lake Pfäffikon. The **Limmat** flows through the city of Zurich. In the north the **Rhine** forms the border in many places.

The canton of Zurich lies on the **Central Plateau** and has no high Alpine mountains. The highest point is the **Schnebelhorn** in the Töss Valley, on the border with the canton of St Gallen. It is just under 1,300 metres high. From there you can see as far as the Alps in clear weather.

**Zurich Airport** is the **largest airport in Switzerland**. It lies mostly on the territory of the municipality of **Kloten**. Aircraft fly from here to many countries of the world. Zurich main station is one of the most important railway stations in the country. In the north the canton borders **Germany**.

In the city of Zurich stand **ETH Zurich** and the **University of Zurich**, two large universities. Many banks, insurance companies and other firms have their seat here. Zurich joined the alliance of the Confederates as early as **1351** and is one of the old members of the Confederation.

gewusst: ETH Zurich counts many Nobel Prize winners, including Albert Einstein, who studied there.
Part of the Rhine Falls belongs to the canton of Zurich: Laufen Castle stands on Zurich soil.

teile.einleitung: Lucerne is the capital of the canton of Lucerne and lies on Lake Lucerne, where the Reuss flows out of the lake. With its old wooden bridges, towers and views of the mountains, it is one of the best-known cities in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Lucerne lies on Lake Lucerne, where the Reuss leaves the lake.
The Chapel Bridge and the Spreuer Bridge are covered wooden bridges.
On the Spreuer Bridge hang pictures of a Dance of Death.
The Museggmauer with nine towers once protected the city.
The KKL by the lake was designed by the architect Jean Nouvel.
In the Glacier Garden you can see traces of the Ice Age.
The Lucerne carnival is one of the largest in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The landmark of Lucerne is the **Chapel Bridge** with the octagonal **Water Tower**. It is one of the oldest covered wooden bridges in Europe. In 1993 it was badly damaged in a fire and then rebuilt. Downstream stands the **Spreuer Bridge**. In its roof hang pictures of a **Dance of Death**. They show that death comes to all people, rich or poor.

Above the old town the **Museggmauer** runs across a hill. It dates from the Middle Ages and has **nine towers**. You can climb some of the towers. One of the two main churches is the **Hofkirche St Leodegar** with two pointed towers. It is dedicated to Saint **Leodegar**, the patron saint of Lucerne.

Right on the lakeshore by the station stands the **KKL Luzern**, the culture and congress centre. It was designed by the French architect **Jean Nouvel**. Its large, flat roof juts far out over the water. Many concerts take place in the concert hall, for example at the **Lucerne Festival**. Orchestras from all over the world come to Lucerne for it.

In the **Glacier Garden** you can see large round holes in the rock, the **glacial potholes**. The meltwater of the Ice Age glaciers drilled them into the rock with stones. Very close by, the **Lion Monument** is carved into a rock face. The dying lion recalls the Swiss Guards who lost their lives in Paris in 1792.

Every year Lucerne celebrates a large **carnival**. Then many **Guggenmusik** bands move through the lanes with loud music and colourful costumes. Around Lucerne stand well-known mountains such as **Pilatus** and the **Rigi**. By boat on Lake Lucerne you can reach many places on the lake.

gewusst: The Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne, with trains, aircraft and ships, is one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.
The Water Tower next to the Chapel Bridge is older than the bridge itself.

teile.einleitung: Basel-Landschaft, Baselbiet for short, lies in the north-west of Switzerland around the city of Basel. The canton is known for cherry trees, Jura mountains and the Roman town of Augusta Raurica. The capital is Liestal.
wichtigste: In 1833 the canton of Basel was divided into two cantons.
People often call their canton the Baselbiet.
In Augst you can visit the Roman town of Augusta Raurica.
At the Chienbäse in Liestal, people carry burning bundles of wood.
The Laufental came from the canton of Bern to Basel-Landschaft in 1994.
The largest municipality is Allschwil.
In 2014 Basel-Landschaft clearly rejected a merger with Basel-Stadt.

abschnitte.text: In the past there was only one **canton of Basel**. People in the countryside felt disadvantaged by the city, and there were disputes and fighting. So in **1833** the canton was divided into **Basel-Stadt** and **Basel-Landschaft**. In September **2014**, both cantons voted on whether to examine a merger. Basel-Stadt said yes, but Basel-Landschaft clearly rejected it, and the cantons stayed separate.

The south of Basel-Landschaft is hilly, and these hills and mountains belong to the **Jura**. Through the **Laufental** flows the **Birs**, which joins the Rhine near Basel. The Laufental long belonged to the canton of Bern. After a popular vote it changed to Basel-Landschaft on **1 January 1994**. The largest municipality is **Allschwil**, which borders directly on the city of Basel.

Around 2,000 years ago the Roman town of **Augusta Raurica** stood in **Augst**. Today you can visit a large **theatre**, walls, temple remains and a museum there. A valuable **silver hoard** was also found there. In the Roman house you can see how people lived at the time. Augusta Raurica is one of the most important Roman excavation sites in Switzerland.

In the Baselbiet there are very many **cherry trees**. The cherries are called **Chriesi** there, and in spring whole hills bloom white. In the capital **Liestal** there is the **Chienbäse** at carnival. In it, people carry burning **bundles of wood** through the town, and carts with fire drive through the town gate. A well-known song about the canton is called the **Baselbieterlied**.

gewusst: Basel-Landschaft and Basel-Stadt each have only one seat in the Council of States, because they used to be one canton.
The Roman theatre of Augusta Raurica is among the best preserved north of the Alps.

teile.einleitung: Schaffhausen is the northernmost canton in Switzerland. It lies almost entirely north of the Rhine and is mostly surrounded by Germany. Well known are the Munot, the old town of Stein am Rhein and the Rhine Falls.
wichtigste: The canton consists of three separate parts.
Apart from Germany, it borders only the cantons of Zurich and Thurgau.
The Munot is a round fortress from the 16th century.
Schaffhausen joined the Confederation in 1501.
The former Allerheiligen monastery is now a large museum.
On 1 April 1944 the town of Schaffhausen was bombed by mistake.
Stein am Rhein is known for its painted house fronts.

abschnitte.text: The canton of Schaffhausen consists of **three separate parts**: a large main part, an area around **Stein am Rhein** and an area around **Rüdlingen and Buchberg**. It lies almost entirely north of the **Rhine** and is mostly surrounded by **Germany**. In Switzerland it borders only **Zurich** and **Thurgau**. In Neuhausen am Rheinfall, the Rhine plunges over the **Rhine Falls**, one of the largest waterfalls in Europe.

Above the town of Schaffhausen towers the **Munot**, a round fortress from the **16th century**. It is the town's landmark. In the tower lives a Munot watchman, who rings the little Munot bell every evening. The **Allerheiligen monastery** was founded in the 11th century. Today the **Museum zu Allerheiligen** shows history, art and nature.

In **1501**, Schaffhausen became a member of the **Confederation**, in the same year as Basel. In the Second World War, Switzerland was neutral. Even so, the town of Schaffhausen was **bombed by mistake** by American aircraft on **1 April 1944**. The crews thought they were over Germany. Around 40 people died, and many houses were destroyed.

The little town of **Stein am Rhein** lies where the Rhine flows out of the Untersee. Its old town is famous for **half-timbered houses** and artistically **painted façades**. The pictures show scenes from stories and from history. Many visitors come to stroll through the old lanes. Above the town stands Hohenklingen Castle.

gewusst: In the Munot, a watchman still lives to this day who rings a little bell every evening.
Schaffhausen is the northernmost canton in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Moors are wet landscapes in which peat has formed over thousands of years. In Switzerland the most valuable moors have been protected by the Federal Constitution since 1987, after the people accepted the Rothenthurm Initiative.
wichtigste: In 1987 the people and the cantons accepted the Rothenthurm Initiative, with about 58 per cent yes.
The trigger was a planned army training ground in the Rothenthurm moor.
Moor protection is now in Article 78, paragraph 5 of the Federal Constitution.
Raised bogs are fed only by rain, fens also by groundwater or slope water.
Peat mosses build up the raised bogs, and peat grows only about one millimetre a year.
Intact moors store a lot of carbon.

abschnitte.text: Near **Rothenthurm** in the canton of Schwyz lies a large moorland with the largest raised bog in Switzerland. The **army** wanted to build a **training ground** there. People affected in the area then launched a **popular initiative** with the support of **WWF**. On **6 December 1987** the people and the cantons accepted it with about **58 per cent** yes. Only the cantons of Schwyz, Thurgau and Valais rejected it.

Moor protection is now in **Article 78, paragraph 5** of the Federal Constitution. It says that **moors and moorland** of special beauty and national importance are protected. **No installations may be built** there and no changes may be made to the ground. The Confederation drew up three inventories for this: **raised bogs** in 1991, **fens** in 1994 and **moorland landscapes** in 1996.

A **raised bog** grows up above the groundwater level. It gets its water **only from precipitation**, that is, from rain and snow. That is why it is **low in nutrients** and **acidic**. A **fen**, by contrast, is also fed by mineral rich **groundwater, spring water or slope water**. It is richer in nutrients, and many sedges, grasses and flowers grow there.

Raised bogs are built up mainly by **peat mosses**, in Latin **Sphagnum**. These mosses keep growing at the top while they die off at the bottom. They can store a great deal of water and make their surroundings acidic. The dead plants hardly decompose in the wet ground and become **peat**. It grows only about **one millimetre a year**. A metre of peat therefore takes about **1,000 years**.

In moors live rare plants and animals, for example the carnivorous **sundew** and many dragonflies. Moors are also important **carbon stores**. The carbon of the dead plants stays stored in the peat. If moors are **drained**, the peat dries out and the carbon escapes into the air as **CO2**. That is why people now try to make damaged moors wet again.

gewusst: In the past, a lot of peat was cut in Switzerland and used as fuel, especially in times when coal was scarce.
A large part of Switzerland's former moors has disappeared through drainage and peat extraction.

teile.einleitung: **Emmental cheese** is a cheese from Switzerland that people all over the world recognise by its large holes. It comes from the Emmental in the canton of Bern. A whole wheel is round like a wheel and very heavy.
wichtigste: You recognise Emmental cheese at once by its large, round holes.
It comes from the Emmental in the canton of Bern, the valley of the Emme.
Emmental cheese is made from raw cow’s milk.
A wheel weighs about 75 to 120 kilograms.
The holes arise from gas that bacteria form during ripening.
Young Emmental tastes mild and nutty.

abschnitte.text: Emmental cheese gets its name from the **Emmental**, a hilly area in the **canton of Bern**. The Emmental is the valley of the **Emme**. This river flows through the landscape and later joins the Aare. Today Emmental cheese is made in several regions of Switzerland, but the name recalls its home.

Emmental cheese is made from **raw cow’s milk**. Raw means that the milk is not strongly heated beforehand. The cows eat **grass and hay** for this, but no **silage**. Silage is fermented grass, which could spoil the cheese during ripening. The cheesemaker turns the milk into a wheel in a large vat.

Tiny **bacteria** live in the cheese. While the cheese ripens in the warm cellar, they form a **gas**. The gas cannot escape and collects in single places in the cheese. There the large, round **holes** arise. The firm outer layer, the **rind**, protects the cheese during ripening.

A whole wheel of Emmental cheese is round and flat like a big **wheel**. That is why people also speak of a **cheese wheel**. A wheel weighs about **75 to 120 kilograms**. This makes Emmental cheese one of the largest cheeses in the world. Young Emmental tastes **mild and slightly nutty**, older Emmental tastes stronger.

gewusst: A large wheel of Emmental cheese can be heavier than a grown-up person.
The holes in Emmental cheese are made by bacteria: they form a gas during ripening.

teile.einleitung: The Furka Pass is a high Alpine pass between the cantons of Uri and Valais. It is known for its winding road, the Rhône Glacier and a historic steam railway.
wichtigste: The Furka Pass links the cantons of Uri and Valais.
It lies at about 2,400 metres above sea level.
Right beside the pass lies the Rhône Glacier, where the Rhône rises.
At the eastern foot lies Realp in Uri, to the west the Goms in the Valais.
In summer a steam railway runs over the old mountain line.
In winter a car-carrying train takes vehicles through the tunnel under the Furka.

abschnitte.text: The **Furka Pass** lies at about **2,429 m above sea level** and links the cantons of **Uri** and **Valais**. At the eastern foot lies the Uri village of **Realp**, to the west the Valais valley region of **Goms**. The pass road has many tight bends. In winter it is closed because of snow.

Right beside the pass lies the **Rhône Glacier**. From its meltwater the **Rhône** rises, which flows through the Valais into Lake Geneva and on to France. By the road stands the **Hotel Belvédère** with a view of the glacier. Because the glacier has shrunk a lot, you can see the ice from the hotel much less well today than in the past.

In the past the railway ran over the top of the pass. Since 1982 the trains have gone through the **Furka Base Tunnel**. On the old **mountain line** a historic **steam railway** runs in summer, operated by many volunteers. In winter a **car train** takes cars through the tunnel between Realp and Oberwald.

The Furka Pass is also a film star. In the **James Bond film** “Goldfinger” of 1964 the agent drives a sports car over the pass road. Since then many fans have come to drive the route themselves. Cyclists and motorcyclists love the bends too.

gewusst: The Furka mountain line steam railway uses locomotives, some of which were brought back to Switzerland from Vietnam.
The name Furka means fork, because the pass lies like a fork between two peaks.

teile.einleitung: The region around Zug, where many companies for **blockchain** and **cryptocurrencies** have settled, is called the **Crypto Valley**. The name recalls Silicon Valley in California. Here you can find out how it came about.
wichtigste: The centre of the Crypto Valley is the canton of Zug.
Since about 2014 many blockchain companies have settled there.
The Ethereum Foundation was founded in Zug in 2014.
From 2016 you could pay small fees in the city of Zug with Bitcoin.
Since 2017 the Crypto Valley Association has represented the companies of the region.
In 2021 the DLT Act came into force.

abschnitte.text: A **blockchain** is a kind of digital account book. The entries are not stored in one single place but on many computers at the same time. This is called **distributed ledger technology**, or **DLT** for short. The blockchain is its best-known form. **Cryptocurrencies** such as Bitcoin are based on it.

Since about **2014** many blockchain and crypto companies have settled in the **canton of Zug**. The starting point is considered to be the founding of the **Ethereum Foundation** in Zug in 2014. This foundation supports the development of the Ethereum blockchain. Zug attracted companies with **low taxes**, an **open administration** and its **closeness to the financial centre of Zurich**.

The city of Zug showed early that it is open to new technologies. From **July 2016** you could pay smaller administrative fees with **Bitcoin**. That was one of the first examples in the world of an authority accepting a cryptocurrency. In 2017 the **Crypto Valley Association** was founded. This association links companies, research and authorities.

In an **initial coin offering**, or **ICO** for short, a project sells digital **tokens**, mostly for cryptocurrencies, in order to raise money. Many Zug blockchain projects financed themselves this way around 2017. Because it was new, it was unclear which rules applied. In February 2018 **FINMA**, the Swiss financial market supervisory authority, published a **guide** on it. This created more legal certainty.

The Confederation also adapted the law. In **2021** the so-called **DLT Act** came into force. Its full name is the Federal Act on the Adaptation of Federal Law to Developments in Distributed Ledger Technology. Among other things it created **digital register rights**, that is, securities that are entered on a blockchain. Cryptocurrencies remain risky, however, because their value can fluctuate strongly.

gewusst: Zug was one of the first authorities in the world to accept Bitcoin as a means of payment for fees.
The name Crypto Valley is an allusion to the famous Silicon Valley in the USA.

teile.einleitung: A border river is a river along which a border runs. Switzerland has many such rivers, above all the Rhine in the north, which forms the border with Germany over long stretches.
wichtigste: With a border river, the two banks lie in different countries or cantons.
The border usually runs down the middle of the river.
Between Lake Constance and Basel, the High Rhine largely forms the border with Germany.
There are many river power stations on the High Rhine, often run jointly by both countries.
In the west of the canton of Geneva, the Rhône forms a stretch of the border with France.
Ponte Tresa lies on the Tresa on the border with Italy.

abschnitte.text: A **border river** separates two countries, cantons or municipalities from each other. One **bank** belongs to one area, the other bank to the other. The border usually runs down the **middle of the river**. Rivers work well as borders because they are easy to recognise. In the past they were also hard to cross.

The **High Rhine** flows from the Untersee near **Stein am Rhein** to **Basel**. Over long stretches it forms the border between Switzerland and **Germany**. In several places **river power stations** stand right across the river, for example near **Rheinfelden**. Because the border runs through the water, such power stations often belong to both countries together.

On some border rivers, two places lie directly opposite each other. There are two **Laufenburgs**: Laufenburg in Aargau and Laufenburg in Baden on the German side. A bridge links the two. On the **Tresa** in Ticino, too, the Swiss **Ponte Tresa** and the Italian **Lavena Ponte Tresa** face each other. A border crossing leads over the bridge.

abschnitte.titel: The Rhône and other border rivers
abschnitte.text: Shortly before the **Rhône** leaves Switzerland, it forms the border with **France** in the west of the canton of Geneva. The joint power station **Chancy-Pougny** stands there. In the Jura, the **Doubs** forms a stretch of the border with France. In the east, the **Alpine Rhine** separates Switzerland from Liechtenstein and Austria.

abschnitte.titel: The Rhine Falls are not a border
abschnitte.text: Although the Rhine often forms the border in the Schaffhausen region, the **Rhine Falls** are not a border waterfall. On one bank lies **Neuhausen** in the canton of Schaffhausen, on the other **Laufen-Uhwiesen** in the canton of Zurich. So both banks belong to Switzerland. There, however, the Rhine is a **cantonal border**.

gewusst: The canton of Schaffhausen lies mostly north of the Rhine and is almost completely surrounded by Germany.
Cantons have border rivers too: at the Rhine Falls the Rhine separates Schaffhausen and Zurich.

teile.einleitung: A debris flow is a fast stream of water, mud and stones that shoots down a steep stream. In the Alps, debris flows are among the most dangerous natural hazards, and in Switzerland they are closely monitored.
wichtigste: Debris flows are most often triggered by heavy rainfall.
Water and rock flow as a dense mixture, which is why a debris flow can sweep along huge boulders.
The front, boulder rich part is called the debris flow head.
In the Grisons and eastern Switzerland a debris flow is often called a Rüfe.
The Illgraben in the Valais is one of the most active debris flow streams in the Alps.
Debris traps catch stones and rubble in front of villages.
Thawing permafrost makes debris flows more likely.

abschnitte.text: In steep gullies there is often a lot of **loose material**: stones, gravel and sand. In **heavy rain** or thunderstorms it becomes soaked and suddenly starts to slide. Strong **snowmelt** can also trigger a debris flow. The mixture of water, mud and stones then shoots down the valley at great speed. In the **Grisons** and eastern Switzerland, people often call this a **Rüfe**.

In an ordinary flood, stones only roll along the bottom, which is called **bedload transport**. In a **debris flow**, by contrast, water and solids flow **as one mixture**. This slurry is much **denser and heavier** than pure water. That is why it can even carry house sized boulders. At the front, the largest boulders gather in the **debris flow head**, which is especially destructive. Behind it follows a more liquid part.

Where a mountain torrent comes out of a narrow valley into the flat main valley, it deposits its rubble in a **fan shape**. This creates an **alluvial fan**. Because these fans lie slightly raised and dry, many mountain villages stand on them. In a debris flow, however, they are especially at risk. In August **2005** a debris flow from the **Glyssibach** hit the village of **Brienz** on Lake Brienz and destroyed several houses. Two people lost their lives.

The **Illgraben** near Leuk in the Valais is regarded as one of the most active debris flow streams in the Alps. Almost every year several debris flows come down into the **Rhône** there. Researchers have installed many **measuring instruments** at the Illgraben. They measure the speed, height and weight of the debris flows. In this way people learn how debris flows work and how to warn earlier.

To protect villages, **debris traps** are built. These are large basins that hold back stones and mud while the water flows on. After an event they have to be dredged out. In the high mountains, **permafrost**, that is, permanently frozen ground, is thawing because of **global warming**. It holds debris together. When it thaws, the material becomes loose, and debris flows become more likely.

gewusst: In 2017 a rockslide on Piz Cengalo and the debris flows that followed caused great damage in the village of Bondo in the Bregaglia.
Many place and field names in the Grisons recall earlier debris flows with the word Rüfe.

teile.einleitung: Appenzell Innerrhoden is the canton with the fewest inhabitants in Switzerland. It lies in Eastern Switzerland at the foot of the Alpstein and is famous for its customs, its Landsgemeinde and its mountain scenery.
wichtigste: The capital has the same name as the canton, namely Appenzell.
In 2023 only about 16,000 people lived in the canton.
The Landsgemeinde takes place on the last Sunday in April.
The Äscher mountain inn clings to a rock face in the Alpstein.
In the Wildkirchli there is a small chapel in a cave.
The Appenzeller Biber is a gingerbread with an almond filling.

abschnitte.text: Appenzell Innerrhoden came into being in 1597, when the land of Appenzell was divided because of religion. The **Catholics** formed Innerrhoden. In 2023, only about **16,000 people** lived in the canton, fewer than in any other canton. The capital is called **Appenzell**. It has a colourful **main street** with painted houses.

On the **last Sunday in April**, the voters gather on the **Landsgemeindeplatz** in Appenzell. There they elect the government and vote on laws, by **show of hands**. This form of democracy is very old. At the Landsgemeinde, many men wear a rapier or sabre as a sign that they are entitled to vote.

In the south of the canton lies the **Alpstein** mountain range. Below the Ebenalp stands the **Äscher** mountain inn, built tight against a steep rock face. Photographs made it known all over the world. Very close by is the **Wildkirchli**. It consists of caves in which a small **chapel** stands. Bones of **cave bears** were also found there.

For festive dress, the Appenzell **Sennen** (herdsmen) wear **yellow leather breeches** and a red waistcoat, for example at the alpine procession. Also typical is the **Streichmusik** with fiddles, bass and **hammered dulcimer** (Hackbrett). The dulcimer is played by striking strings with small mallets. A sweet speciality is the **Appenzeller Biber**, a gingerbread with an almond filling, often with a picture pressed into it.

gewusst: Appenzell Innerrhoden only introduced women's right to vote in 1990, after a ruling by the Federal Supreme Court.
In caves in the Alpstein, bones of cave bears were found that lived a very long time ago.

teile.einleitung: The Grossmünster is one of the best-known churches in Switzerland. With its two towers it is a landmark of Zurich. This is where Huldrych Zwingli began the Reformation in Zurich.
wichtigste: The Grossmünster has two identical towers.
It was built from about 1100 to 1220.
According to a legend, Charlemagne founded the church.
It stands above the graves of the city's patron saints Felix and Regula.
Huldrych Zwingli preached in the Grossmünster from 1519.
Today it is a Protestant Reformed church.

abschnitte.text: The **Grossmünster** stands in the old town of Zurich on the bank of the **Limmat**. Its **two towers** can be seen from far away. Building began around **1100**, and the church was finished around **1220**. It is built in the **Romanesque style**, with thick walls and round arches. On the other side of the Limmat stands the Fraumünster.

A **legend** tells how the Grossmünster came to be. Emperor **Charlemagne** is said to have followed a **stag** to Zurich while out hunting. There he found the graves of **Felix and Regula**. The two are the **patron saints** of Zurich. He had a church built over their graves. That is why a figure of Charlemagne sits on the south tower.

**Huldrych Zwingli** came to the Grossmünster as a priest in **1519**. He preached that the church should be guided by the **Bible**. From here he changed the church in Zurich. This renewal is called the **Reformation**. Since then the Grossmünster has been a **Protestant Reformed** church. It belongs to the Reformed Church of the canton of Zurich.

The Grossmünster has some special works of art. In **1933**, the artist **Augusto Giacometti** from the Grisons made three choir windows showing the **Christmas story**. In 2009, windows by the artist Sigmar Polke were added, some of them made from thinly sliced stones. In **1950**, **Otto Münch** made a large **bronze** door with scenes from the Bible.

You can climb one of the towers: the south tower, also called the **Karlsturm**. **187 steps** lead up. At the top there is a fine view over the old town, the Limmat and Lake Zurich. In good weather you can even see the Alps.

gewusst: The original figure of Charlemagne from the tower now stands protected in the crypt.
Thanks to Zwingli, Zurich was, alongside Geneva, one of the most important centres of the Reformation.

teile.einleitung: The Folded Jura is the part of the Jura Mountains in which the layers of rock were pushed together like a tablecloth. In this way long, parallel mountain ridges and valleys arose in the north-west of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Folded Jura arose when layers of rock were pushed together.
The thrust came from the formation of the Alps and was transmitted underneath the Central Plateau.
The layers slid on soft layers of salt and anhydrite from the Triassic.
Upward-arching folds are called anticlines, the troughs between them synclines.
A Klus is a transverse valley through which a river breaks through a ridge.
At 1,607 m the Chasseral is the highest summit of the Bernese Jura.

abschnitte.text: If you push a tablecloth together on a table, waves appear. Something similar happened to the **limestone layers** of the Jura. The pressure of the **formation of the Alps** was passed on underneath the Central Plateau as far as the Jura. This is called **long-distance thrust**. In this way the layers folded into long ridges.

Under the limestone layers lie soft **layers of salt and anhydrite** from the **Triassic**, a geological period over 200 million years ago. They worked like a lubricant. On them the whole stack of rock could slide off and fold into waves. The base underneath was hardly folded along with it.

A fold arching upwards is called an **anticline**, or vault. It forms a mountain ridge. The troughs between them are called **synclines** and form the longitudinal valleys. If erosion has broken open the crest of a vault and cleared out the soft core, a **combe** arises.

Some rivers break right across a Jura ridge. Such a narrow transverse valley is called a **Klus** (plural **Klusen**). Well-known examples are near **Balsthal** and **Moutier**. Klusen are important transport routes, because roads and railways can cross the ridges there.

The **Chasseral** at 1,607 m above sea level is the highest summit of the Bernese Jura. It lies between Lake Biel and the Vallon de Saint-Imier. The **Val de Travers** in the Neuchâtel Jura is regarded as the home of **absinthe**, a herbal spirit that was first made there at the end of the 18th century.

gewusst: The word Klus comes from the Latin clausa, which means roughly “closed place”.
The name Jura stands worldwide for a whole geological period, the Jurassic, named after this mountain range.

teile.einleitung: The **Creux du Van** is a huge rock amphitheatre in the Neuchâtel Jura. Its steep limestone cliffs form a semicircle and are among the best-known natural wonders of Switzerland. At the top, on the rim, there is a wide view.
wichtigste: The Creux du Van lies above the Val de Travers in the canton of Neuchâtel.
The rock walls fall about 160 metres vertically.
The rock circle is around 4 kilometres long in total.
The amphitheatre probably formed after the last cold period through erosion.
The spring Fontaine Froide has water of about 4 °C all year round.
Ibex and chamois live in the rocks.
The area has been protected since 1972.

abschnitte.text: The **limestone cliffs** of the Creux du Van fall about **160 metres** vertically. Together they form a semicircle around **4 kilometres** long. The amphitheatre is about 1,200 metres wide and 500 metres deep. It lies above the **Val de Travers**, near the border with the canton of Vaud. From **Noiraigue** a steep walking path leads up.

According to present views, the rock amphitheatre probably formed after the **Würm glaciation**, the last great cold period. **Erosion** means that rock is slowly worn away. At the Creux du Van it was above all **frost** and **water** that broke the rock up and carried it away. In this way the great circle came about over time.

Down in the shady amphitheatre lies the spring **Fontaine Froide**. The name means “cold fountain”. Its water is an even **4 °C** cold all year round. In the amphitheatre it is often much cooler than in the surroundings. That is why plants also grow there that otherwise occur more at higher altitudes.

In the rock walls you often see **ibex** and **chamois**. They are skilful climbers and find shelter on the rock ledges. Often they can be watched from close up. In **1974 and 1975** a pair of **lynx** from the Slovak Carpathians was released in each of two years in the region. In this way the lynx was meant to return to the Jura.

Since **1972** the area of the Creux du Van has been under **protection**. It also belongs to the **Federal Inventory of Landscapes** of national importance. Visitors should stay on the paths and not disturb the animals. At the edge of the cliffs care is important, because there is not a railing everywhere.

gewusst: The rock walls of the Creux du Van are about as high as a tower block with around 50 floors.
The spring Fontaine Froide stays only about 4 °C cold even in the hottest summer.

teile.einleitung: The CH2018 climate scenarios show how the climate of Switzerland could change in the future. They were drawn up by the Confederation together with universities and were replaced by new scenarios in 2025.
wichtigste: The CH2018 climate scenarios were published by the National Centre for Climate Services (NCCS) of the Confederation.
The four key messages are: drier summers, heavier rainfall, more hot days and snow poor winters.
Without climate protection, the zero degree line in winter could rise from around 850 m to up to 1,500 m.
The RCP8.5 scenario stands for a future without climate protection.
In November 2025 the CH2018 scenarios were replaced by the CH2025 climate scenarios.
According to the 2025 climate scenarios, Switzerland had warmed by around 2.9 °C by 2024.

abschnitte.text: A **climate scenario** describes how the climate could develop. For this, researchers use **climate models** to calculate different possibilities. The **CH2018** scenarios were published by the **National Centre for Climate Services (NCCS)**. This is a network of the Confederation in which MeteoSwiss and universities such as ETH Zurich take part. Municipalities, cantons and firms use such scenarios to prepare for the future climate.

CH2018 calculates with different **emission scenarios**. They show how many greenhouse gases people will emit in the future. The **RCP8.5** scenario stands for a future **without climate protection measures**, in which emissions keep rising. Another scenario shows what happens if the world cuts emissions sharply. Then the changes are much smaller.

CH2018 sums up its results in **four key messages**: **drier summers**, **heavier rainfall**, **more hot days** and **snow poor winters**. Average summer rainfall tends to decrease in the long term. Without climate protection, the hottest summer days could be 2 to 5.5 °C warmer by the middle of the century. The wettest day of the year would bring around 10 per cent more rain by then.

The **zero degree line** is the height above which it is colder than 0 degrees. In winter it currently lies on average at around **850 metres**. Without climate protection it could rise to up to **1,500 metres**, according to CH2018. Then rain instead of snow would fall much more often at lower altitudes. This affects, for example, ski areas at middle heights.

In **November 2025** the CH2018 scenarios were replaced by the **CH2025 climate scenarios**. They are based on newer measurements and models. According to CH2025, Switzerland had already warmed by around **2.9 °C** by 2024 compared with pre-industrial times. That is about twice as much as the worldwide average.

gewusst: Air warms faster over land than over the oceans, which is why the warming in Switzerland is greater than the worldwide average.
Climate scenarios are not weather forecasts but show possible developments over decades.

teile.einleitung: Every country has points that lie furthest north, south, west and east. In addition there are the highest and the lowest point. They are called the extreme points of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The northernmost point lies near Bargen in the canton of Schaffhausen.
The southernmost point lies near Pedrinate, a part of Chiasso in Ticino.
The westernmost point lies near Chancy in the canton of Geneva.
The easternmost point lies on the Piz Chavalatsch in the Val Müstair in Graubünden.
The highest point is the Dufourspitze at 4,634 m, the lowest is Lake Maggiore at 193 m.
The difference in height is about 4,440 metres.

abschnitte.text: The northernmost point of Switzerland lies near **Oberbargen** in the municipality of **Bargen** in the canton of **Schaffhausen**. Schaffhausen lies north of the Rhine and is almost completely surrounded by Germany. There you are already further north than in many parts of southern Germany.
The southernmost point lies near **Pedrinate**, a part of **Chiasso** in the canton of **Ticino**. Italy begins right behind it. In the south of Ticino the climate is mild, and even palm trees grow.

Right in the west lies the Geneva municipality of **Chancy** on the Rhône, surrounded by France. Right in the east lies the **Piz Chavalatsch** in the municipality of **Val Müstair** in the canton of Graubünden, on the border with Italy. Between these two points there are about 350 kilometres as the crow flies.

abschnitte.titel: Right at the top and right at the bottom
abschnitte.text: The highest point is the **Dufourspitze** in the Monte Rosa massif in the Valais at **4,634 m above sea level**. The lowest point is the surface of **Lake Maggiore** in Ticino at about **193 m above sea level**. If you subtract the two numbers from each other, you get a difference of about **4,441 metres**. So in a small space there are huge differences in height.

gewusst: From Lake Maggiore with its palm trees to the glaciers of the Dufourspitze it is only a good 100 kilometres as the crow flies.
All four extreme points in the compass directions lie directly on the national border.

teile.einleitung: Flooding occurs when a river or lake carries much more water than normal. In Switzerland, floods are one of the most important natural hazards. People try to protect themselves with hazard maps and by giving rivers more room.
wichtigste: The flood of August 2005 was the most expensive natural event of recent decades.
The damage at that time was around 3 billion francs.
The Matte district of Bern was flooded in 1999 and 2005.
Hazard maps show where natural hazards threaten.
Red means considerable, blue medium and yellow low danger.
A gauge measures the water level.

abschnitte.text: Flooding usually happens after **heavy or prolonged rain**. **Snowmelt** can also make rivers swell greatly. When the ground can no longer absorb the water, it flows straight into streams and rivers. These then burst their **banks**. In the mountains, **debris flows** can also occur, that is, streams of water, mud and stones.

In **August 2005** it rained very heavily for days on the north side of the Alps. The damage was around **3 billion francs**. This makes it the most expensive natural event in Switzerland in recent decades. In **Bern**, the low-lying **Matte** district on the Aare was under water in 1999 and 2005. At the end of June **2024**, severe storms hit the **Maggia Valley** in Ticino, especially the Val Bavona. Several people died.

A **gauge** measures the **water level** of a river or lake. If the gauge rises quickly, a flood may be on the way. A **hundred-year flood** is a flood that occurs on average about **once every 100 years**. This describes a **probability**. Such a flood can therefore also come twice in quick succession.

A **hazard map** uses colours to show where natural hazards such as flooding, avalanches or landslides threaten. **Red** stands for considerable danger. There, building is usually not allowed. **Blue** means medium and **yellow** low danger. Municipalities and cantons use these maps when planning where building is allowed.

In the past, many rivers were straightened and squeezed into narrow channels. Today, **flood protection** often gives them **more room** again. A wide river bed takes in a lot of water, and the flood flows more slowly. This also creates valuable **habitats** for plants and animals. In addition there are dams, retention basins and warning systems.

gewusst: Even a hundred-year flood can occur two years in a row.
In Bern you can see markings on house walls in the Matte showing how high the water stood.

teile.einleitung: The Great St Bernard is a high pass in Lower Valais on the border with Italy. It is famous for its old hospice and for the St Bernard dogs that helped travellers there.
wichtigste: The Great St Bernard links the Valais with the Aosta Valley in Italy.
The top of the pass is at around 2,469 metres above sea level.
The pass is named after Bernard of Aosta.
Canons, a kind of monk, live in the hospice.
Napoleon crossed the pass with his army in May 1800.
Since 1964 there has been a road tunnel that is open all year round.

abschnitte.text: The **Great St Bernard** lies in **Lower Valais**. The top of the pass is at around **2,469 metres** above sea level. From there the road leads down into the **Aosta Valley** in **Italy**. At the top of the pass there is a small **mountain lake**. The border with Italy runs very close by. It is often cold and windy up there, even in summer.

In the **11th century**, Saint **Bernard of Aosta** founded a **hospice** on the pass. A hospice is a building where travellers find shelter, food and a place to sleep. The pass is named after Bernard. For almost 1,000 years, **canons**, a kind of monk, have lived there. They still take in guests today.

The monks kept large, strong dogs. The dogs helped to find paths in the snow and to track down travellers who had lost their way. They are called **St Bernards** after the hospice. The most famous was **Barry**. He is said to have saved over 40 people. Today you can see him in the **Natural History Museum in Bern**. A foundation in Martigny continues to breed the dogs.

In May **1800**, **Napoleon Bonaparte** crossed the Great St Bernard with a very large number of soldiers. He wanted to march into **Italy**. The soldiers even had to drag cannons over the snowy pass. A famous painting shows Napoleon on a rearing horse, but in reality he rode a mule.

In winter there is a lot of snow on the pass, so the pass road is closed. Anyone who then wants to drive from the Valais to Italy goes through the **road tunnel**. It has been there since **1964**. It is around 6 kilometres long and open **all year round**.

gewusst: In reality the St Bernards did not wear a little barrel around their necks; that is an invention of painters.
Barry lived on the pass around the year 1800.

teile.einleitung: Lausanne is the capital of the canton of Vaud and lies on a steep slope above Lake Geneva. The city is known around the world as the Olympic Capital.
wichtigste: The International Olympic Committee has its headquarters in Lausanne.
Lausanne has the nickname “Olympic Capital”.
In the Olympic Museum you can see torches and medals from the Games.
The Federal Supreme Court has its seat in Lausanne.
The city is very hilly, so a metro runs uphill under the city.
The Ouchy district lies directly on the lakeshore.
The tower watchman of Notre-Dame Cathedral calls out the hours every night.

abschnitte.text: **Lausanne** lies on the north shore of **Lake Geneva** and is the capital of the canton of Vaud. The city's landscape is **very hilly**: from the lakeshore to the upper districts it is a steep climb. That is why a **metro** runs **uphill** under the city and links the lake with the centre and the station. Down at the lake lies the **Ouchy** district with its harbour and a lakeside promenade.

The **International Olympic Committee** has its headquarters in Lausanne. It organises the Olympic Games. That is why Lausanne is called the **“Olympic Capital”**. In Ouchy stands the **Olympic Museum**. There you can see torches, medals and many other things from the history of the Games. Many other international sports federations also have their seats in the region.

The Gothic **Notre-Dame** Cathedral is one of the most important buildings of the Middle Ages in Switzerland. High up in the tower lives a **tower watchman**. Every night he **calls out the hours**, from late evening until after midnight. In the past he was meant to warn of fires in the city. Today it is a fine old tradition.

The **Federal Supreme Court** stands in Lausanne. It is the highest court in Switzerland. There are also large universities here: **EPFL**, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, and the University of Lausanne. They lie side by side on the lakeshore. Thousands of students from many countries learn and do research here.

gewusst: The M2 metro in Lausanne is regarded as one of the steepest metros in the world.
The International Olympic Committee moved to Lausanne in 1915.

teile.einleitung: Geneva lies in the far south-west of Switzerland at the end of Lake Geneva. The city is famous as the home of many international organisations, as a centre of the Reformation and as the birthplace of the Red Cross.
wichtigste: Geneva lies at the south-western end of Lake Geneva.
In Geneva the Rhône flows out of Lake Geneva towards France.
The canton is almost completely surrounded by France.
The Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863.
