Geneva has been a canton of the Confederation since 1815.
John Calvin made Geneva a centre of the Reformation.
In December Geneva celebrates the Escalade.

abschnitte.titel: At the end of the lake
abschnitte.text: Geneva lies at the **south-western end of Lake Geneva**. Here the **Rhône** leaves the lake and flows on to **France**. The canton is almost completely surrounded by France, with only a small stretch bordering the canton of **Vaud**. In the lake stands the **Jet d'eau**, a tall fountain that is a landmark of the city. French is spoken in Geneva.

In the 16th century the reformer **John Calvin** worked in Geneva. He made the city a centre of the **Reformation**, which is why Geneva was also called the “Protestant Rome”. In the **Parc des Bastions** by the university stands the **Reformation Wall**, a long wall with large statues. It was unveiled in 1909 for the 400th anniversary of Calvin's birth.

The Genevan **Henry Dunant** founded the **Red Cross** in 1863 with others. It helps the wounded and people in need all over the world. Today many **international organisations** have their seat in Geneva, for example a large seat of the **UN**. That is why politicians from many countries often meet in Geneva. In **1815** Geneva joined the Confederation as a canton.

abschnitte.titel: Escalade, clock and coat of arms
abschnitte.text: In December Geneva celebrates the **Escalade**. It commemorates the year **1602**, when the city repelled a night-time attack. At the festival, a **soup pot made of chocolate** is smashed. In the **English Garden** stands a **flower clock**, whose dial is made of thousands of flowers. The Geneva **coat of arms** shows a **half eagle** on the left and a **key** on the right.

gewusst: At the Escalade, a pot made of chocolate and filled with marzipan vegetables is smashed.
The canton of Geneva is almost completely surrounded by France.

teile.einleitung: The Grande Dixence is a huge dam in the canton of Valais. It is the tallest gravity dam in the world and holds back the Lac des Dix, the largest reservoir in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Grande Dixence stands in the Val d'Hérémence in the canton of Valais.
The dam is 285 metres high.
It is the tallest gravity dam in the world.
Behind the wall lies the Lac des Dix, about 5 kilometres long.
The lake holds around 400 million cubic metres of water.
Most of the water is meltwater from glaciers.

abschnitte.text: The **Grande Dixence** is **285 metres** high. That is almost as tall as the Eiffel Tower in Paris. More than **6 million cubic metres of concrete** went into the wall. It weighs about **15 million tonnes**. It was built in the 1950s, and over 3,000 workers were involved. It stands high up in the **Val d'Hérémence**, a side valley in the Valais.

There are different kinds of dam. An **arch dam** is curved and pushes the force of the water sideways into the rocks. A **gravity dam**, by contrast, holds back the water with its own enormous **weight**. That is why it is very thick at the bottom. No other gravity dam in the world is as tall as the Grande Dixence.

Behind the wall lies the **Lac des Dix**. “Dix” is the name of the valley and here does not mean the number ten. The lake is about **5 kilometres** long. When it is full, its water level is at around **2,364 metres** above sea level. It holds around **400 million cubic metres** of water, more than any other reservoir in Switzerland.

Most of the water comes from **glaciers**. In summer a lot of ice melts in the mountains around the valley. The **meltwater** is collected and led into the lake through long tunnels. In summer the lake fills, and in winter the water is used. That is when Switzerland needs particularly large amounts of electricity.

The water from the Lac des Dix flows through pipes and tunnels down to **power stations** in the Rhône Valley. There it drives **turbines** that generate electricity. Because the water falls a very long way, it produces a lot of power. **Hydropower** is the most important source of electricity in Switzerland. Visitors can look round the wall in summer.

gewusst: At 285 metres, the Grande Dixence is the tallest structure in Switzerland.
In summer you can walk through passages inside the dam.

teile.einleitung: The Morteratsch Glacier lies in the Upper Engadine in the canton of the Grisons. It flows north from the Bernina group and is easy to reach on foot. On the glacier trail you can clearly see how much it has retreated.
wichtigste: The Morteratsch Glacier lies in the Upper Engadine in the Grisons.
It comes from the Bernina group, the highest mountain range in the Eastern Alps.
Above its accumulation area stands Piz Bernina, 4,049 metres high.
The Bernina Railway has a Morteratsch station in front of the glacier.
From 1878 to 2015 it became about 2.6 kilometres shorter.
In 2015 it separated from the Pers Glacier and was still about 6 kilometres long.

abschnitte.text: The **Morteratsch Glacier** flows from the **Bernina group** in the south of the Upper Engadine north into the valley. The Bernina group is the **highest mountain range in the Eastern Alps**. Above the glacier's **accumulation area**, where snow is compressed into ice, rises **Piz Bernina**. It is **4,049 metres** high and the only four thousander in the Eastern Alps.

The **Bernina Railway** from St Moritz to Tirano has a **Morteratsch station**. It lies in the valley in front of the glacier. At the last great high point in **1857**, the ice reached to within about 100 metres of this spot. Today you have to walk quite a while from the station before you reach the ice.

From the station a **glacier trail** leads to the glacier tongue. Along the path there are **signs with years on them**. They show how far the ice reached in which year. In this way you walk through time, as it were, and see with your own eyes how far the glacier has **retreated**. Where ice used to lie, plants and small trees are already growing again.

From the start of measurements in **1878** to **2015**, the tongue retreated by about **2.6 kilometres**. That is on average about 17 metres a year. In the past, the Morteratsch Glacier was joined to the **Pers Glacier**. In the hot summer of **2015** the connection broke, and since then they have been two separate glaciers. At that time the Morteratsch Glacier was still about **6 kilometres** long. The reason for the retreat is above all **global warming**.

gewusst: The Morteratsch Glacier is one of the most easily reached large glaciers in Switzerland.
Its length has been measured regularly since 1878, which is one of the long measurement series in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Lake Lugano lies in the south of Ticino between high mountains. It is narrow, has several arms and belongs partly to Switzerland and partly to Italy.
wichtigste: Switzerland shares Lake Lugano with Italy.
The Swiss part lies in the canton of Ticino.
An old name of the lake is Ceresio.
The lake is about 49 square kilometres in size.
At Melide a causeway for road and railway crosses the lake.
The Italian village of Campione d'Italia lies on the shore, surrounded by Swiss territory.
Scheduled boats connect Lugano with villages such as Morcote and Gandria.

abschnitte.text: Lake Lugano is **long, narrow and branching**. It has several arms that push in between the mountains. Its area is about **49 square kilometres**. The larger part lies in the canton of **Ticino**, a smaller part in **Italy**. The people of Ticino also call it **Ceresio**. The lake drains via the **Tresa** into Lake Maggiore.

At **Melide** the lake is especially narrow. There a **causeway** runs across the water. On it run the A2 motorway, a road and the railway line towards **Chiasso** and Italy. The causeway divides the lake into a northern and a southern part. Without it, cars and trains would have to make a long detour around the lake.

On the shore of Lake Lugano lies the village of **Campione d'Italia**. It belongs to **Italy** but is completely surrounded by Swiss territory. Something like this is called an **exclave**. Anyone who wants to get to Campione from Italy has to travel through Switzerland.

Pretty villages lie all around the lake. **Morcote** at the southern end is known for its lanes and its many **steps**. **Gandria** east of Lugano is an old fishing village on the slope, close to the border with Italy. **Scheduled boats** run between the places. Above the lake rise viewing mountains such as **Monte San Salvatore** and **Monte Brè**.

gewusst: On Monte San Giorgio, between two arms of Lake Lugano, famous fossils of marine reptiles were found.
The marine reptile Ceresiosaurus is named after the old name of Lake Lugano.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Bern stretches from the Jura across the Central Plateau to the Alps. By area it is the second largest canton in Switzerland, and in its capital Bern sit the Federal Council and Parliament.
wichtigste: By area, only the Grisons is larger than Bern.
Around 1.06 million people live in the canton of Bern (as of the end of 2023); only Zurich has more.
Bern joined the Confederation in 1353.
The Bernese coat of arms shows a black bear on red and yellow.
In the old town of Bern stand many old fountains with colourful figures.
The local mountain of the city of Bern is called the Gurten.

abschnitte.titel: From the Jura to the Alps
abschnitte.text: The canton of Bern is very varied. In the north lies part of the **Jura**, in the middle the **Central Plateau** and in the south the **Bernese Oberland** with high mountains. By area only the **Grisons** is larger. Around **1.06 million** people live in the canton of Bern (as of the end of 2023), which puts it in **second place** after Zurich. German is spoken, and in the Bernese Jura and in Biel French as well.

In **1353**, Bern concluded an alliance with **Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden** and so became part of the Confederation. The heraldic animal is the **bear**. The Bernese coat of arms is **red**, with a **yellow** stripe on which the black bear walks. The city of Bern is today the **federal city** of Switzerland. The Federal Council and Parliament meet there in the **Federal Palace**.

The **old town of Bern** is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It has long arcades and many **fountains** that are over 450 years old. On their columns stand **brightly painted figures**. On the edge of the city stands the **Zentrum Paul Klee**, a museum for the painter Paul Klee, whose roofs look like three waves of hills. A funicular railway goes up the **Gurten**, the city's local mountain.

In summer, many people in Bern jump into the **Aare** and let the current carry them downstream. The **Bernese mountain dog**, with its black, white and brown coat, comes from the canton. In the past it helped farmers and pulled small **milk carts**. Also typical of Bern is the **Berner Platte**, with many kinds of meat and sausage, served with sauerkraut, beans and potatoes.

gewusst: Switzerland officially has no capital. Bern is called the “federal city”.
In the Bear Park by the Aare in Bern, real bears live in the middle of the city.

teile.einleitung: MeteoSwiss is the official weather and climate service of Switzerland. The federal office makes weather forecasts, warns of storms and observes how the climate is changing.
wichtigste: MeteoSwiss is the Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology.
It belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs.
The headquarters are at Zurich Airport.
Other sites are Geneva, Payerne and Locarno-Monti.
Weather warnings come in five danger levels.
Five weather radars cover the whole of Switzerland.
The state weather service has existed since 1881.

abschnitte.text: **MeteoSwiss** is officially called the **Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology**. Meteorology is the study of weather, climatology the study of climate. The office makes **weather forecasts**, issues **warnings** and collects measurement data over many years. It belongs to the **Federal Department of Home Affairs** (FDHA). The **headquarters** are at **Zurich Airport**, and other sites are Geneva, Payerne and Locarno-Monti.

In the case of storms, thunderstorms, heavy rain, snow or heat, MeteoSwiss warns the public. The warnings have **five danger levels**. Level 1 means no or little danger, level 5 very great danger. The colours range from **green** to **dark red**. This way everyone can quickly see how serious the situation is.

MeteoSwiss operates **five weather radars**. They stand on the **Albis**, on **La Dôle**, on **Monte Lema**, on the **Pointe de la Plaine Morte** and on the **Weissfluhgipfel**. Together they detect rain and snow across the whole country. In **Payerne**, **weather balloons** carrying measuring instruments, the **radiosondes**, are launched regularly. They measure temperature, humidity and wind up to great heights.

As early as **1881**, the **Central Meteorological Institute** began its work. From it came today's weather service, which has been called **MeteoSwiss** since 1996. Weather does not respect borders, so the weather services of many countries work together. The **World Meteorological Organization** (WMO) is a UN organisation based in **Geneva**. MeteoSwiss represents Switzerland there.

gewusst: Some temperature records in Switzerland go back over 150 years and clearly show that it has become warmer.
You can also call up the MeteoSwiss forecasts in an app on your phone, together with warnings.

teile.einleitung: The geographical centre of Switzerland lies on the Älggi Alp above Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden. It was calculated in 1988 by the Federal Office of Topography.
wichtigste: The centre was calculated in 1988.
The occasion was the 150th anniversary of the Federal Office of Topography.
It was determined as the centre of gravity of the country's area.
It lies in the Alps, in the municipality of Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden.
The memorial stone stands at around 1,650 m above sea level on the Älggi Alp.
The exact point is hard to reach, so the stone stands a little way off.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Topography**, today called swisstopo, was founded in **1838**. For its **150th birthday** in **1988** it calculated the centre of Switzerland. It used the national borders of the time. Since then the place has been a popular destination for outings.

They determined the **centre of gravity of the country's area**. Imagine you cut Switzerland out of cardboard. At this point you could **balance the cardboard Switzerland on the tip of a needle**. There are other ways of finding a centre, so this point is a matter of definition.

The calculated point lies above a **rock face** and is hard to reach. That is why the **memorial stone** stands about 500 metres away on an alpine pasture. It lies at around **1,650 m above sea level** on the **Älggi Alp** above **Sachseln**. So the centre lies right in the middle of the **Alps**.

The municipality of Sachseln has more than just the centre. **Niklaus von Flüe**, known as **Brother Klaus**, is buried in the parish church. He lived as a hermit in the Ranft in the 15th century and is the **national saint** of Switzerland. Many people make a pilgrimage to his grave.

gewusst: If you counted the lakes differently or chose another method, you would arrive at a slightly different place.
The centre is not in a town or city, but on a remote alpine pasture.

teile.einleitung: The Jet d'eau is a huge fountain in Lake Geneva. Its jet of water shoots around 140 metres into the air. It is the best-known landmark of the city of Geneva.
wichtigste: The Jet d'eau stands in Lake Geneva at the edge of Geneva.
“Jet d'eau” is French and means “jet of water”.
The jet reaches a height of around 140 metres.
The water comes straight from Lake Geneva.
It shoots out of the nozzle at around 200 km/h.
In strong wind and in frost it is switched off.

abschnitte.text: The **Jet d'eau** stands in **Lake Geneva**, right at the edge of the city of **Geneva**. A pier leads close up to it. “Jet d'eau” is French and means **“jet of water”**. The jet reaches around **140 metres**. That is taller than a tower block with 40 storeys. So it can be seen from far away, even from a plane.

abschnitte.titel: Lots of water and lots of speed
abschnitte.text: Powerful **pumps** draw the water straight from Lake Geneva. About **500 litres** are pumped up every second. The water leaves the nozzle at around **200 kilometres per hour**. A fast train travels that fast too. According to the Geneva utilities, around **7 tonnes** of water are in the air at any one time. Afterwards the water falls back into the lake.

The first Jet d'eau came about in **1886** not as decoration at all. A **waterworks** used it to release excess **water pressure**. So the jet was a kind of **valve**. Because people thought it was beautiful, a proper fountain was later made of it. It was moved to a better place in the lake. It has been shooting up this high in its present form since **1951**.

The Jet d'eau does not always run. In **strong wind**, the water would be blown onto roads, boats and people. So it is switched off then. It also stays off in **frost**, so that no ice forms. In the evening it is often lit up, sometimes in special colours on important occasions.

gewusst: If you stand on the pier near the Jet d'eau, you often get quite wet in a light wind.
The Jet d'eau is one of the tallest fountains in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Limmat is the river of Zurich. It flows out of Lake Zurich through the middle of the old town and then through the Limmat Valley to the Aare. Although it is short, it carries a lot of water.
wichtigste: The Limmat flows out of Lake Zurich.
It flows through the middle of Zurich, past the Grossmünster.
The Limmat is about 35 kilometres long.
It is really the continuation of the Linth from the canton of Glarus.
In Zurich the Sihl flows into the Limmat.
The spa town of Baden lies on the Limmat.
At Brugg the Limmat flows into the Aare.

abschnitte.text: The water of the Limmat comes from the canton of **Glarus**. There the river is still called the **Linth**. The Linth flows through Lake Walen and Lake Zurich. Only at the lower end of Lake Zurich, in the city of Zurich, is the river called the **Limmat**. The Linth and the Limmat together form a river system of about 140 kilometres. The Limmat itself is only about 35 kilometres long.

In Zurich the Limmat flows through the **old town**. On the right bank stands the **Grossmünster** with its two towers, on the left the **Fraumünster**. Along the right bank runs the **Limmatquai**, a street with many old houses. At the **Platzspitz** behind the main station, the **Sihl** flows into the Limmat. The Sihl comes from Lake Sihl in the canton of Schwyz.

After Zurich the Limmat flows north west through the **Limmat Valley**. Places such as **Schlieren** and **Dietikon** lie here. The valley is densely populated, and many people work in Zurich. In the past, factories used the power of the river. Even today several **hydroelectric power stations**, which produce electricity, stand on the Limmat.

In the canton of Aargau the Limmat flows through the town of **Baden**. Baden has been known since Roman times for its **warm springs**. There the Limmat has cut deep into the rock. At **Brugg** it flows into the **Aare**. Nearby, the Reuss also flows into the Aare. That is why this area is called the **Wasserschloss** (water castle) of Switzerland.

gewusst: In summer many people swim in the Limmat in Zurich, and there are even river baths there.
Almost all the water from the canton of Glarus flows through Zurich, first as the Linth and later as the Limmat.

teile.einleitung: The Valais is a mountain canton in the south-west of Switzerland. It lies around the valley of the Rhône and has very high mountains, a lot of sun and well-known specialities such as raclette.
wichtigste: The capital of the Valais is Sion.
There are 13 stars on the Valais flag.
In the Rhône Valley the weather is often sunny and dry.
Particularly many apricots grow in the Valais.
Raclette and rye bread are Valais specialities.
The mountain village of Zermatt is car-free.
Leukerbad is known for its hot thermal springs.

abschnitte.text: The Valais lies around the valley of the **Rhône**. On both sides stand very high mountains, many of them over 4,000 metres. The capital is **Sion** (German Sitten). In Upper Valais German is spoken, in Lower Valais French. On the flag, divided into red and white, there are **13 stars**. They stand for the old districts of the land, the so-called Zenden.

The **Rhône Valley** is protected all round by high mountains. That is why the weather there is often **sunny and dry**. So that enough water reached the fields, long water channels called **Suonen** were built in the past. In the warm valley many **apricots**, apples and vines grow. The Valais is the largest winegrowing canton in Switzerland.

**Raclette** comes from the Valais. A wheel of cheese is heated, and the melted layer is scraped onto the plate. It is eaten with potatoes. Another speciality is the dark **Valais rye bread**. It is firm and stays fresh for a long time. In the past, mountain farmers baked it only a few times a year.

In many Valais villages stand old **granaries** (Stadel) made of dark wood. They stand on wooden posts with round **stone slabs**. This stopped mice from climbing in and eating the grain. **Zermatt** at the foot of the Matterhorn is **car-free**: you arrive by train and get around the village in small electric vehicles.

The **Glacier Express** runs from **Zermatt** to **St Moritz** in the Grisons. It is slow so that you can enjoy the landscape, and takes about eight hours. **Leukerbad** is a spa resort with hot **thermal springs**. The water comes warm out of the ground, and you can bathe outdoors, even in winter.

gewusst: The Dufourspitze, the highest mountain in Switzerland, is in the Valais.
The Great Aletsch Glacier in the Valais is the longest glacier in the Alps.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Glarus lies in a deep Alpine valley in Eastern Switzerland. It is known for its Landsgemeinde, the green Schabziger cheese and the Martinsloch near Elm. The capital is also called Glarus.
wichtigste: The Landsgemeinde takes place on the first Sunday in May on the Zaunplatz in Glarus.
Saint Fridolin is shown on the coat of arms.
Schabziger is a green cheese from the Glarus region.
On a few days the sun shines through the Martinsloch onto the church of Elm.
The Klausen Pass links Glarus with Uri.
In 1861 a fire destroyed a large part of the town of Glarus.
The ski racer Vreni Schneider comes from Elm.

abschnitte.text: On the **first Sunday in May**, the voters gather on the **Zaunplatz** in the capital **Glarus**. At the **Landsgemeinde** they vote in the open air by **show of hands**. They can even put forward motions and change laws. Along with Appenzell Innerrhoden, Glarus is one of the few cantons that still has this old form of democracy.

The Glarus **coat of arms** shows **Saint Fridolin**, as a pilgrim with a staff and a Bible. He is the **patron saint** of the canton. A well-known speciality is **Schabziger**. It gets its green colour and strong taste from **blue fenugreek** (Zigerklee). It often has the shape of a small cone and is grated over food.

Near **Elm** there is a special natural spectacle. In the rocks of the **Tschingelhörner** there is a hole, the **Martinsloch**. On a few days in March and in autumn, the **sun** shines exactly through it and falls on the church tower of Elm. The area belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage Site **Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona**. There you can see how older rocks were pushed over younger ones.

In **1861**, a fire broke out in Glarus in a strong **foehn wind** and destroyed a large part of the town. Glarus was then rebuilt with wide, straight streets. Over the **Klausen Pass** you can get from Linthal into the Schächental in the canton of **Uri**; in winter the road is closed. **Vreni Schneider**, who won three Olympic gold medals in skiing, comes from Elm.

gewusst: Since 2011 the canton of Glarus has had only three municipalities: Glarus, Glarus Nord and Glarus Süd.
The sun shines through the Martinsloch onto the church of Elm on only a few days of the year.

teile.einleitung: The Julier Pass is an Alpine pass in the canton of the Grisons. It links the Surses (Oberhalbstein) with the Upper Engadine and has been used since Roman times.
wichtigste: The Julier Pass lies entirely in the canton of the Grisons.
The top of the pass is at 2,284 metres above sea level.
The road leads from Tiefencastel through the Oberhalbstein via Bivio to the pass.
On the Engadine side, the Julier road ends in Silvaplana.
At the top of the pass stand remains of columns from Roman times.
The pass is cleared in winter and is usually open all year round.
Since 2017 there has been a theatre tower at the top of the pass.

abschnitte.text: The Julier Pass links two valley regions in the Grisons. In the north lies the **Oberhalbstein**, a valley region that begins at Tiefencastel. The road climbs through the valley up to **Bivio**, the last village before the top of the pass. After that it goes over the pass and down into the **Upper Engadine**, a long high valley through which the Inn flows. There the road ends in **Silvaplana** on Lake Silvaplana.

Almost 2,000 years ago, the **Romans** already crossed the Julier. For them the pass was an important route over the Alps to the south. At the time, a **sanctuary** stood at the top of the pass, that is, a place where gods were worshipped. Remains of it are the old **columns** that now stand beside the road. Archaeologists have also found coins and other finds from this period on the Julier.

Many Alpine passes are closed in winter because of snow. The Julier Pass, by contrast, is **cleared** and so is usually passable all year round. It is therefore an important link from Chur to the Engadine, for example to St Moritz. In heavy snowfall, cars sometimes need **snow chains**. These are put around the wheels so that cars slip less on snow and ice.

In 2017 a special structure opened at the top of the pass: a **theatre tower**. It is ten-sided, red and was designed by Giovanni Netzer. Netzer runs the Origen cultural festival in the Oberhalbstein. From the start, the tower was intended as a **temporary building**. The first performance took place in August 2017, and many people marvelled at a theatre in the middle of the mountains.

gewusst: On the Julier Pass, at over 2,200 metres, there stood a theatre that could be seen from far away.
Romans already travelled over this pass almost 2,000 years ago.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Neuchâtel lies in the west of Switzerland between Lake Neuchâtel and the Jura. French is spoken there, and the canton is world-famous for its watches. In German it is called Neuenburg.
wichtigste: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland.
Watches have been made in the Neuchâtel Jura for a long time.
La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle have been UNESCO World Heritage since 2009.
The Creux du Van is a huge rock cirque.
Neuchâtel long belonged to the King of Prussia.
On 1 March the canton celebrates the founding of its republic.
The flag has three stripes in green, white and red.

abschnitte.text: The canton of Neuchâtel lies between **Lake Neuchâtel** and the **Jura**. Lake Geneva and Lake Constance are larger, but they also lie in other countries. Lake Neuchâtel is therefore the **largest lake entirely in Switzerland**. In the Jura lies the **Creux du Van**, a huge round cirque of rock walls in which ibexes and chamois live. Near Les Brenets, the Doubs plunges about 27 metres in the **Saut du Doubs**.

In the Neuchâtel Jura, **watches** have been made for a long time. Many well-known watch firms have their workshops there. The towns of **La Chaux-de-Fonds** and **Le Locle** lie high up in the Jura. Their streets were planned so that the **watchmakers** could live and work well. In **2009** the two towns became **UNESCO World Heritage**.

Neuchâtel long belonged to the **King of Prussia**. At the same time, since **1815**, it was a Swiss canton, which was a very special situation. On **1 March 1848**, republicans marched to Neuchâtel and removed the royal government. Since then Neuchâtel has been a **republic**, and 1 March is a public holiday in the canton. The **flag** has three stripes in **green, white and red**, with a white cross in the red part at the top.

At **La Tène** on the north-eastern end of Lake Neuchâtel, very many **Celtic** weapons and tools were found. A whole period was named after this site: the **La Tène culture**, the later Iron Age. Archaeologists all over Europe use this name. In Hauterive on the lake, the **Laténium** museum shows many finds from the early history of the region.

gewusst: A whole era of the Celts in Europe is named after a site in the canton of Neuchâtel.
For a time, Neuchâtel was both a Swiss canton and a principality of the Prussian king.

teile.einleitung: Delémont, in German **Delsberg**, is the main town of the canton of Jura. The town lies in the Jura on the Sorne and is the largest municipality of the youngest Swiss canton.
wichtigste: The official name is Delémont, Delsberg is the German name.
Delémont is the main town and largest municipality of the canton of Jura.
The town lies on the Sorne shortly before it flows into the Birs.
At the end of 2023 around 12,700 people lived in Delémont.
Every year in September the Fête du peuple jurassien takes place.

abschnitte.titel: Position on the Sorne and the Birs
abschnitte.text: Delémont lies in a wide valley in the **Jura**. The town lies on both sides of the **Sorne**, shortly before it flows into the **Birs**. The Birs flows on towards Basel and enters the Rhine there. In the canton of Jura people speak **French**, so the town is officially called **Delémont**.

abschnitte.titel: Main town of the canton of Jura
abschnitte.text: Delémont is the **main town** of the canton of Jura. The government and parliament of the canton have their seat here. At the end of **2023**, **12,739** people lived in Delémont. That is few compared with other cantonal capitals, yet Delémont is the **largest municipality** of the canton. The old town with its castle and fountains is well preserved.

Every year in **September** the **Fête du peuple jurassien** takes place in Delémont, the festival of the Jura people. It has been held since **1947**. The festival recalls the long political struggle for a **canton of Jura** of its own. The canton came into being after popular votes and since 1979 has been the youngest canton of Switzerland.

gewusst: The canton of Jura with its main town Delémont has been the youngest canton of Switzerland since 1979.
The Fête du peuple jurassien has been celebrated since 1947, long before the canton existed.

teile.einleitung: The Helvetic Zone is a large rock zone of the Alps. Its rocks were once laid down in the sea on the southern edge of Europe and were pushed north when the mountains formed. Many well-known mountains of the northern Alps belong to it.
wichtigste: The rocks of the Helvetic Zone formed on the shallow shelf at the southern edge of Europe.
The name comes from Helvetia, the Latin name of Switzerland.
The Helvetic nappes consist mainly of limestone and marl.
During the formation of the mountains, the layers were sheared off and pushed north.
The Säntis shows especially fine folds in the Helvetic Zone.
The Schrattenkalk forms many pale rock faces.

abschnitte.text: Many millions of years ago there was a sea south of present-day Europe. At the edge of the continent there was a shallow sea floor, the **shelf**. Mud, lime and the shells of small sea creatures were deposited there. In time these became **sedimentary rocks**. They date from the **Jurassic**, the **Cretaceous** and the early Tertiary. Towards the south the layers become thicker and richer in limestone.

The **Helvetic Zone** was first described in detail in Switzerland. That is why it is named after **Helvetia**, the Latin name of Switzerland. Many typical sites are found here. The Helvetic Zone forms a large part of the **northern Alps**, for example in the Bernese Oberland, Central Switzerland, the Glarus region and Eastern Switzerland.

The Helvetic **nappes** consist mainly of **limestone** and **marl**. Marl is a rock made of lime and clay that is rather soft. A well-known limestone is the **Schrattenkalk** from the Lower Cretaceous. It is pale and massive and forms striking rock faces, for example at the **Schrattenfluh**. Because rainwater slowly dissolves it, **karren fields** with grooves in the rock are formed.

The Alps formed as Africa and Europe moved towards each other. In the process, the Helvetic sediments came loose from their **crystalline basement** along soft layers. They were **sheared off** and pushed north as large slabs of rock. Such slabs are called **nappes**. The Helvetic Zone forms the northernmost part of this stack of nappes. The extreme southern edge of the shelf is called the **Ultrahelvetic Zone**.

On the **Säntis** in Eastern Switzerland you can see the **folds** of the limestone layers especially well. The **Churfirsten** on Lake Walen consist of Cretaceous limestones tilted to the north. Their rock edges drop steeply to the lake. In the **Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona** in the Glarus region, older rocks lie over younger ones. This **Glarus Thrust** has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage since 2008.

gewusst: In some limestone rocks of the Helvetic Zone you can find fossilised shells and other sea creatures, high up in the mountains.
Through the Martinsloch, a hole in the rock in the Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona, the sun shines twice a year onto the church of Elm.

teile.einleitung: Locarno is a town in the canton of Ticino on the north shore of Lake Maggiore. It is known for its mild, sunny climate and for the film festival, where thousands of people watch films in the open air on the Piazza Grande.
wichtigste: Locarno lies on the north shore of Lake Maggiore.
The town is among the sunniest places in Switzerland.
The film festival has existed since 1946 and usually takes place in August.
The main prize is called the “Pardo d'oro”, the Golden Leopard.
Above the town stands the pilgrimage church of Madonna del Sasso.
Between Locarno and Ascona, the Maggia flows into the lake.
In 1925, treaties to secure peace were concluded in Locarno.

abschnitte.text: Locarno lies on **Lake Maggiore**, the “great lake”. Most of the lake belongs to Italy, and only the north to Switzerland. Locarno is sheltered by mountains and has a **mild climate** with many sunny days. That is why palms, camellias and other plants from warmer countries grow here. Right next to Locarno lies **Ascona**, and between them the **Maggia** flows from the Maggia Valley into the lake.

The **Locarno Film Festival** was held for the first time in **1946**. It is one of the oldest film festivals in the world. Every year in summer, mostly in **August**, film people and guests come from many countries. On the **Piazza Grande** a huge screen is then put up. Thousands of people watch films together there in the evening under the starry sky. The festival's emblem is a **leopard**, and the main prize is called the **“Pardo d'oro”**.

High above the town stands the pilgrimage church of **Madonna del Sasso**. It sits on a rock, and “sasso” means stone. You can reach it on foot or by **funicular railway**. From there you have a wide view over the town and the lake. From **Orselina** an aerial cableway also goes up to **Cardada**, a viewing mountain above Locarno.

In 1925 politicians from several European countries met in Locarno for a **conference**. Germany, France and other states agreed on their **borders in the west**. The **Locarno Treaties** were meant to secure **peace** in Europe after the First World War. This made Locarno known across the whole world.

gewusst: During the film festival the Piazza Grande becomes one of the largest open air cinemas in Europe.
Locarno lies very low, and Lake Maggiore is the lowest point in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Fribourg lies in the west of Switzerland between Bern and Lake Geneva. It is bilingual and known for cheese, chocolate and the little town of Gruyères. In German it is called Freiburg.
wichtigste: In the canton of Fribourg, French and German are spoken.
The River Sarine often separates the French-speaking and German-speaking areas.
Gruyère cheese comes from the canton of Fribourg.
The Fribourg flag is black at the top and white at the bottom.
Cailler has been making chocolate in Broc since 1898.
Fribourg joined the Confederation in 1481 together with Solothurn.

abschnitte.text: The canton of Fribourg is **bilingual**. Most people speak **French**, and many others **German**. The city is called **Freiburg** in German, and many street signs are in both languages. Often the river **Sarine**, in German **Saane**, separates the two languages: to the west people mostly speak French, to the east mostly German. The **University of Fribourg** also teaches in both languages.

Fribourg was admitted to the Confederation in **1481** together with **Solothurn**. This was made possible by the **Covenant of Stans**, an agreement among the member states. The canton's flag is very simple: **black** at the top, **white** at the bottom. The little town of **Murten** on Lake Murten, with its old town wall, also belongs to the canton. Most people there speak German.

**Gruyère** is a hard cheese made from cow's milk that matures for many months in the cheese cellar. It takes its name from the little town of **Gruyères**, with a castle on a hill. Typical of Fribourg is the **moitié-moitié** fondue. That means “half and half”, because Gruyère and **Vacherin Fribourgeois** are mixed.

In **Broc** in the Gruyère region there is a chocolate factory of the **Cailler** brand. Chocolate has been made there since **1898**. The milk for it comes from cows in the surrounding area. Visitors can look round the factory and taste chocolate. So cheese and chocolate in the canton of Fribourg are both linked to **dairy farming**.

gewusst: The border between German and French is often called the “Röstigraben” in Switzerland, and it runs right through the canton of Fribourg.
Moitié-moitié simply means “half and half” in French.
